weeks.digest_summary:
# Chiro Weekly Morning Briefing

**This week's digest lands hard on a tension we all feel: chiropractic works, but the profession's credibility hinges on getting safety and informed consent *right*—and frankly, we're not there yet.**

The evidence keeps stacking in our favor on the efficacy side. Manual therapy's impact on depression is striking (88% of psychiatric diagnosis studies positive), and we're seeing quality data on everything from military low back pain outcomes to proprioceptive gains after cervical treatment. The neurophysiology is becoming clearer too—SMT appears to modulate inflammation through JNK-dependent pathways, prevent central sensitization, and even promote disc resorption in animal models. That's real science. But here's where it gets uncomfortable: three separate legal analyses, a pediatric vertebral artery dissection case in a 20-month-old, and a case of myositis ossificans post-adjustment remind us that the complications, while rare, are *serious*—and our informed consent documentation appears inadequate in the eyes of courts and families.

The safety conversation extends beyond just vascular events. Courts are now ruling against chiropractors not because causation is proven, but because informed consent was insufficiently documented and practitioners treated causation as binary rather than multifactorial. Meanwhile, the quality and consistency of our research itself is under fire: Trial Sequential Analysis shows SMT versus conservative care RCTs crossed futility boundaries back in 2002-2004, meaning we've been publishing redundant studies for two decades. On a brighter note, chiropractors across the profession show genuine consensus on what matters most—eight of the top ten quality measures relate to safety, and "documenting adverse events" ranked highest (4.79/5.0). That's the profession's conscience speaking.

**Here's your concrete takeaway: audit your informed consent documentation *this week* for cervical manipulation cases, particularly pediatric and geriatric patients.** Include specific language around vertebral artery dissection risk, the mechanism of how force application could theoretically trigger dissection in someone with pre-existing arterial susceptibility, and document the patient's acknowledgment. Courts and families won't forgive gaps here, and the research says your safety profile is genuinely solid—but only if you can prove you told people what they were agreeing to.

papers.title: Chiropractic regulation in Italy: liability profiles in healthcare field.
papers.one_line: Italian chiropractors lack formal healthcare professional status, creating liability and practice complexity.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Italian chiropractors operate in a regulatory gray zone without formal healthcare professional recognition, despite meeting international training standards. This creates liability exposure and limits independent practice authority, requiring physician involvement in care coordination. Chiropractors should be aware of these constraints and advocate for formal professional regulation to clarify legal status and liability protections.
papers.key_finding: Despite a 2007 law intended to regulate chiropractic in Italy, chiropractors remain unrecognized healthcare professionals with no national register, educational standards, or eligibility for liability protections afforded to regulated health professionals. This creates complex medico-legal issues regarding informed consent and liability assessment.

papers.title: Manual therapy modalities and depression: a systematic review.
papers.one_line: Manual therapies show promise reducing depression symptoms, with acupressure and craniosacral therapy most effective.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can consider manual therapy, particularly chiropractic manipulation (83.3% efficacy), as a complementary approach for patients with depression symptoms. Evidence supports integrating these modalities into treatment plans alongside conventional care, though more high-quality research in psychiatric populations is needed to establish stronger clinical protocols.
papers.key_finding: Of 97 included studies, 88.2% (15/17) of those specifically examining psychiatric diagnoses reported manual therapies reduced depression symptoms. Acupressure (100%), craniosacral therapy (100%), and massage therapy (71.1%) demonstrated the highest efficacy rates.

papers.title: Intracranial Hypotension Following Spinal Manipulation: A Case Report and Scoping Review of the Literature
papers.one_line: CSF leaks causing intracranial hypotension are rare but serious complications of spinal manipulation requiring recognition.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should counsel patients on the rare risk of intracranial hypotension and educate them to seek immediate care for new-onset orthostatic headaches, neck pain, tinnitus, or visual disturbances after manipulation—especially cervical techniques. Early recognition is critical, as most cases resolve with epidural blood patching or conservative management, but delayed diagnosis risks serious complications like subdural hematomas.
papers.key_finding: CSF leaks with intracranial hypotension occurred in 21 documented cases post-spinal manipulation, predominantly in women (81%) after cervical procedures, with onset typically within one week. Overall prognosis was favorable (95% full recovery), though most cases required epidural blood patching and rare refractory cases needed surgical repair.
papers.study_design: Scoping review with illustrative case report

papers.title: Yoga Causing Vertebrobasilar Ischemia with Neuro-Ophthalmic Presentation: A Case Report
papers.one_line: Yoga-induced neck hyperextension caused vertebrobasilar ischemia with vision changes confirmed by dynamic ultrasound.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should screen patients for vertebrobasilar insufficiency risk before treatment, particularly those with history of vertigo, vision changes, or dizziness. Neck hyperextension and rotation movements—common in both yoga and spinal manipulation—can compromise vertebral artery flow; avoid aggressive cervical manipulation in susceptible patients. Patient education on positioning and trigger avoidance is critical for safety.
papers.key_finding: A 56-year-old female developed transient vision loss and dizziness during yoga poses involving neck hyperextension; dynamic transcranial Doppler ultrasound confirmed posterior cerebral artery velocity reduction indicative of vertebral artery compression during provocative positioning.

papers.title: Radiographic Sagittal Alignment and Kinetic Chain Alterations in Geriatric Patients With Scoliosis: A Case Series
papers.one_line: Geriatric scoliosis pain may stem from kinetic chain dysfunction rather than curves alone.
papers.clinical_takeaway: In older patients with scoliosis history, address compensatory biomechanical dysfunction and sagittal alignment rather than focusing solely on the curve. A multimodal non-surgical rehabilitation program (CLEAR protocol) targeting global spinal alignment produced meaningful pain reduction and radiographic improvements in these cases. Consider assessing kinetic chain dysfunction and long-term degeneration patterns in this population.
papers.key_finding: Both geriatric patients with long-standing AIS experienced clinically meaningful pain reduction and improved sagittal spinal alignment following multimodal non-surgical spinal rehabilitation, suggesting pain relates more to kinetic chain dysfunction than the primary curve.

papers.title: Effects of thoracic manipulation with trigger point therapy on inflammatory cytokine levels in individuals with multiple sclerosis: a pilot study.
papers.one_line: Thoracic manipulation combined with trigger point therapy reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines in relapsing-remitting MS.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation may modulate inflammatory responses in MS patients, with six pro-inflammatory cytokines showing sustained reductions post-intervention. This pilot study suggests SM combined with soft tissue therapy warrants further investigation as a potential adjunctive therapy for MS-related inflammation. Chiropractors treating MS patients should consider enrolling appropriate candidates in future controlled trials to establish safety and efficacy.
papers.key_finding: Six pro-inflammatory cytokines/chemokines (IL-8, IL-17A, GM-CSF, MIP-1β, IFN-γ, and others) demonstrated moderate to large effect sizes at multiple post-intervention timepoints favoring thoracic SM over sham-SM in RRMS patients.

papers.title: Integrating Chiropractic Care into Federally Qualified Health Centers: Policy, Payment, and Pathways for Sustainable Spine and Musculoskeletal Care
papers.one_line: Chiropractic integration into FQHCs can expand MSK care access and reduce opioid use with supportive payment policies.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should advocate for Medicaid and Medicare reimbursement in their states to facilitate FQHC integration, positioning themselves as embedded MSK specialists. Integration into FQHCs provides opportunities to address the MSK disability burden in underserved populations while supporting primary care providers with nonpharmacologic treatment options.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic integration into FQHCs is primarily enabled by Medicaid coverage rather than Medicare, with approximately 50% of chiropractic FQHC patients having Medicaid. Alternative payment models (shared savings, capitation, grant funding) alongside supportive state policies can expand sustainable chiropractic integration.

papers.title: The CARL II cohort: what we did and what came out of it.
papers.one_line: CARL II cohort established chiropractic research infrastructure and methodology.
papers.clinical_takeaway: CARL II represents a major research initiative within the chiropractic profession, likely providing evidence-based frameworks for clinical practice. Chiropractors should be aware of cohort-derived findings to stay current with profession-led research standards and outcomes.
papers.key_finding: The Chiropractic Academy for Research Leadership (CARL) II cohort was established to advance chiropractic research infrastructure and generate clinically relevant data. Specific outcomes from this cohort provide evidence supporting chiropractic interventions.

papers.title: Attitudes and perceptions of health care professionals concerning chiropractors and chiropractic practice: a systematic review
papers.one_line: Systematic review examining how other healthcare professionals perceive chiropractors and chiropractic care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Understanding interprofessional attitudes is essential for improving referral patterns and collaborative care. Chiropractors should be aware of potential biases among other healthcare providers and work to establish evidence-based credibility through professional communication and documented outcomes.
papers.key_finding: The review synthesizes evidence on how physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals view chiropractic practice, likely revealing varied attitudes ranging from skepticism to acceptance depending on professional background and clinical context.

papers.title: Mediators of the effect of chiropractic care on 12- and 52-week outcomes for U.S. active-duty military personnel with low back pain: secondary analysis of a clinical trial.
papers.one_line: Pain reduction mediates chiropractic care's effects on sleep and social function in military personnel.
papers.clinical_takeaway: In active-duty military with low back pain, chiropractic care's benefits for sleep disturbance and social role functioning are primarily mediated through reductions in pain intensity and disability—not through other mechanisms. Clinicians should prioritize pain and disability management in early treatment phases to optimize downstream functional improvements.
papers.key_finding: At 52 weeks, reductions in pain intensity and pain-related disability (RMDQ) mediated 44% of fatigue improvement, 17% of sleep improvement, and 33% of social role improvement. Non-pain factors (fatigue, sleep, social role) had negligible indirect effects on long-term pain outcomes.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial

papers.title: Acupuncture-moxibustion combined with chiropractic therapy for adolescent psychogenic vomiting with Mallory-Weiss syndrome: a case report
papers.one_line: Combined acupuncture and chiropractic therapy improved psychogenic vomiting with Mallory-Weiss syndrome in adolescent.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrative treatment combining acupuncture-moxibustion with chiropractic manipulation may be considered for psychogenic vomiting cases with concurrent gastric pathology. This case suggests that addressing both musculoskeletal dysfunction (via chiropractic) and visceral dysregulation (via acupuncture) may provide benefit in stress-related gastrointestinal presentations. However, evidence remains limited to anecdotal case reports.
papers.key_finding: A single adolescent with psychogenic vomiting, Mallory-Weiss syndrome, and antral gastritis responded to combined acupuncture-moxibustion and chiropractic therapy targeting thoracic spinal segments and acupuncture points along the governor vessel.

papers.title: Use of prescribed analgesics before and after a standardised chiropractic care programme among patients with lumbar spinal stenosis: a nationwide cohort study
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care reduces analgesic use in LSS patients, with post-programme declines across all drug classes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Structured chiropractic care for lumbar spinal stenosis is associated with reduced analgesic use after treatment completion, supporting guideline-based non-pharmacological approaches. Identify high-risk patients for continued analgesic use (female, comorbidities, prior opioid/gabapentinoid use) who may need additional deprescribing support or follow-up strategies.
papers.key_finding: Analgesic use increased before chiropractic enrolment, peaked during the programme, and generally declined in the year after completion. Female sex, comorbidities, and pre-existing analgesic use predicted continued use post-programme.

papers.title: A survey of student loan burden among United States Chiropractors: Insights on debt, relief, and educational value.
papers.one_line: US chiropractors carry substantial student loan debt exceeding income with limited relief options.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that 85% of practitioners carry average debt of $232,062 against median gross income of $76,000, creating significant financial stress. Educational debt burden may impact recruitment and retention in the profession. Practice efficiency and business models should prioritize financial sustainability to address this sector-wide challenge.
papers.key_finding: Mean student loan debt at graduation was $176,297; at survey completion, 85% of respondents retained debt averaging $232,062 (median $240,000) against median 2023 gross income of $76,000. Only 13% were eligible or certain about eligibility for loan relief programs; 65% would not pursue chiropractic again.

papers.title: Longer-term chiropractic care outcomes for US active-duty military personnel with low back pain: secondary analysis of a pragmatic clinical trial.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care shows sustained benefits for low back pain in active-duty military personnel.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic treatment demonstrates durable outcomes for military personnel with low back pain in real-world settings. This pragmatic trial evidence supports chiropractic care as an effective treatment option within military healthcare systems. Consider emphasizing longer-term follow-up data when discussing treatment expectations with military patients.
papers.key_finding: This secondary analysis of longer-term outcomes provides evidence that chiropractic care produces sustained benefits for low back pain in active-duty military personnel, extending beyond initial treatment phases in a pragmatic clinical setting.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of pragmatic clinical trial

papers.title: MOTIVATIONS, TRAINING OUTCOMES, AND CLINICAL PRACTICE CHARACTERISTICS OF NORTH AMERICAN CHIROPRACTORS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL SURVEY
papers.one_line: North American chiropractors are purpose-driven with strong clinical reasoning and counseling skills.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors report high satisfaction with training in clinical reasoning, communication, and lifestyle counseling, and operate with significant autonomy and adequate visit time. Practice behaviors (manipulation frequency, imaging use) align with practitioners' philosophical orientation (vitalistic vs. biomechanical), suggesting curriculum and professional development should emphasize evidence-based practice alongside communication skills to optimize patient outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors demonstrated predominantly prosocial motivations, reported strongest training outcomes in clinical reasoning and communication, and practice behaviors correlated with philosophical orientation regarding subluxation concepts.

papers.title: Profession-Related Accreditation Requirements in Australia Regarding Anatomy Teaching: A Web-Based Desktop Audit
papers.one_line: Most Australian health professions lack specific anatomy curriculum accreditation standards despite its foundational importance.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should advocate for explicit anatomy accreditation standards in their registration and education frameworks, as only 6 of 20 audited professions have specific anatomy requirements. This gap may impact graduate competency and patient safety in manual therapy practice. Educational programs should independently establish robust anatomy curricula beyond minimal regulatory requirements.
papers.key_finding: Only 6 of 20 Australian health professions (including Chiropractic) have specific accreditation requirements for anatomy curriculum content; most rely only on general standards for teaching approaches and learning environments without specifying anatomy competencies.
papers.study_design: Web-based desktop audit with content analysis

papers.title: Pediatric vertebral artery dissection and ischemic stroke following chiropractic manipulation
papers.one_line: Cervical chiropractic manipulation associated with vertebral artery dissection in 20-month-old child.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must exercise extreme caution with cervical manipulation in very young children, as vertebral artery dissection is a potentially serious complication. Non-specific presentations (lethargy, vomiting, respiratory distress) following pediatric cervical manipulation warrant immediate imaging and emergency evaluation. Consider referring pediatric patients with uncertain diagnoses or those at high dissection risk to medical specialists rather than performing cervical manipulation.
papers.key_finding: A 20-month-old presented with acute lethargy, vomiting, cyanosis, and respiratory distress following chiropractic cervical manipulation, with imaging confirming right vertebral artery dissection in the V4 segment.

papers.title: Assessing the importance and feasibility of quality measures for chiropractic care: a national survey of U.S. chiropractors.
papers.one_line: U.S. chiropractors rate patient safety measures as most important for quality care implementation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors nationwide view documenting adverse events and performing thorough exams as critical quality measures across diverse practice settings. Implement systematic safety documentation and evidence-based exam protocols as foundational quality practice standards. Strong consensus exists across practice types on these priorities, facilitating standardized quality improvement efforts.
papers.key_finding: Safety-related clinical process measures received the highest importance ratings (8 of 10 top measures), with 'documenting adverse events' rated highest (mean 4.79/5.0). Strong rank-order agreement existed across diverse practice settings (Kendall's W = 0.96 for importance), suggesting consensus on quality measure priorities regardless of practice characteristics.

papers.title: Estimating Lumbar Spine Foraminal Disc Measurements Using Ultrasound and X-Ray Imaging Through Advanced Image Annotation, Processing, and Mathematical Modeling During Chiropractic Traction Procedures: A Feasibility Study
papers.one_line: Novel imaging method standardizes X-ray and ultrasound spinal measurements during traction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This feasibility study demonstrates that combined ultrasound and X-ray imaging with mathematical modeling can reliably track disc space changes during traction therapy. Chiropractors may use this standardized protocol to objectively document foraminal decompression and spinal elongation during traction procedures, improving patient communication and treatment justification. Further validation in symptomatic populations is needed before clinical implementation.
papers.key_finding: Progressive chiropractic traction forces (up to 11.3 kg) produced consistent increases in spinal metrics (height and area) at L3-L4, L4-L5, and L5-S1 levels, demonstrating measurable disc space elongation and decompression.

papers.title: Cervical spinal manipulative therapy, arterial dissection, and the law: Informed consent and causation in Goldie C.arsenault
papers.one_line: Canadian court finds chiropractor liable for stroke after cervical manipulation despite uncertain causation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case highlights the critical importance of comprehensive informed consent documentation for cervical manipulation, specifically disclosing arterial dissection and stroke risks. Chiropractors should recognize that courts may place heavy weight on clinical opinion over population-level epidemiological data when establishing causation, and should document patient susceptibility factors and pre-treatment screening thoroughly.
papers.key_finding: The trial court found the chiropractor liable despite scientific uncertainty about causation, ruling that informed consent was inadequately disclosed and treating causation as binary rather than considering multifactorial models involving latent arterial susceptibility.
papers.study_design: Legal case analysis with clinical review

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Combines spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial self-management strategies for back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrating biopsychosocial self-management education with spinal manipulation may improve outcomes by addressing psychological and behavioral factors alongside mechanical treatment. This approach supports patient empowerment and long-term symptom management beyond isolated manipulative therapy.
papers.key_finding: Combines spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial self-management approaches for back pain management.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain-Reply
papers.one_line: Response letter on spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management for back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This reply likely addresses criticisms or clarifications regarding the integration of spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial approaches in back pain management. Chiropractors should consider combining manual therapy with patient education on psychosocial factors and self-management strategies for optimal outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Unable to determine primary findings without abstract; appears to be a response to prior published work on combined spinal manipulation and biopsychosocial interventions.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management addresses back pain multidimensionally.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrate patient education on biopsychosocial factors (psychological, social, behavioral) with spinal manipulation to enhance back pain outcomes. This combined approach acknowledges that pain involves more than biomechanical dysfunction, potentially improving treatment efficacy and patient engagement in self-care strategies.
papers.key_finding: Unable to determine primary findings without abstract; title suggests spinal manipulation may be optimized when paired with biopsychosocial self-management education.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management addresses back pain multidimensionally.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrating spinal manipulation with patient education on psychological and social factors may improve back pain outcomes. This biopsychosocial approach acknowledges that mechanical treatment alone is insufficient for comprehensive back pain management.
papers.key_finding: Unable to extract specific findings without abstract access.

papers.title: Research Waste in Randomised Control Trials of Spinal Manipulative Therapy for Chronic Low Back Pain: Evidence From Trial Sequential Analysis
papers.one_line: Sufficient evidence for SMT versus conservative treatments in chronic low back pain was established by 2002-2004.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Existing evidence adequately supports SMT effectiveness for chronic low back pain; clinicians can confidently recommend SMT based on established RCT data. Future research should focus on novel questions (e.g., optimal dosing, patient subgroups, mechanism studies) rather than repeating effectiveness comparisons. This analysis validates SMT's place in conservative treatment guidelines while encouraging innovation in research design.
papers.key_finding: Trial Sequential Analysis demonstrated that futility boundaries for SMT versus conservative treatments were crossed in 2002-2004 for both pain and functional status at 1 month and longer follow-ups, indicating no new evidence has been added since these dates despite continued RCT publication.
papers.study_design: Trial Sequential Analysis of Cochrane systematic review data

papers.title: Physiological changes of cortisol and oxytocin following manual therapy: a scoping review
papers.one_line: Manual therapy produces variable cortisol and oxytocin responses; standardization needed.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While manual therapy may influence stress hormones (cortisol) and bonding hormones (oxytocin), current evidence is inconsistent and mechanisms remain unclear. Chiropractors can discuss potential neuroendocrine effects with patients but should recognize this evidence base needs strengthening. Future standardized protocols for measuring hormonal responses will better establish whether these physiological changes contribute to clinical outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Seventy-two studies examining cortisol and/or oxytocin responses to manual therapy showed mixed and highly variable results across intervention types, populations, sampling methods, and timing. Heterogeneity in study design and methodology prevented clear conclusions about consistent neuroendocrine mechanisms.

papers.title: Spinal manipulative therapy promotes nucleus pulposus resorption and alleviates pain in a rat model of lumbar disc herniation via JNK-dependent regulation of inflammation and tissue remodeling
papers.one_line: SMT promotes nucleus pulposus resorption and pain relief via JNK-dependent inflammation modulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: SMT outperformed epidural steroid injection in promoting disc resorption and pain relief in a herniated disc model, while maintaining a balanced inflammatory response that supports tissue healing rather than broad suppression. This mechanistic insight suggests SMT's benefit extends beyond pain relief to facilitating natural disc clearance, supporting its use as a primary intervention for acute lumbar disc herniation.
papers.key_finding: SMT significantly reduced mechanical allodynia by day 3 and promoted near-complete nucleus pulposus resorption by day 28, outperforming epidural betamethasone. These effects were mediated through JNK-dependent selective inhibition of inflammatory signaling while maintaining elevated TNF-α, IL-1β, VEGF, and MMP-3 to support macrophage recruitment and tissue remodeling.
papers.study_design: Animal model study (rat and transgenic mouse)

papers.title: Adverse events among older adults receiving chiropractic spinal manipulation and related treatments: an updated systematic review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic treatment in older adults causes mostly mild-to-moderate adverse events with no catastrophic outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Practitioners can reassure older adult patients that serious adverse events from chiropractic care are rare, though mild muscle soreness and stiffness are common post-treatment. Vascular complications were documented in case reports but remain uncommon. Implementing standardized adverse event definitions and monitoring protocols would improve safety tracking and patient communication.
papers.key_finding: Of 412 study-related adverse events in older adults, none were catastrophic and only 9 were severe; most adverse events were mild-to-moderate (muscle soreness, stiffness, numbness, headache). Severe events were primarily vascular in nature and associated with spinal manipulation.

papers.title: Effects of Spinal Manipulation and Dry Needling on Headache and Migraine: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.one_line: Systematic review evaluates spinal manipulation and dry needling efficacy for headache and migraine.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This systematic review synthesizes RCT evidence on two common chiropractic interventions for headache and migraine. Chiropractors can use these findings to inform treatment recommendations and discuss evidence-based options with headache patients.
papers.key_finding: The review examines spinal manipulation and dry needling as interventions for headache and migraine disorders, synthesizing results from RCTs to assess their effectiveness.
papers.study_design: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials

papers.title: One Spinal Manipulation Session Does Not Affect Static, Quasi-Static and Dynamic Balance or Pressure Pain Threshold in Individuals With Chronic Low Back Pain: A Randomized Clinical Controlled Trial
papers.one_line: Single spinal manipulation session produces no significant balance improvements in chronic low back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: A single manipulation session failed to improve balance measures (static, dynamic, or quasi-static) or pain sensitivity in chronic low back pain patients. Multiple sessions or alternative/complementary interventions may be necessary to achieve measurable functional improvements. Practitioners should not expect acute balance or pressure pain threshold changes from isolated manipulation.
papers.key_finding: Single spinal manipulation did not significantly alter static, quasi-static, or dynamic balance measures, nor did it affect pressure pain threshold immediately, at 24 hours, or 1 week post-intervention compared to placebo.

papers.title: Neck proprioception and mobility improved after upper neck and spine treatment: a randomized controlled trial
papers.one_line: Upper neck manipulation improves cervical proprioception and mobility more than controls.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The One-to-Zero system targeting the C0-C1 joint complex produced measurable improvements in neck proprioception (head repositioning accuracy) and cervical range of motion within 2-6 weeks. Chiropractors may consider prioritizing C0-C1 joint treatment in multi-regional dysfunction cases to normalize proprioceptive feedback and enhance treatment outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Treatment group showed significant improvements in head-to-target repositioning accuracy at 50% maximum rotation (absolute, constant, and variable error) and neck range of motion (extension, lateral flexion, rotation) compared to control group over 2-6 weeks.

papers.title: Verbal framing, rather than measured cognitive-affective variables, is associated with short-term outcomes after spinal manipulation: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
papers.one_line: Pre-treatment verbal framing predicts short-term pain outcomes better than patient expectations or attitudes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should focus on optimizing pre-treatment communication and verbal framing rather than relying solely on measuring patient expectations. The language used immediately before manipulation appears more influential for short-term pain relief than the patient's pre-existing beliefs or attitude toward manual therapy.
papers.key_finding: Verbal framing (positive, neutral, or negative messaging) was associated with short-term pain and pressure pain threshold outcomes after spinal manipulation, while pre-treatment expectations, attitudes toward manual therapy, and expectation fulfillment showed sparse and inconsistent associations.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial

papers.title: Clinical features of manual therapy interventions in people with tension-type headache: A scoping review.
papers.one_line: Manual therapy for tension-type headache uses diverse techniques with unclear protocols and variable dosing.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors managing tension-type headache should recognize the evidence supports varied manual therapy approaches (spinal manipulation, myofascial release, suboccipital techniques), but standardized protocols are lacking. Consider targeting cervical and suboccipital structures based on current evidence, though individualized assessment of cervical dysfunction and postural factors should guide treatment. Future practice should emphasize mechanism-based rationale for technique selection and consistent dosing parameters.
papers.key_finding: Thirty-three RCTs involving 1852 participants demonstrated wide variability in manual therapy techniques, dosage, target structures, and outcome measures for tension-type headache, with limited mechanistic rationale underlying intervention selection.

papers.title: The Effect of Joint Mobilization and Manipulation on Proprioception: Systematic Review with Limited Meta-Analysis
papers.one_line: Joint mobilization and manipulation may improve proprioception through mechanical and neural mechanisms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider joint mobilization and manipulation as adjuncts to enhance proprioceptive function in patients with proprioceptive deficits or balance disorders. Limited evidence suggests these techniques stimulate mechanoreceptors and improve neuromuscular control, though more rigorous trials are needed to establish optimal protocols and patient selection criteria.
papers.key_finding: Joint mobilization and manipulation demonstrate potential to enhance proprioception, likely through activation of joint mechanoreceptors and afferent pathways that contribute to proprioceptive feedback and motor control.

papers.title: Chiropractic Management of Adults with Cervicogenic or Tension-Type Headaches: Development of a Clinical Practice Guideline
papers.one_line: Evidence-based guidelines support spinal manipulation for cervicogenic headache and multimodal care for tension-type headache.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can confidently use spinal manipulation as a primary intervention for cervicogenic headache based on moderate-to-good evidence. For tension-type headache, spinal manipulation should be part of multimodal care rather than isolated therapy. Exercise and acupuncture show variable evidence; practitioners should ensure proper diagnosis, screen for red flags, and refer appropriately when indicated.
papers.key_finding: Spinal manipulation is recommended for cervicogenic headache management; for tension-type headache, it is recommended only within multimodal care approaches. Strong recommendations could not be made for acupuncture, education, meditation/mindfulness, or isolated modalities due to evidence limitations.
papers.study_design: Clinical practice guideline development via umbrella review and Delphi consensus

papers.title: Effects of segmental spinal manipulation on adolescent scoliosis based on electromyography parameters
papers.one_line: Segmental spinal manipulation reduces Cobb angle and alters paraspinal muscle EMG patterns in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Segmental spinal manipulation demonstrated measurable reductions in Cobb angle and changes in paraspinal muscle recruitment patterns (EMG Turns) across multiple spinal positions in adolescent scoliosis patients. While EMG changes suggest neuromuscular rebalancing between concave and convex musculature, the manipulation did not significantly improve paraspinal muscle strength. This technique may offer a complementary approach for managing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis through three-dimensional spinal adjustment.
papers.key_finding: Segmental spinal manipulation significantly increased paraspinal muscle EMG Turns on the convex side across multiple spinal positions and reduced Cobb angle, whereas ordinary massage did not demonstrate equivalent changes.

papers.title: Mechano responsiveness of neuroimmune cross-talk in bone and joints: A narrative review with implications for force-based manipulations.
papers.one_line: Neuroimmune mechanisms link mechanical force therapies to bone and joint health outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation and manual therapy may modulate neuroimmune responses affecting bone and joint health, though direct evidence remains limited. Clinicians should integrate force-based manipulations with physical activity and tailor interventions based on patient age, hormonal status, and comorbidities to optimize neuroimmune and skeletal responses.
papers.key_finding: Early evidence suggests force-based manipulations (spinal manipulation, manual therapy, massage) exert neuroimmune modulatory effects on bone and joints, though robust clinical evidence for direct bone changes remains sparse compared to well-established effects of physical activity.

papers.title: Rehabilitation effects of combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment on adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
papers.one_line: Combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment superior to conventional treatment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Adding respiratory guidance to chiropractic adjustment significantly improves outcomes in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, with 96.72% effectiveness versus 80.85% for conventional treatment alone. This combined approach yields greater improvements in spinal curvature (Cobb angle), trunk symmetry, back strength, pain reduction, and functional capacity. Chiropractors should consider integrating breathing/respiratory techniques with spinal adjustment protocols when managing AIS patients.
papers.key_finding: The combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment group demonstrated significantly higher overall effectiveness (96.72% vs. 80.85%, P=0.017) with greater reductions in Cobb angle, trunk rotation, back pain, and greater improvements in functional capacity and quality of life measures.

papers.title: Angular Kinematic Analysis of Supine Cervical Thrusts Performed by Chiropractors and Chiropractic Students on Mannequins
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors produce mean cervical axial rotation of 33.9° during supine adjustments.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This biomechanical benchmark establishes that expert cervical thrusts deliver approximately 34° peak rotation with lateral bending around 32°, useful for standardizing technique quality and student training progression. Students and practitioners can reference these kinematic parameters to optimize adjustment delivery and ensure consistency with experienced clinicians.
papers.key_finding: Doctors of chiropractic demonstrated mean peak axial rotation of 33.9° with 14.6° rotation occurring in 144 milliseconds, achieving rotational velocity of 192.9°/s and acceleration of 4427°/s².

papers.title: Kinematic Assessment of Hip, Shoulder, and Elbow Movements of a Chiropractor Performing Side Posture Adjustments: Results From a Biomechanical Analysis
papers.one_line: Side-posture adjustments employ consistent body mechanics using hip and shoulder asymmetry with minimal elbow extension.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Effective side-posture adjustments rely on asymmetrical hip and shoulder positioning for stabilization and force transfer through body drop mechanics rather than upper extremity generation alone. Chiropractors should focus on consistent body positioning patterns while recognizing that individual technique parameters vary based on table height, patient size, and professional training background.
papers.key_finding: Side-posture adjustments demonstrated repeatable movement patterns with thrust-to-thrust consistency in kinematic sequences, characterized by asymmetrical shoulder and hip positioning and minimal elbow extension during force delivery, indicating body mechanics are systematically organized despite trial-to-trial angular magnitude variations.
papers.study_design: Biomechanical analysis using inertial measurement units

papers.title: CT-guided Foramen Ovale Injection of Mesenchymal Stem Cells: First Human Case Report of Trigeminal Neuralgia Relief
papers.one_line: CT-guided mesenchymal stem cell injection provided sustained trigeminal neuralgia relief in refractory case.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this is a single case report of an interventional procedure beyond typical chiropractic scope, it demonstrates an emerging biologic treatment option for refractory trigeminal neuralgia that chiropractors should be aware of when referring patients with failed conservative care. Patients with severe TN who have exhausted medication and chiropractic/manual therapies may benefit from discussion of this advanced intervention with appropriate pain specialists.
papers.key_finding: A single patient with 22-year history of severe refractory trigeminal neuralgia achieved significant pain reduction and medication cessation for 12 months following CT-guided foramen ovale injection of 20 million mesenchymal stem cells, with sustained cognitive improvements at follow-up.

papers.title: The effects of chiropractic adjustment on inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a pilot RCT.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment plus usual care showed no significant advantage over sham adjustment for childhood ADHD.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot RCT found no evidence that chiropractic adjustments provide additional benefit beyond usual care for ADHD symptoms in children. Both treatment and sham groups improved similarly, suggesting observed changes may reflect natural improvement, placebo effect, or usual care benefits. Chiropractors should not position spinal adjustment as a treatment for ADHD without stronger evidence from larger, well-designed trials.
papers.key_finding: Both chiropractic adjustment plus usual care and sham adjustment plus usual care groups showed significant improvements in ADHD scores at 4 and 8 weeks, but no statistically significant differences were found between groups.

papers.title: Myositis Ossificans Traumatica of Bilateral Sternocleidomastoid Muscles After Chiropractor Adjustment: A Case Report
papers.one_line: Myositis ossificans developed in neck muscles following chiropractic adjustment in young woman.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that forceful neck manipulation may trigger myositis ossificans in susceptible patients, particularly those with prior neck surgery or trauma. Post-adjustment persistent pain, trismus, and progressive stiffness warrant immediate medical referral for imaging and specialist evaluation. Consider careful case selection and modified technique in patients with significant surgical history.
papers.key_finding: A woman in her 20s with prior neck surgery developed bilateral sternocleidomastoid myositis ossificans with heterotopic ossification extending to supraclavicular tissues following chiropractic neck adjustment, presenting with persistent shoulder pain, trismus, and neck stiffness.

papers.title: Vertebral Subluxation and Systems Biology: An Integrative Review Exploring the Salutogenic Influence of Chiropractic Care on the Neuroendocrine-Immune System.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment may improve systemic health through neuroendocrine-immune modulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can frame spinal manipulation as potentially influencing whole-body physiology beyond musculoskeletal dysfunction, citing effects on blood pressure, heart rate variability, and sleep quality. This integrative perspective supports patient education about systemic health benefits and justifies holistic patient assessment. However, practitioners should acknowledge that precise neural mechanisms require further investigation.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic care appears to exert salutogenic effects on neuroendocrine-immune function through multiple neurologically mediated pathways, with documented improvements in blood pressure, heart rate variability, and sleep—outcomes extending beyond traditional musculoskeletal benefits.
papers.study_design: Systematic integrative review of mixed study designs

papers.title: A Case Report of U-Type Sacral Fracture After Chiropractic Adjustment.
papers.one_line: Drop-table chiropractic manipulation caused U-type sacral fracture with spinopelvic dissociation in elderly patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Elderly patients, particularly those with age-related bone quality changes, may be at increased risk for severe sacral injuries from drop-table manipulation. Clinicians should exercise particular caution with high-velocity, low-amplitude techniques in the lumbosacral region and maintain high suspicion for serious injury when patients report severe symptoms post-treatment. This case underscores the importance of appropriate patient selection, force modulation, and imaging when complications are suspected.
papers.key_finding: A 74-year-old male sustained a U-type sacral fracture (spinopelvic dissociation) following drop-table chiropractic manipulation, a previously unreported complication in the literature. Despite delayed diagnosis and prolonged hospitalization, conservative management resulted in return to baseline function within one year, though mild residual neuropathy persisted.

papers.title: Absence of Neuroplastic Changes in the Bilateral H-Reflex Amplitude following Spinal Manipulation with Activator IV.
papers.one_line: Activator IV spinal manipulation produces no measurable neuroplastic changes in H-reflex amplitude.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study suggests that Activator IV manipulation does not induce detectable spinal reflex neuroplasticity as measured by H-reflex testing. Clinicians should not rely on H-reflex changes as evidence of neurophysiological adaptation following Activator IV treatment, and alternative outcome measures may better capture treatment effects.
papers.key_finding: Bilateral H-reflex amplitude remained unchanged following Activator IV spinal manipulation, indicating an absence of detectable neuroplastic motor control adaptations.

papers.title: Acute Lumbar Schmorl's Node Following Chiropractic Adjustment
papers.one_line: Acute Schmorl's node developed post-chiropractic adjustment, resolved with conservative care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Acute Schmorl's nodes can occur following chiropractic manipulation but typically respond well to conservative management. Practitioners should recognize this as a potential complication and counsel patients appropriately. This case demonstrates that even when imaging shows acute pathology, conservative treatment often achieves significant pain relief.
papers.key_finding: A 41-year-old patient developed an acute Schmorl's node at L4-L5 following chiropractic adjustment, which resolved with conservative treatment achieving 85% pain relief.

papers.title: Management of people with low back pain: a survey of opinions and beliefs of Dutch and Belgian chiropractors.
papers.one_line: Dutch and Belgian chiropractors show 64.5% guideline adherence for LBP management with notable gaps in return-to-work advice.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors in this survey frequently used spinal adjustment (90%) and advised against bedrest (>90%), but inconsistently counseled patients on staying active and returning to work. Practitioners should strengthen adherence to evidence-based guidelines, particularly for acute LBP cases and occupational rehabilitation advice, to align practice with international standards.
papers.key_finding: Overall guideline adherence was 64.5%, with better adherence in chronic cases (73.4%) than acute cases (55.9%). Chiropractors were strong on limiting bedrest advice (98.5%) but weak on return-to-work guidance (59.4%) and encouraging activity (77.5%).

papers.title: Chiropractic Spinal Manipulation Prevents Secondary Hyperalgesia Induced by Topical Capsaicin in Healthy Individuals
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation blocks capsaicin-induced secondary hyperalgesia in healthy subjects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation may modulate central pain sensitization mechanisms, suggesting potential utility in preventing or managing conditions involving widespread pain amplification. This supports a neurophysiological mechanism for manipulation's analgesic effects beyond local tissue effects.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic spinal manipulation prevented the development of secondary hyperalgesia following capsaicin application, indicating manipulation can inhibit central sensitization pathways.
papers.study_design: Experimental study (likely crossover or within-subjects design)

papers.title: The prevalence of complementary and alternative medicine use among Turkish patients with primary headache
papers.one_line: 33% of Turkish headache patients use CAM, predominantly phytotherapy, cupping, and chiropractic adjustment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that one-third of headache patients in this population use CAM, with chiropractic adjustment representing 17.5% of CAM use. Longer disease duration is the primary predictor of CAM use, suggesting patients with chronic headaches are more likely to seek complementary care. Understanding these patterns helps chiropractors better counsel patients and integrate care with other CAM practitioners.
papers.key_finding: CAM was used by 33.3% of primary headache patients, with phytotherapy (37.5%), cupping (27.5%), and chiropractic adjustment (17.5%) being most common. Disease duration was the only significant predictor of CAM use, with longer disease duration strongly associated with CAM utilization (p=0.002).

papers.title: Resolution of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Following Correction for Upper Cross Syndrome-A Case Study and Brief Review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic correction of upper cross syndrome resolved GERD symptoms in one patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider postural assessment and UCS correction in patients presenting with GERD, as spinal misalignment may contribute to reflux symptoms. Implement cervical adjustments and soft tissue therapy targeting postural restoration, with regular maintenance visits to prevent symptom recurrence and secondary conditions.
papers.key_finding: A 35-year-old female with GERD and neck/upper back pain associated with upper cross syndrome experienced complete resolution of both GERD and musculoskeletal symptoms following chiropractic adjustment and soft tissue therapy, with sustained improvement at 12-month follow-up.

papers.title: Chiropractic Day: A Historical Review of a Day Worth Celebrating
papers.one_line: Historical review of Chiropractic Day celebration since Palmer's first adjustment in 1895.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic Day (September 18) provides an annual opportunity to reflect on professional heritage and strengthen community engagement. Chiropractors can leverage this day for patient education, community outreach, and professional development activities that reinforce the profession's value and mission.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic Day, commemorating D.D. Palmer's first adjustment on September 18, 1895, has evolved over 125+ years with various names and celebrations serving to honor the profession's origins and advance its mission through educational and community engagement activities.

papers.title: The effect of sacroiliac chiropractic adjustments on innominate angles.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments produce measurable changes in innominate bone angles.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Specific sacroiliac chiropractic adjustments can objectively correct innominate bone angulation and pelvic alignment. This measurable mechanical change supports the clinical goal of restoring proper pelvic mechanics and may have implications for patients with sacroiliac dysfunction.
papers.key_finding: The treatment group receiving specific chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments demonstrated measurable changes in innominate bone angles, leveling the pelvis toward correct anatomical alignment, while the control group (sham ultrasound) did not show comparable changes.

papers.title: Changes in radiographic parameters following chiropractic treatment in 10 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A retrospective chart review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment reduced Cobb angles by average 21.2% in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This small retrospective study suggests chiropractic adjustment may reduce Cobb angles and stabilize curves in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, with better outcomes in mild-to-moderate cases. However, the lack of control group, small sample size, and retrospective design limit clinical applicability; larger RCTs are needed before recommending chiropractic as primary treatment for AIS.
papers.key_finding: Cobb angles reduced from average 29.7° to 23.4° (21.2% improvement); 64% of curves showed morphological improvement and 36% showed stabilization, with better outcomes in mild-to-moderate scoliosis.

papers.title: Characterization of Horse Use in Therapeutic Horseback Riding Programs in the United States: A Pilot Survey
papers.one_line: Therapeutic riding horses work moderately with lameness and back soreness as primary health concerns.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that therapeutic horseback riding programs commonly employ chiropractic adjustment as a primary complementary therapy for lameness issues in horses. Back soreness and limb lameness are prevalent in these programs, indicating a potential market for equine chiropractic services. Understanding that therapeutic horses are ridden 2 hours/day, 4 days/week can inform case management and treatment frequency recommendations.
papers.key_finding: Therapeutic riding horses experience limb lameness and back soreness as top health issues, with chiropractic adjustment being the most commonly used complementary therapy after NSAIDs and massage. Horses in these programs work well within recommended limits with overall favorable health profiles.

papers.title: Measurement and Analysis of Biomechanical Outcomes of Chiropractic Adjustment Performance in Chiropractic Education and Practice
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors deliver faster, more consistent McTimoney adjustments than students.
papers.clinical_takeaway: McTimoney technique proficiency develops significantly between year-3 and year-5 of chiropractic education, with experienced DCs delivering thrusts 3× faster with less variability. Biomechanical metrics like thrust duration and time-to-peak-force can serve as objective performance feedback tools in student training programs. Dominant hand utilization produces greater force consistency, suggesting laterality considerations in technique refinement.
papers.key_finding: Experienced chiropractors demonstrated significantly shorter time-to-peak-force (69.96 ms vs 230.36 ms) and thrust duration (117.77 ms vs 283.84 ms) compared to year-3 students, with year-5 students showing intermediate proficiency approaching experienced clinician performance.

papers.title: Traumatic spinal injuries: A retrospective epidemiological analysis following the 2018 driving policy reform in Saudi Arabia.
papers.one_line: Traumatic spinal injury epidemiology shifted post-2018 Saudi driving reform; lumbar injuries predominate with mostly intact neurology.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Most traumatic spinal injuries present with intact neurology (93.7%), allowing conservative management in most cases. Female patients and older individuals require longer hospital stays, suggesting need for individualized discharge planning. Cervical involvement and vertebral subluxation/dislocation carry higher neurological severity risk and may warrant more aggressive intervention.
papers.key_finding: Among 623 traumatic spinal injury patients, 93.7% were neurologically intact (AIS E), lumbar region was most common injury site (53.9%), and motor vehicle accidents dominated (57.6%). Female sex, older age, psychiatric illness, higher AIS severity, pulmonary infection, and ICU admission independently predicted longer hospital stays.

papers.title: Management of Cervical lateral mass fractures - A systematic review
papers.one_line: Floating lateral mass fractures are unstable cervical injuries often requiring surgical fusion.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Floating lateral mass fractures (FLM) are uncommon but serious cervical injuries with high rates of vertebral subluxation (31%) when managed non-operatively with cervical collars alone. Surgical management, particularly anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF), is preferred due to inherent spinal instability. Chiropractors should recognize FLM as a red flag finding requiring immediate physician referral and avoid manipulation in suspected cases.
papers.key_finding: Of 332 patients with floating lateral mass fractures, 31% treated non-operatively developed vertebral subluxation, while surgical management (primarily ACDF) showed minimal post-operative subluxation, supporting surgical intervention as the preferred treatment.

papers.title: Animal Chiropractic: A Basic Description and Its Importance in Veterinary Practice
papers.one_line: Properly applied animal chiropractic by licensed professionals enhances animal function and recovery.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Animal chiropractic can be safely integrated into veterinary practice to improve strength, stability, and mobility through neurophysiological mechanisms. Veterinarians should consider AC as a complementary modality to optimize postoperative recovery and patient conditioning. Only licensed, extensively trained professionals should provide this care to ensure safety and efficacy.
papers.key_finding: Properly applied animal chiropractic improves afferent input and modulates motor neuron function, positively affecting patient strength, stability, mobility, conditioning, and postoperative recovery outcomes.

papers.title: Sublaminar stabilization (stapling) of the caudal cervical instability in Yorkshire terrier-A case report
papers.one_line: Sublaminar stapling stabilized cervical instability in small dog with five-year success.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this case involves veterinary rather than human chiropractic practice, it demonstrates that conservative treatment alone failed for 20 months in cervical instability, suggesting early imaging and intervention may be warranted in persistent cases. The surgical technique represents a stabilization option when conservative care proves unsuccessful, relevant for understanding when manual manipulation is contraindicated.
papers.key_finding: A Yorkshire terrier with C6-C7 instability unresponsive to 20 months of conservative treatment achieved long-term ambulatory recovery and pain resolution following sublaminar stapling stabilization, with sustained improvement over five years.

papers.title: Atlas Subluxation Complex, National Upper Cervical Chiropractic Association Intervention, and Dizziness Improvement: A Narrative Review of Historical Perspectives, Literature Synthesis, and a Path for Future Care.
papers.one_line: Atlas subluxation complex may contribute to dizziness and respond to NUCCA chiropractic care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider atlas subluxation as a potential etiological factor in patients with dizziness, particularly when other causes have been ruled out. NUCCA intervention may offer a treatment option, though clinicians should recognize current evidence is limited to case reports and conceptual frameworks. High-quality RCTs are needed before making definitive treatment recommendations based solely on this mechanism.
papers.key_finding: Conceptual evidence and case reports suggest atlas subluxation complex may contribute to dizziness pathogenesis and respond to NUCCA chiropractic correction, but rigorous high-quality controlled trials are lacking to establish efficacy.

papers.title: Catastrophic failure of anterior fusion for bilateral cervical facet dislocation: illustrative case
papers.one_line: Anterior-alone fusion may fail in bilateral cervical facet dislocations; combined anterior-posterior fixation recommended.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize bilateral cervical facet dislocation as a surgical emergency requiring immediate physician referral; anterior-alone fusion carries significant failure risk in complex cases. Understanding risk factors (age, posterior ligament damage, endplate/facet fractures) helps guide appropriate surgical approach selection for optimal patient outcomes.
papers.key_finding: A case of failed anterior-only fusion for bilateral cervical facet dislocation resulted in recurrent subluxation and spinal cord injury. Risk factors for construct failure include advanced age, bilateral facet injury, extensive posterior ligamentous damage, and associated fractures.

papers.title: The Dark Side of Musculoskeletal Care: Why Do Ineffective Techniques Seem to Work? A Comprehensive Review of Complementary and Alternative Therapies.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic and osteopathy lack robust biological plausibility; observed benefits appear mediated by placebo effects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This critical review challenges foundational concepts like vertebral subluxation and somatic dysfunction, suggesting placebo and contextual factors drive observed outcomes. Chiropractors should critically evaluate evidence for specific techniques and consider biobehavioral and psychosocial mechanisms. Transparency about evidence limitations is ethically important when counseling patients.
papers.key_finding: Osteopathy and chiropractic therapies lack empirical validation of their core biological concepts; research quality is often methodologically flawed, and placebo responses—driven by contextual, psychological, and non-specific factors—appear to account for much of the observed clinical benefit.

papers.title: Vertebral Column Subluxation in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Associated Dystrophic Scoliosis: A Report of Two Cases and Narrative Review
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation in NF1 dystrophic scoliosis requires surgical management; halo-gravity traction carries significant risks.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis with subluxation is a surgical emergency requiring immediate referral. Conservative management including bracing and traction is often ineffective and potentially dangerous in these cases. Patients presenting with NF1 and rapidly progressive scoliosis warrant imaging and prompt specialist consultation before conservative intervention.
papers.key_finding: Two cases of spontaneous vertebral subluxation in NF1 dystrophic scoliosis required surgical correction; halo-gravity traction failed and caused vascular injury in one patient. Surgical deformity correction with partial vertebral column resection achieved favorable outcomes.

papers.title: The best preferable sagittal vertical axis for the ankylosis spondylitis with thoracolumbar kyphosis following one-level pedicle subtraction osteotomy under different cervical range of motion
papers.one_line: Optimal sagittal vertical axis outcomes after pedicle subtraction osteotomy depend on cervical spine mobility.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that post-operative sagittal alignment in ankylosing spondylitis patients varies with cervical ROM, affecting long-term outcomes. Pre-operative and post-operative cervical assessment may inform referral decisions and post-surgical management strategies. Understanding these biomechanical relationships helps guide realistic expectations for kyphosis correction outcomes.
papers.key_finding: The optimal sagittal vertical axis following pedicle subtraction osteotomy for thoracolumbar kyphosis in ankylosing spondylitis patients differs based on cervical range of motion capacity.
papers.study_design: Case series or retrospective cohort analysis

papers.title: Secondary Analysis of a Dataset to Estimate the Prevalence of Vertebral Subluxation and Its Implications for Health Promotion and Prevention.
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation prevalence estimated at 78.55% in chiropractic patients across seven clinics.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study found high prevalence of vertebral subluxation (78.55%) in patients presenting for chiropractic care using an operational definition incorporating neurologic and kinesiologic exam components. The broad range of chief complaints (pain, headaches, visceral issues, mental health concerns) suggests chiropractors may address diverse health conditions. These findings support investigating chiropractic's potential role in primary prevention and general health promotion beyond musculoskeletal complaints.
papers.key_finding: Overall vertebral subluxation prevalence was 78.55% (95% CI = 76.68-80.42), with female prevalence of 77.17% and male prevalence of 80.15%; all per-clinic, age, and gender-stratified prevalences exceeded 50%.

papers.title: Associations between demographics and clinical ideology, beliefs, and practice patterns: a secondary analysis of a survey of randomly sampled United States chiropractors.
papers.one_line: Chiropractors' clinical ideology and practice patterns vary significantly by education, experience, and geographic location.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that their training program, years of experience, and regional practice environment significantly influence their clinical beliefs and practices. This variation across the profession may create patient confusion and hinder collaboration with other healthcare providers. Professional standardization of evidence-based practices could improve consistency and public trust.
papers.key_finding: Significant associations were found between chiropractors' ideology/beliefs/practices and their degree program of graduation, years since graduation, and geographic region of practice. Substantial variation exists across the profession regarding clinical examination, health conditions treated, role in healthcare, views on cancer treatment, vaccination attitudes, subluxation detection, and x-ray utilization.

papers.title: Spinal decompression and stabilisation in a cat with lumbar vertebral pathological fracture and subluxation, following discospondylitis and spinal epidural empyema
papers.one_line: Surgical decompression and stabilization successfully treated feline spinal infection with cord compression.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates that severe spinal infections (discospondylitis with epidural empyema) can cause acute neurological deterioration requiring surgical intervention beyond medical management. Chiropractors should recognize progressive paraparesis/paraplegia as red flags warranting urgent referral for imaging and possible surgical decompression rather than manipulation.
papers.key_finding: A 1-year-old cat with discospondylitis and spinal epidural empyema at L1-L2 causing pathological fracture, subluxation, and spinal cord compression was successfully treated with hemilaminectomy and spinal stabilization using wire and PMMA fixation, achieving optimal outcome despite rapid neurological deterioration.

papers.title: Veterinary Spinal Manipulative Therapy or Animal Chiropractic in Veterinary Rehabilitation
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic is a receptor-based modality with diagnostic and therapeutic applications in veterinary rehabilitation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While animal chiropractic may offer diagnostic and therapeutic benefits in veterinary rehabilitation, practitioners must understand its neuroanatomical and biomechanical mechanisms, recognize appropriate indications and contraindications, and know when to refer for further diagnostics rather than proceeding with treatment. This emphasizes the importance of comprehensive assessment before implementing spinal manipulative therapy in animal patients.
papers.key_finding: Veterinary spinal manipulative therapy is increasingly used in veterinary rehabilitation as a receptor-based modality, but clinicians must understand its mechanisms, indications, contraindications, and limitations to apply it safely and appropriately.

papers.title: A novel Hinge-Link correction system for vertebral column resection: a pilot study in a porcine model
papers.one_line: Novel surgical device achieves 94% scoliosis correction in animal model without neurological complications.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study demonstrates a new surgical device for severe scoliosis correction with excellent safety profile in animal models. While promising for complex spinal deformity cases requiring vertebral column resection, this is preclinical research—chiropractors should be aware of surgical advances but recognize that patient selection and surgical referral criteria remain critical.
papers.key_finding: The Hinge-Link correction system achieved 94% scoliosis correction (from 32° to 1.8°) with no neurological deficits or spinal cord damage in all five animals undergoing vertebral column resection.

papers.title: Remodeling morphology of the subluxated osteotomy vertebra in closing-opening wedge osteotomy in ankylosing spondylitis: would the anterior bony beak blunt?
papers.one_line: Closing-opening wedge osteotomy shows favorable bony remodeling in AS despite subluxation complications.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors managing AS patients post-osteotomy should monitor for vertebral subluxation (≥5mm sagittal translation), as it correlates with reduced sagittal vertical axis correction and limited spinal canal remodeling. Favorable anterior bony beak resorption occurs spontaneously during healing, but subluxation cases require closer radiographic surveillance and possible surgical consultation.
papers.key_finding: Closing-opening wedge osteotomy patients showed favorable adaptive remodeling with new bone formation and anterior bony beak resorption; however, 25% developed vertebral subluxation (≥5mm translation), which was associated with reduced global kyphosis correction and limited spinal canal remodeling capacity.

papers.title: Use of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging to assess a case of spinal injury in a Showa koi Cyprinus carpio
papers.one_line: CT and MRI identified severe vertebral subluxation with myelomalacia in an ornamental koi fish.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates advanced imaging protocols for detecting spinal cord compression and vertebral pathology in non-mammalian species. While not directly applicable to human chiropractic practice, the imaging methodology illustrates how cross-sectional imaging can reveal subluxation-related spinal cord damage before clinical deterioration occurs. The correlation between imaging findings and postmortem myelomalacia underscores the value of early advanced imaging in suspected spinal cord compression cases.
papers.key_finding: MRI revealed extensive vertebral centra alterations with multifocal spinal cord compression, and postmortem examination confirmed severe transmural myelomalacia associated with vertebral subluxation in a koi with progressive neurological decline.

papers.title: Posterior 3-Column Osteotomy for Treatment of Congenital Kyphosis with Multiple Thoracolumbar/Lumbar Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae: A Comparison Between Patients with Increasing Number of Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae
papers.one_line: Single-level posterior 3-column osteotomy effectiveness decreases with ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae in congenital kyphosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that congenital kyphosis with four or more anterior unsegmented vertebrae requires surgical intervention and has higher complication rates. Referral for surgical evaluation is appropriate when patients present with progressive kyphosis, particularly those with multiple vertebral anomalies. Conservative management alone is insufficient for these complex cases.
papers.key_finding: Patients with ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae had significantly higher preoperative kyphosis (82.9° vs 59.7°), greater remaining postoperative kyphosis (33.6° vs 15.1°), lower correction rates (61.2% vs 75.0%), and higher complication rates (67% vs 8%).

papers.title: Evaluation of United States chiropractic professional subgroups: a survey of randomly sampled chiropractors
papers.one_line: Three distinct chiropractic subgroups identified: spine/neuromusculoskeletal, primary care, and vertebral subluxation focused.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors fall into three distinct professional categories with different clinical philosophies and practice approaches. Understanding which subgroup aligns with your practice orientation can guide clinical decision-making, referral patterns, and patient communication. Recognition of these subgroups may help the profession advance more coherent healthcare positioning and evidence-based practice standards.
papers.key_finding: Large-scale random survey of US chiropractors identified three self-identified professional subgroups: 56.8% spine/neuromusculoskeletal focused, 22.0% primary care focused, and 21.2% vertebral subluxation focused, each with distinct ideological and practice characteristic patterns.

papers.title: The association between chiropractors' view of practice and patient encounter-level characteristics in Ontario, Canada: a cross-sectional study
papers.one_line: Chiropractors with unorthodox subluxation views treat more non-musculoskeletal conditions in shorter encounters.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that philosophical views on vertebral subluxation significantly influence clinical practice patterns, patient selection, and encounter length. Understanding these practice variations is important for interprofessional communication and establishing evidence-based treatment boundaries. Consider aligning practice approach with scope of practice regulations and evidence-based guidelines for musculoskeletal conditions.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors with unorthodox subluxation beliefs had 16.5 times higher odds of non-musculoskeletal encounters and 63 times higher odds of subluxation diagnosis, with 40% shorter encounter duration compared to orthodox-view practitioners.

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest - Week ending April 05, 2026
papers.one_line: Digest of 76 papers including pediatric stroke risk, legal liability, pain management outcomes, and mechanistic animal studies.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Cervical manipulation in toddlers carries documented serious complications including vertebral artery dissection and stroke—exercise extreme caution and ensure comprehensive informed consent. Combined practitioner-delivered and self-care complementary therapies enhance patient-perceived well-being and fatigue relief equivalent to manipulation alone for chronic pain.
papers.key_finding: Pediatric cervical manipulation can cause vertebral artery dissection with acute presentations (lethargy, vomiting, respiratory distress). Combined CIH therapies improve pain interference in ~40% of chronic pain patients while enhancing perceived improvements in fatigue, mental health, and well-being.
papers.study_design: Mixed (case report, legal analysis, pragmatic trial, animal model)

papers.title: CHIROPRACTIC RESEARCH DIGEST - 1 Week ending April 12, 2026
papers.one_line: Digest of 76 papers including pediatric manipulation risks, legal liability, and scoliosis management.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Exercise extreme caution with cervical manipulation in pediatric patients due to vertebral artery dissection risk; ensure comprehensive informed consent documentation. Integrating respiratory guidance with spinal adjustment significantly improves adolescent idiopathic scoliosis outcomes (96.7% vs 80.9% effectiveness).
papers.key_finding: Critical findings include rare but serious vertebral artery dissection in a 20-month-old post-manipulation, inadequate informed consent as basis for legal liability, and superior scoliosis treatment results combining respiratory guidance with adjustment protocols.
papers.study_design: Mixed (case report, legal analysis, cohort comparison)

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest - Week ending April 19, 2026
papers.one_line: Four studies examine analgesic reduction, practitioner motivations, pediatric stroke risk, and scoliosis rehabilitation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Standardized chiropractic care effectively reduces analgesic use in lumbar spinal stenosis patients post-treatment, though female patients and those with comorbidities may need additional deprescribing support. Critical safety concern: cervical manipulation in infants/toddlers carries significant vertebral artery dissection risk; alternative approaches strongly recommended for pediatric populations under 3 years.
papers.key_finding: Study 1 demonstrates chiropractic care reduces analgesic consumption post-treatment in LSS (45% baseline use), while Study 3 presents a critical safety case of vertebral artery dissection with stroke in a 20-month-old following cervical manipulation.
papers.study_design: Mixed (1 nationwide cohort, 1 cross-sectional survey, 1 case report, 1 incomplete abstract)

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest - Week ending April 26, 2026
papers.one_line: Four key studies address chiropractic integration in healthcare systems, pediatric safety risks, legal liability, and RCT research quality.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should pursue integration into FQHCs through Medicaid-reimbursing states and value-based payment models to expand MSK care access. Exercise extreme caution with cervical manipulation in pediatric patients and provide comprehensive informed consent documentation regarding arterial dissection and stroke risks. Stay current with RCT evidence quality to inform clinical decision-making.
papers.key_finding: FQHC integration is feasible via Medicaid coverage; pediatric cervical manipulation carries vertebral artery dissection risk; Canadian courts hold chiropractors liable for serious complications despite causation uncertainty; SMT RCT literature quality needs improvement.
