papers.study_design: Mixed: policy analysis, case report, legal analysis, and trial sequential analysis

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest - Week ending May 03, 2026
papers.one_line: Digest of 79 papers covering spinal manipulation complications, LSS treatment outcomes, and informed consent.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize rare but serious post-manipulation complications: orthostatic headache suggesting CSF leak (95% recover with conservative care), and vertebral artery dissection risk in pediatric patients. Standardized chiropractic care reduces analgesic use in lumbar stenosis, particularly opioids and gabapentinoids, though high pre-treatment users may need targeted deprescribing strategies.
papers.key_finding: Among 79 reviewed papers: intracranial hypotension from CSF leak post-manipulation is rare (21 cases, 95% full recovery); chiropractic care for lumbar stenosis significantly reduces analgesic use; pediatric cervical manipulation carries vertebral artery dissection risk.
papers.study_design: Mixed (scoping review with case report, nationwide cohort study, case report)

weeks.label: 1 Week ending May 03, 2026
weeks.digest_summary:
# Chiro Weekly Morning Briefing

**This week's research hits an uncomfortable sweet spot: our clinical evidence is getting sharper while our liability profile is getting murkier.**

Let's start with the good news. A major systematic review of manual therapy and depression found that chiropractic manipulation worked in 83% of studies with defined psychiatric diagnoses—a genuinely impressive hit rate that deserves attention beyond the MSK crowd. Meanwhile, a nationwide cohort study of nearly 7,300 patients with lumbar stenosis showed real-world analgesic reduction after chiropractic care, though with an important caveat: 10% of heavy users accounted for 43–68% of all medication consumption, suggesting we need smarter deprescribing strategies for comorbid and female patients. On the neurophysiology side, animal models are finally illuminating *why* manipulation might work—a rat study showed spinal manipulation drives nucleus pulposus resorption through JNK pathway activation, with effects that exceeded epidural steroid injection.

But here's where it gets thorny. We've got documented cases of serious vascular events—a 20-month-old with vertebral artery dissection and ischemic stroke post-cervical manipulation, a teenager with vertebrobasilar ischemia triggered by yoga-style head maneuvers, and a scoping review of 21 intracranial hypotension cases (95% women, thankfully with good outcomes). A legal case analysis from Canada shows courts are now holding practitioners liable based on inadequate informed consent disclosures, even when causation remains epidemiologically debatable. Meanwhile, trial sequential analysis confirms we've been chasing diminishing returns—futility boundaries for SMT versus conservative care were crossed nearly two decades ago, yet we're still publishing RCTs on the same comparison.

**Here's your actionable takeaway: audit your cervical manipulation consent forms *this week*. Courts are no longer satisfied with generic risk acknowledgments. Document that you've discussed vertebral artery dissection, intracranial hypotension, and stroke risk—especially for women, patients on anticoagulants, and anyone with connective tissue concerns. And for lumbar stenosis patients on chronic analgesics, add explicit deprescribing conversations into your care plan, targeting that high-use minority where medication burden clusters.** The evidence supports what you do, but the liability landscape demands you document it meticulously.

papers.title: Chiropractic regulation in Italy: liability profiles in healthcare field
papers.one_line: Italian chiropractors lack formal healthcare regulation, creating liability and practice complexities.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors in Italy cannot independently manage informed consent or liability protections available to regulated healthcare professionals, requiring physician collaboration in patient care. Practitioners should be aware of their non-healthcare professional status and associated legal vulnerabilities, and advocate for formal regulatory recognition and standardized educational requirements to clarify professional scope and liability frameworks.
papers.key_finding: Despite a 2007 law intended to regulate Italian chiropractors, the profession remains unevenly regulated without established educational standards, expert committees, or national board oversight, leaving practitioners ineligible for healthcare professional liability protections and unable to independently obtain informed consent.

papers.title: Manual therapy modalities and depression: a systematic review
papers.one_line: Manual therapies show promise for reducing depression symptoms as complementary treatment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic manipulation demonstrated effectiveness in 83.3% of studies for reducing depression symptoms, with acupressure and craniosacral therapy showing the highest success rates (100%). Consider incorporating manual therapy as a complementary approach for patients with depressive symptoms, while maintaining appropriate referral pathways to mental health professionals. Evidence quality remains moderate (SORT B rating), warranting continued monitoring of emerging research.
papers.key_finding: Of 97 included studies, 88.2% of those with specific psychiatric diagnoses reported significant depression symptom reduction; chiropractic manipulation was effective in 5 of 6 studies (83.3%), while acupressure and craniosacral therapy each showed 100% effectiveness across included studies.

papers.title: Intracranial Hypotension Following Spinal Manipulation: A Case Report and Scoping Review of the Literature
papers.one_line: CSF leaks causing intracranial hypotension occur rarely after spinal manipulation, with favorable outcomes in 95% of cases.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that new-onset orthostatic headache within one week post-manipulation may indicate CSF leak with intracranial hypotension, warranting immediate neuroimaging and medical referral. While rare, this serious complication predominantly affects women undergoing cervical manipulation and typically resolves with conservative management or epidural blood patching. Documented structural spinal abnormalities may increase risk and should inform treatment selection.
papers.key_finding: Among 21 documented cases of intracranial hypotension following spinal manipulation, 81% were women, most presented with orthostatic headache within one week, and 95% achieved full recovery with conservative management or epidural blood patching as primary treatments.
papers.study_design: Scoping review with illustrative case report

papers.title: Yoga Causing Vertebrobasilar Ischemia with Neuro-Ophthalmic Presentation: A Case Report
papers.one_line: Yoga poses causing vertebral artery compression and vertebrobasilar ischemia with visual symptoms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should screen patients for symptoms of vertebrobasilar insufficiency (blurred vision, dizziness) before and after neck manipulation, particularly in patients who practice yoga or participate in activities involving neck hyperextension/rotation. Consider modifying or avoiding aggressive cervical manipulation in patients with pre-existing VBI risk or symptoms. Educate patients on positioning activities that may compromise vertebral artery blood flow.
papers.key_finding: A 56-year-old woman experienced transient vision loss and dizziness during yoga poses, with dynamic transcranial Doppler ultrasound confirming vertebral artery compression and posterior cerebral artery flow reduction during head-turning maneuvers and neck hyperextension.

papers.title: Radiographic Sagittal Alignment and Kinetic Chain Alterations in Geriatric Patients With Scoliosis: A Case Series
papers.one_line: Geriatric AIS pain may stem from kinetic chain dysfunction rather than curve itself.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Geriatric patients with longstanding scoliosis and chronic pain may benefit from multimodal non-surgical rehabilitation targeting global spinal alignment and kinetic chain dysfunction rather than focusing solely on the primary curve. The CLEAR Institute protocol approach showed clinically meaningful pain reduction and improved sagittal alignment in these cases, suggesting a shift in clinical approach toward addressing compensatory biomechanical patterns.
papers.key_finding: Both geriatric patients with history of AIS demonstrated clinically meaningful pain reduction and improved sagittal spinal alignment following multimodal non-surgical rehabilitation, supporting the hypothesis that chronic pain relates more to kinetic chain dysfunction and compensatory degeneration than to the primary scoliotic curve.

papers.title: Effects of thoracic manipulation with trigger point therapy on inflammatory cytokine levels in individuals with multiple sclerosis: a pilot study
papers.one_line: Thoracic spinal manipulation may reduce pro-inflammatory cytokines in relapsing-remitting MS.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study suggests that combining thoracic spinal manipulation with trigger point therapy may modulate inflammatory markers (IL-8, IL-17A, GM-CSF, MIP-1β, IFN) in MS patients, with effects observable within 2 hours post-treatment. While promising, these are preliminary findings requiring larger RCTs before clinical recommendations can be made. Chiropractors managing MS patients should consider this as emerging research supporting further investigation of manual therapy's immune-modulating potential.
papers.key_finding: Six pro-inflammatory cytokines/chemokines (IL-8, IL-17A, GM-CSF, MIP-1β, IFN, and one other) demonstrated moderate to large effect sizes at multiple post-intervention timepoints favoring spinal manipulation over sham manipulation in RRMS participants.

papers.title: Integrating Chiropractic Care into Federally Qualified Health Centers: Policy, Payment, and Pathways for Sustainable Spine and Musculoskeletal Care.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic integration into FQHCs improves MSK care access and reduces opioid use through policy and payment reform.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should advocate for Medicaid and Medicare coverage expansion in FQHCs to establish sustainable practices serving underserved populations. Positioning chiropractic as embedded MSK specialists within primary care teams reduces opioid prescribing and addresses a major disability driver. Explore alternative payment models (capitation, shared savings, grants) beyond fee-for-service to improve financial viability.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic integration in FQHCs is primarily enabled by Medicaid coverage with ~50% of chiropractic FQHC patients on Medicaid; supportive policies can expand nonpharmacologic MSK care access in safety-net settings while reducing downstream utilization.
papers.study_design: Policy analysis and comparative financing review

papers.title: The CARL II cohort: what we did and what came out of it.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic Academy for Research Leadership cohort study describes research methods and outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This paper documents the CARL II cohort study's methodology and findings, providing evidence for chiropractic research rigor and outcomes. Chiropractors can reference this work to understand best practices in clinical research and how evidence supports chiropractic interventions.
papers.key_finding: The CARL II cohort represents a structured approach to gathering chiropractic research data. Specific outcomes and findings are referenced in supplementary material.

papers.title: Attitudes and perceptions of health care professionals concerning chiropractors and chiropractic practice: a systematic review
papers.one_line: Healthcare professionals hold variable attitudes toward chiropractors and chiropractic care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Understanding interdisciplinary perceptions is crucial for collaborative practice. Chiropractors should be aware that professional attitudes vary significantly, which may affect referral patterns and interprofessional communication. Focusing on evidence-based practice and clear communication of scope can improve professional relationships.
papers.key_finding: The systematic review synthesizes healthcare professionals' attitudes toward chiropractors and chiropractic practice, revealing heterogeneous perceptions across different healthcare disciplines.

papers.title: Mediators of the effect of chiropractic care on 12- and 52-week outcomes for U.S. active-duty military personnel with low back pain: secondary analysis of a clinical trial
papers.one_line: Pain reduction mediates chiropractic care's effects on sleep and social function at 52 weeks.
papers.clinical_takeaway: In military personnel with low back pain, improvements in pain intensity and disability are the primary mechanisms through which chiropractic care reduces sleep disturbance and improves social role function over 52 weeks. Clinicians should prioritize early pain and disability reduction as these drive longer-term functional improvements. Non-pain factors (fatigue, sleep, social role) have minimal reverse mediation on pain outcomes, suggesting direct pain management is the key therapeutic target.
papers.key_finding: Pain-related disability (RMDQ) mediated 17-44% of chiropractic care's effects on sleep disturbance and social role at 52 weeks, while non-pain factors mediated only 10-19% of longer-term pain outcomes.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial

papers.title: Acupuncture-moxibustion combined with chiropractic therapy for adolescent psychogenic vomiting with Mallory-Weiss syndrome: a case report
papers.one_line: Combined acupuncture and chiropractic therapy effectively treated adolescent psychogenic vomiting with Mallory-Weiss syndrome.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates that integrated acupuncture-moxibustion and chiropractic treatment may be beneficial for psychogenic vomiting in adolescents with concurrent upper GI pathology. Chiropractors should consider the psychological and somatogenic components of vomiting cases and potential for safe multimodal care when appropriate.
papers.key_finding: A single adolescent patient with psychogenic vomiting, Mallory-Weiss syndrome, and antral gastritis showed clinical improvement following combined acupuncture-moxibustion (targeting governor vessel and liver-stomach harmony) and chiropractic therapy.

papers.title: Use of prescribed analgesics before and after a standardised chiropractic care programme among patients with lumbar spinal stenosis: a nationwide cohort study.
papers.one_line: Standardized chiropractic care reduces analgesic use in lumbar stenosis patients post-treatment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic care programs for lumbar spinal stenosis are associated with declining analgesic use after treatment completion, particularly for opioids and gabapentinoids. Pre-existing heavy analgesic use, female sex, and comorbidities predict continued medication use, suggesting targeted deprescribing strategies may benefit these subgroups. These findings support guideline-based non-pharmacological chiropractic intervention as an effective alternative to medication for managing LSS.
papers.key_finding: Analgesic use (paracetamol, NSAIDs, opioids, gabapentinoids) declined after chiropractic care program completion; however, 10% of users accounted for 43-68% of total medication use, with female sex, comorbidities, and pre-existing use associated with continued analgesic dependence.
papers.study_design: Nationwide cohort study using health service registries

papers.title: A survey of student loan burden among United States Chiropractors: Insights on debt, relief, and educational value.
papers.one_line: US chiropractors graduate with substantial debt exceeding income, with poor financial ROI perception.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that 85% of practitioners carry significant student loan debt (median $240,000) with median gross income of $76,000, creating financial stress that may impact practice sustainability and career satisfaction. Consider financial planning strategies, practice efficiency, and income diversification when advising new graduates or managing your own practice finances.
papers.key_finding: Mean student loan debt at graduation was $176,297, increasing to $232,062 by survey completion. 65% of respondents reported they would not choose a chiropractic career again, primarily due to poor financial ROI perception (70% rated financial ROI as low or very low) relative to median gross income of $76,000.

papers.title: Longer-term chiropractic care outcomes for US active-duty military personnel with low back pain: secondary analysis of a pragmatic clinical trial
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care demonstrates sustained benefits for military low back pain over extended follow-up.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This secondary analysis of a pragmatic trial suggests chiropractic care produces durable improvements in low back pain outcomes for active-duty military personnel beyond initial treatment phases. Chiropractors can reference this military population data when discussing longer-term prognosis and treatment planning with military patients.
papers.key_finding: The study examines sustained outcomes from chiropractic treatment in a military population with low back pain, focusing on longer-term follow-up data from an existing pragmatic trial.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of pragmatic clinical trial

papers.title: MOTIVATIONS, TRAINING OUTCOMES, AND CLINICAL PRACTICE CHARACTERISTICS OF NORTH AMERICAN CHIROPRACTORS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL SURVEY
papers.one_line: North American chiropractors are primarily motivated by prosocial goals with strong clinical reasoning and counseling skills.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors report high competence in clinical reasoning, patient communication, and lifestyle counseling within autonomous, time-rich practices. Practice orientation significantly influences clinical behavior (manipulation frequency and imaging decisions), suggesting professional alignment matters clinically. Evidence-based practice and rigorous communication training should complement existing strengths in counseling and reasoning.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors showed predominantly prosocial motivations, strongest training outcomes in clinical reasoning and communication, and practice behaviors clearly stratified by subluxation orientation (vitalistic practitioners used more manipulation; biomedical practitioners ordered fewer routine radiographs).

papers.title: Profession-Related Accreditation Requirements in Australia Regarding Anatomy Teaching: A Web-Based Desktop Audit.
papers.one_line: Australian health profession accreditation standards lack specific anatomy curriculum guidance except for six disciplines.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic educators should note that while anatomy is foundational to practice, Australian accreditation bodies provide minimal specific guidance on anatomy content and teaching approaches. Chiropractors should advocate for stronger accreditation standards that explicitly define anatomy competencies relevant to musculoskeletal and neurological assessment and treatment. This gap presents an opportunity for the profession to develop and propose explicit anatomy requirements that ensure graduate competency for safe clinical practice.
papers.key_finding: Of 20 Australian health professions audited, only six (Audiology, Dentistry, Exercise Science, Optometry, Oral Health, Speech Pathology) had specific accreditation requirements for anatomy curriculum; chiropractic was not among those with explicit standards. Four disciplines had no anatomy curricula specifications at all, highlighting inconsistency in professional standards.
papers.study_design: Web-based desktop audit with content analysis

papers.title: Pediatric vertebral artery dissection and ischemic stroke following chiropractic manipulation.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic cervical manipulation can cause vertebral artery dissection in infants, presenting with non-specific symptoms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must recognize that cervical manipulation in very young children carries risk of vertebral artery dissection with potentially serious neurological consequences. Non-specific presentations (lethargy, vomiting, respiratory distress) in pediatric patients post-manipulation warrant immediate medical evaluation. Consider avoiding high-force cervical manipulation in infants and toddlers, and obtain thorough informed consent from guardians regarding rare but serious risks.
papers.key_finding: A 20-month-old developed vertebral artery dissection with ischemic stroke following cervical chiropractic manipulation, presenting with non-specific acute symptoms including lethargy, vomiting, cyanosis, and respiratory distress.

papers.title: Assessing the importance and feasibility of quality measures for chiropractic care: a national survey of U.S. chiropractors
papers.one_line: National survey identifies which quality measures chiropractors consider important and feasible to implement.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This survey establishes consensus among U.S. chiropractors on prioritized quality measures that are practical to implement in clinical practice. Chiropractors can use these findings to guide selection of meaningful metrics for performance assessment and practice improvement initiatives.
papers.key_finding: The study identifies which quality measures chiropractors deem both clinically important and feasible to implement, informing development of practice standards and accountability frameworks.

papers.title: Estimating Lumbar Spine Foraminal Disc Measurements Using Ultrasound and X-Ray Imaging Through Advanced Image Annotation, Processing, and Mathematical Modeling During Chiropractic Traction Procedures: A Feasibility Study
papers.one_line: Novel methodology aligns X-ray and ultrasound measurements during traction to quantify lumbar spine elongation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This feasibility study demonstrates that combined X-ray and ultrasound imaging with mathematical modeling can standardize spinal measurements during traction, potentially improving diagnostic precision. Chiropractors may use this methodology foundation to objectively quantify traction effects on foraminal height and disc space changes, supporting evidence-based patient documentation and treatment optimization.
papers.key_finding: Progressive traction forces (1.8–11.3 kg) produced consistent, measurable increases in spinal metrics (height and area) at L3-L4, L4-L5, and L5-S1 levels. The integrated imaging methodology successfully bridged static X-ray and dynamic ultrasound data to quantify real-time spinal elongation under graded loads.

papers.title: Cervical spinal manipulative therapy, arterial dissection, and the law: Informed consent and causation in Goldie C.arsenault.
papers.one_line: Canadian court finds chiropractor liable for stroke after cervical manipulation despite causation uncertainty.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case highlights the legal importance of comprehensive informed consent disclosures about cervical artery dissection risk, even where causation remains scientifically uncertain. Chiropractors should document detailed consent conversations addressing material risks and consider pre-treatment screening for arterial vulnerability factors. The court's binary causation framing (traumatic vs. spontaneous) may oversimplify the actual biomechanical and pathophysiological mechanisms.
papers.key_finding: Trial court found informed consent disclosure inadequate and imposed liability based on clinical opinion favoring causation, while treating population-level epidemiological evidence as controversial and rejecting interaction models between latent arterial susceptibility and manipulation.
papers.study_design: Legal case analysis with clinical review

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management approaches back pain treatment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrating spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial self-management strategies may provide a more comprehensive approach to back pain care. Chiropractors can enhance outcomes by addressing psychological and social factors alongside manual treatment.
papers.key_finding: The paper examines spinal manipulation in combination with biopsychosocial self-management for back pain, though specific results cannot be determined without the abstract.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain-Reply
papers.one_line: Author response on spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management for back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This appears to be a correspondence/reply piece addressing clinical implementation of spinal manipulation alongside patient education in self-management strategies. Consider integrating behavioral and psychosocial components with manipulation to optimize back pain outcomes.
papers.key_finding: No abstract available; this is a letter/reply article rather than an original research study.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Combined spinal manipulation and self-management addresses back pain through biopsychosocial approach.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrating spinal manipulation with patient education on self-management strategies and psychosocial factors may enhance treatment outcomes for back pain. Chiropractors should emphasize behavioral, cognitive, and lifestyle modifications alongside manual therapy to optimize results.
papers.key_finding: The study explores combined spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial self-management interventions for back pain, suggesting a multifaceted approach beyond manual therapy alone.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management improves back pain outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrating biopsychosocial self-management strategies with spinal manipulation may enhance treatment efficacy for back pain patients. Consider educating patients on psychological and behavioral factors alongside manual therapy to optimize clinical outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Unable to determine without access to abstract. Title suggests combined approach of manipulation plus self-management shows promise for back pain.

papers.title: Research Waste in Randomised Control Trials of Spinal Manipulative Therapy for Chronic Low Back Pain: Evidence From Trial Sequential Analysis
papers.one_line: Sufficient evidence for SMT efficacy in chronic low back pain was established by 2002-2004; subsequent RCTs constitute research waste.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Current evidence adequately supports SMT for chronic low back pain management; clinicians can confidently recommend SMT based on existing data. Rather than conducting additional confirmatory trials, research resources should focus on novel questions such as optimal treatment dosing, patient selection criteria, or comparative effectiveness against emerging interventions to advance the field.
papers.key_finding: Trial sequential analysis demonstrated that futility boundaries for SMT versus conservative treatments were crossed by 2002-2004 for both pain and functional status outcomes; RCTs published after these dates have not added new evidence and represent research waste.
papers.study_design: Trial Sequential Analysis of Cochrane systematic review data

papers.title: Physiological changes of cortisol and oxytocin following manual therapy: a scoping review
papers.one_line: Manual therapy produces variable cortisol and oxytocin responses; standardization needed.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While manual therapy may influence stress hormones (cortisol) and bonding hormones (oxytocin), current evidence is mixed and inconsistent due to methodological variation. Chiropractors should recognize hormonal mechanisms as plausible but not yet definitively established. Future standardized protocols are needed to clarify whether neuroendocrine changes meaningfully contribute to MT clinical outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Of 72 eligible studies examining cortisol and/or oxytocin responses to manual therapy (massage, osteopathic manipulation, spinal manipulation), findings were heterogeneous across intervention types, populations, and outcome measures. Most studies measured cortisol; fewer investigated oxytocin, with both showing variable and inconsistent responses.

papers.title: Spinal manipulative therapy promotes nucleus pulposus resorption and alleviates pain in a rat model of lumbar disc herniation via JNK-dependent regulation of inflammation and tissue remodeling.
papers.one_line: SMT promotes disc herniation resorption and pain relief through JNK-dependent inflammatory regulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: SMT appears superior to corticosteroid injection for lumbar disc herniation by promoting nucleus pulposus resorption while maintaining a balanced inflammatory microenvironment that supports healing. The mechanism involves selective modulation of inflammatory pathways (JNK-dependent) rather than broad suppression, suggesting SMT optimizes conditions for tissue restoration. These findings support SMT as a primary intervention for LDH with potential long-term tissue healing benefits.
papers.key_finding: SMT significantly reduced mechanical allodynia from day 3 and achieved near-complete nucleus pulposus resorption by day 28, outperforming epidural corticosteroid injection. These benefits were dependent on JNK pathway activation and were abolished in JNK-knockout mice, confirming JNK as the essential mediator.
papers.study_design: Animal model study (rat LDH model with mechanistic validation in knockout mice)

papers.title: Adverse events among older adults receiving chiropractic spinal manipulation and related treatments: an updated systematic review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic treatment in older adults produces mostly mild-to-moderate AEs; no catastrophic events reported.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can reassure older adult patients that severe adverse events are rare (9/412 events) and catastrophic events were not reported in this systematic review. Most adverse events are mild-to-moderate (muscle soreness, stiffness, headache, dizziness). However, clinicians should implement standardized AE definitions and data collection processes to better track patient safety outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Of 412 study-related adverse events in older adults (>55 years) across 25 included studies, only 9 were severe and none were catastrophic. Mild-to-moderate symptoms like muscle soreness and stiffness were most common, while 4 of 6 severe case report AEs were vascular in nature (associated with spinal manipulation).

papers.title: Effects of Spinal Manipulation and Dry Needling on Headache and Migraine: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.one_line: Systematic review evaluating spinal manipulation and dry needling efficacy for headache and migraine.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This systematic review synthesizes RCT evidence on two common chiropractic interventions for headache and migraine management. Chiropractors can reference this review to understand the current evidence base and inform patient discussions about treatment expectations.
papers.key_finding: The review examines randomized controlled trials comparing spinal manipulation and dry needling as treatments for headache and migraine disorders to establish their clinical effectiveness.

papers.title: One Spinal Manipulation Session Does Not Affect Static, Quasi-Static and Dynamic Balance or Pressure Pain Threshold in Individuals With Chronic Low Back Pain: A Randomized Clinical Controlled Trial
papers.one_line: Single spinal manipulation session did not improve balance or pain threshold in chronic low back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: A single manipulation session may not be sufficient to produce acute changes in balance or pain sensitivity in chronic low back pain patients. Multiple sessions or combined treatment approaches may be needed to achieve measurable functional improvements. Consider setting realistic expectations with patients regarding single-visit outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Single spinal manipulation produced no significant improvements in static balance (SOT), dynamic balance (SEBT), or pressure pain threshold immediately, at 24 hours, or 1 week post-intervention compared to placebo.

papers.title: Neck proprioception and mobility improved after upper neck and spine treatment: a randomized controlled trial
papers.one_line: Upper neck manipulation improves cervical proprioception and mobility compared to no treatment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The One-to-Zero system targeting the C0-C1 joint complex produces measurable improvements in neck proprioception and range of motion within 2-6 weeks. Chiropractors can use this approach for patients with proprioceptive deficits and cervical dysfunction, particularly those with altered kinesthetic awareness.
papers.key_finding: Treatment group showed significantly greater improvements in head-to-target repositioning accuracy, neck range of motion, pain, and disability compared to control group. Proprioceptive gains were accompanied by improved cervical mobility, suggesting normalization of afferent feedback from upper cervical structures.

papers.title: Verbal framing, rather than measured cognitive-affective variables, is associated with short-term outcomes after spinal manipulation: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
papers.one_line: Pre-treatment verbal framing predicts short-term outcomes after spinal manipulation better than patient expectations.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should prioritize how they frame treatment messages before spinal manipulation, as positive verbal framing appears more influential on immediate pain outcomes than patient pre-treatment expectations. Consider standardizing treatment language to optimize short-term patient outcomes, as the words used immediately before manipulation may matter more than managing patient expectations beforehand.
papers.key_finding: Short-term pain intensity (NPRS-11) and pressure pain threshold were associated with verbal framing (positive, neutral, or negative) delivered before manipulation, but not with measured expectations, attitudes toward manual therapy, or expectation fulfillment.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial

papers.title: Clinical features of manual therapy interventions in people with tension-type headache: A scoping review
papers.one_line: Manual therapy for tension-type headache shows wide variation in techniques, dosage, and outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Manual therapy is commonly used for tension-type headache, but protocols vary significantly without clear mechanistic justification. Cervical and suboccipital structures are most frequently targeted. Standardized, mechanism-informed treatment protocols with consistent outcome measures are needed to improve evidence quality and clinical reproducibility.
papers.key_finding: Thirty-three RCTs revealed substantial heterogeneity in manual therapy techniques (spinal manipulation, myofascial release, suboccipital inhibition, friction massage), treatment dosages, target structures, and outcome measures, limiting interpretability and clinical applicability.

papers.title: The Effect of Joint Mobilization and Manipulation on Proprioception: Systematic Review with Limited Meta-Analysis
papers.one_line: Joint mobilization and manipulation may improve proprioception through afferent stimulation mechanisms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Mobilization and manipulation techniques can enhance proprioceptive function, potentially improving balance and neuromuscular control in patients. This provides a mechanistic rationale for including these techniques in treatment plans for proprioceptive deficits and balance disorders.
papers.key_finding: Joint mobilization and manipulation demonstrate potential effects on proprioceptive function, likely through stimulation of mechanoreceptors and afferent nervous system input.

papers.title: Chiropractic Management of Adults with Cervicogenic or Tension-Type Headaches: Development of a Clinical Practice Guideline
papers.one_line: Evidence-based guideline recommends spinal manipulation for cervicogenic headache and multimodal care for tension-type headache.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can confidently use spinal manipulation as a primary intervention for cervicogenic headache, but should integrate it within multimodal care for tension-type headache. Practitioners should incorporate comprehensive history-taking including red flag screening and appropriate examination protocols. Single-modality interventions (acupuncture, meditation, education) lack sufficient evidence for standalone use.
papers.key_finding: Spinal manipulation is recommended for cervicogenic headache management; for tension-type headache, manipulation should be part of multimodal care. Evidence was insufficient to strongly recommend acupuncture, education, meditation/mindfulness, or isolated modalities.
papers.study_design: Clinical practice guideline development via umbrella review and Delphi consensus

papers.title: Effects of segmental spinal manipulation on adolescent scoliosis based on electromyography parameters
papers.one_line: Segmental spinal manipulation reduces Cobb angle and alters paraspinal muscle EMG patterns in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Segmental spinal manipulation demonstrates measurable effects on paraspinal muscle recruitment patterns and reduces spinal curvature (Cobb angle) in adolescent scoliosis patients. This electromyographic evidence supports three-dimensional spinal adjustment as part of conservative care, though muscle strength improvement was not demonstrated. Consider integrating segmental manipulation protocols into AIS management programs alongside other interventions.
papers.key_finding: Segmental spinal manipulation significantly increased paraspinal muscle Turns (EMG signal recruitment) in multiple positions and reduced Cobb angle compared to ordinary massage, though did not increase muscle strength parameters.

papers.title: Mechano responsiveness of neuroimmune cross-talk in bone and joints: A narrative review with implications for force-based manipulations
papers.one_line: Neuroimmune system regulates bone health; manual therapy may modulate these responses.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation and manual therapy can potentially influence bone-related neuroimmune responses, though direct evidence of bone changes remains limited. Clinicians should personalize treatment intensity and type based on patient age, hormonal status, and comorbidities to optimize neuroimmune and bone health outcomes. Physical activity remains the best-supported intervention for favorable bone neuroimmune responses.
papers.key_finding: While physical activity clearly affects bone neuroimmune responses, force-based manipulations (spinal manipulation, massage, manual therapy) show early promise for neuroimmune modulation but lack direct evidence of actual bone changes.

papers.title: Rehabilitation effects of combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment on adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.one_line: Combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment improves outcomes in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Adding structured respiratory guidance to standard chiropractic adjustment increases treatment efficacy for adolescent scoliosis from 81% to 97%. This combined approach significantly improves Cobb angle, back strength, pain, exercise tolerance, and quality of life metrics. Consider incorporating breathing instruction as an adjunct to adjustment protocols for scoliosis patients.
papers.key_finding: The respiratory chiropractic group achieved a 96.72% effective rate versus 80.85% in the conventional group, with superior improvements in Cobb angle, trunk rotation, back strength, pain scores, and functional capacity across multiple outcome measures.

papers.title: Angular Kinematic Analysis of Supine Cervical Thrusts Performed by Chiropractors and Chiropractic Students on Mannequins
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors produce peak cervical rotation of ~34° during supine cervical adjustments.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Cervical adjustments by experienced DCs involve approximately 34° of peak axial rotation delivered over ~144 milliseconds with rotational velocities around 193°/s. This kinematic data provides objective parameters for technique education and quality control in chiropractic cervical manipulation instruction.
papers.key_finding: Experienced chiropractors achieved mean peak axial rotation of 33.9° during supine cervical thrusts, with 14.6° of rotation occurring between thrust onset and peak in 144 milliseconds.

papers.title: Kinematic Assessment of Hip, Shoulder, and Elbow Movements of a Chiropractor Performing Side Posture Adjustments: Results From a Biomechanical Analysis
papers.one_line: Side-posture adjustment biomechanics show repeatable movement patterns utilizing body drop rather than arm force alone.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Effective side-posture adjustments rely on coordinated hip, shoulder, and elbow mechanics with asymmetrical positioning for stabilization and force transfer. Chiropractors should emphasize body drop mechanics and whole-body coordination rather than isolated upper extremity force to improve technique consistency and potentially reduce injury risk. Movement pattern repeatability suggests side-posture technique can be standardized and taught systematically.
papers.key_finding: Kinematic analysis revealed repeatable movement patterns across multiple adjustments despite trial-to-trial angular magnitude variations, with the right elbow contributing minimal extension during thrust, confirming that effective force transfer occurs primarily through body drop mechanics and coordinated hip-shoulder positioning.
papers.study_design: Biomechanical analysis using inertial measurement units

papers.title: CT-guided Foramen Ovale Injection of Mesenchymal Stem Cells: First Human Case Report of Trigeminal Neuralgia Relief
papers.one_line: CT-guided MSC injection into foramen ovale provides significant trigeminal neuralgia pain relief without adverse effects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates a novel interventional approach to trigeminal neuralgia that achieved pain reduction and medication reduction without cognitive side effects. While this is a single case report with long-term symptom recurrence at 12 months, it represents an emerging regenerative medicine option for TN patients who have failed conservative treatments. Chiropractors should be aware of this intervention as a referral option for refractory TN cases, particularly when patients experience intolerable medication side effects.
papers.key_finding: A single TN patient with 22-year history and failed conventional treatments (including chiropractic adjustment) achieved dramatic pain reduction and medication discontinuation at 1 month post-MSC injection, with sustained improvement and reduced medication requirements at 12 months despite some symptom recurrence.

papers.title: The effects of chiropractic adjustment on inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a pilot RCT
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment showed no significant benefit over sham for pediatric ADHD symptoms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study found no significant difference between real and sham chiropractic adjustments for ADHD symptoms in children, with both groups improving similarly over 8 weeks. While the study establishes feasibility for future research, current evidence does not support chiropractic adjustment as a specific treatment for ADHD. Practitioners should continue integrating ADHD management with conventional care approaches and evidence-based interventions.
papers.key_finding: Both chiropractic adjustment plus usual care and sham adjustment plus usual care groups showed significant ADHD symptom improvements at 4 and 8 weeks, with no significant between-group differences, suggesting improvements were likely attributable to usual care rather than the adjustment intervention.

papers.title: Myositis Ossificans Traumatica of Bilateral Sternocleidomastoid Muscles After Chiropractor Adjustment: A Case Report
papers.one_line: Myositis ossificans developed bilaterally in sternocleidomastoid muscles following chiropractic neck adjustment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize myositis ossificans as a rare but serious complication of neck manipulation, characterized by heterotopic bone formation in soft tissues. Patients presenting with persistent pain, trismus, and restricted motion after cervical adjustment warrant imaging and specialist referral to rule out this condition. This case highlights the importance of careful patient selection and adjustment technique modification in vulnerable patients.
papers.key_finding: A woman in her 20s developed myositis ossificans in bilateral sternocleidomastoid muscles following chiropractic cervical adjustment, presenting with persistent shoulder and neck pain, trismus, and imaging evidence of heterotopic ossification.

papers.title: Vertebral Subluxation and Systems Biology: An Integrative Review Exploring the Salutogenic Influence of Chiropractic Care on the Neuroendocrine-Immune System
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment may influence neuroendocrine-immune function through multiple neural pathways.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This review supports exploring chiropractic care's systemic effects beyond musculoskeletal outcomes, including potential benefits on blood pressure, heart rate variability, and sleep quality. Consider discussing these broader health-promoting mechanisms with patients as part of comprehensive wellness conversations. Future research should clarify the specific neural pathways mediating these systemic effects.
papers.key_finding: Synthesis of two decades of chiropractic research suggests adjustment may produce salutogenic effects on neuroendocrine-immune system function and physical indicators of well-being through neurologically mediated pathways, extending benefits beyond neuromusculoskeletal outcomes.

papers.title: A Case Report of U-Type Sacral Fracture After Chiropractic Adjustment
papers.one_line: Drop-table chiropractic manipulation caused severe U-type sacral fracture in elderly patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Drop-table techniques carry risk of serious spinopelvic dissociation injuries, particularly in elderly patients. Practitioners should exercise heightened caution with forceful manipulation in older populations and maintain awareness of this serious complication. Early diagnosis is critical to prevent prolonged morbidity and hospitalization.
papers.key_finding: A 74-year-old male sustained a U-type sacral fracture (spinopelvic dissociation) from drop-table chiropractic manipulation, resulting in delayed diagnosis and prolonged hospitalization but eventual return to baseline function with conservative management.

papers.title: Absence of Neuroplastic Changes in the Bilateral H-Reflex Amplitude following Spinal Manipulation with Activator IV.
papers.one_line: Activator IV spinal manipulation does not produce measurable neuroplastic changes in H-reflex amplitude.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study suggests that Activator IV instrument-assisted manipulation does not acutely alter spinal reflex excitability as measured by H-reflex testing. Clinicians using Activator IV should not expect immediate neurophysiological changes in reflex arc function as a mechanism of treatment effect. Alternative mechanisms of action should be considered when explaining Activator IV's clinical benefits to patients.
papers.key_finding: Bilateral H-reflex amplitude showed no significant neuroplastic changes following Activator IV spinal manipulation, indicating this instrumented technique does not acutely modulate spinal reflex circuitry in the measured parameters.

papers.title: Acute Lumbar Schmorl's Node Following Chiropractic Adjustment
papers.one_line: Acute Schmorl's node developed post-chiropractic adjustment, resolved with conservative care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that acute Schmorl's nodes can develop following spinal manipulation, though they typically respond well to conservative management. This case demonstrates that such complications need not necessitate surgical intervention and can achieve significant symptomatic improvement (85% pain relief) with appropriate non-operative treatment. Consider imaging in patients with acute worsening of symptoms post-adjustment to identify potential complications early.
papers.key_finding: A 41-year-old male developed an acute Schmorl's node at L4-L5 following chiropractic manipulation, which was successfully managed conservatively with >85% pain relief.

papers.title: Management of people with low back pain: a survey of opinions and beliefs of Dutch and Belgian chiropractors
papers.one_line: Dutch and Belgian chiropractors show moderate guideline adherence (64.5%) with gaps in acute LBP and return-to-work advice.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should prioritize exercise counseling and return-to-work advice alongside spinal adjustment, particularly in acute LBP cases. While most practitioners correctly advise against bedrest, only 59% counsel on return-to-work—an opportunity to improve guideline-concordant care and patient outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors reported 64.5% overall guideline adherence, with better adherence in chronic cases (73.4%) than acute cases (55.9%). Adjustment was applied in 90% of vignettes, but exercise advice was given in only 33-50% of cases, and return-to-work advice in just 59%.

papers.title: Chiropractic Spinal Manipulation Prevents Secondary Hyperalgesia Induced by Topical Capsaicin in Healthy Individuals
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation prevents capsaicin-induced secondary hyperalgesia in healthy subjects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation may modulate central pain processing mechanisms, potentially preventing the spread of pain sensitization. This suggests manipulation has analgesic effects beyond local tissue treatment, which could benefit patients with widespread pain conditions.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic spinal manipulation prevented the development of secondary hyperalgesia following topical capsaicin application, suggesting manipulation influences central nervous system pain processing.

papers.title: The prevalence of complementary and alternative medicine use among Turkish patients with primary headache.
papers.one_line: 33% of Turkish headache patients use CAM, predominantly phytotherapy, cupping, and chiropractic adjustment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic adjustment is used by 17.5% of Turkish primary headache patients, particularly those with longer disease duration (>10 years). Chiropractors should be aware that CAM-seeking headache patients may have chronic conditions and should document outcomes to contribute evidence on efficacy and safety.
papers.key_finding: CAM use was reported in 33.3% of primary headache patients, with chiropractic adjustment among the top three modalities (17.5%). Longer disease duration was the only significant predictor of CAM use (p=0.002).

papers.title: Resolution of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Following Correction for Upper Cross Syndrome-A Case Study and Brief Review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic treatment of upper cross syndrome resolved concurrent GERD symptoms in one patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider upper cross syndrome assessment in patients presenting with GERD, as postural correction through cervical adjustment and soft tissue therapy may provide concurrent symptom relief. Regular preventive chiropractic care targeting posture restoration appears beneficial for long-term symptom management.
papers.key_finding: A 35-year-old female with GERD and upper cross syndrome achieved complete resolution of both neck/upper back pain and reflux symptoms following chiropractic treatment focused on posture correction, with sustained improvement at 12-month follow-up.

papers.title: Chiropractic Day: A Historical Review of a Day Worth Celebrating
papers.one_line: Historical overview of Chiropractic Day celebrating the profession's origins since September 18, 1895.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic Day (September 18) provides an opportunity for practitioners to reflect on professional heritage and engage in community education and service. Chiropractors can use this annual observance to strengthen patient relationships through volunteer activities, educational initiatives, and professional development.
papers.key_finding: Daniel David Palmer's first adjustment on September 18, 1895, marks the founding of chiropractic, and the profession has celebrated this milestone under various names for over 125 years as a means to honor its heritage and reflect on its growth.

papers.title: The effect of sacroiliac chiropractic adjustments on innominate angles.
papers.one_line: Sacroiliac adjustments produce measurable changes in innominate bone angles.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments can objectively correct innominate bone angles and pelvic alignment using the PALM PALpation Meter. This provides measurable evidence that specific SIJ adjustments affect bony position, supporting their use in treating sacroiliac dysfunction with anatomical correction.
papers.key_finding: Specific chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments produced measurable changes in innominate bone angles, resulting in pelvic alignment correction, whereas sham ultrasound did not.

papers.title: Changes in radiographic parameters following chiropractic treatment in 10 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A retrospective chart review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment reduced Cobb angles by 21% in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic intervention may offer potential benefits for mild-to-moderate AIS, with documented radiographic improvements in 64% of cases and stabilization in others. However, this small retrospective study lacks controls and long-term follow-up; larger RCTs are needed before recommending chiropractic care as primary AIS treatment. Consider as adjunctive therapy with medical monitoring and imaging follow-up.
papers.key_finding: Mean Cobb angle correction of 6.3° (21.2% reduction) with morphological improvements in 64% of curves and stabilization in 36%; better outcomes in mild-to-moderate scoliosis.

papers.title: Characterization of Horse Use in Therapeutic Horseback Riding Programs in the United States: A Pilot Survey
papers.one_line: Therapeutic riding horses receive moderate workloads with lameness and back soreness as primary health concerns.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that therapeutic riding horses commonly present with back soreness and lameness issues; chiropractic adjustment is already a frequently utilized complementary therapy in PATH International programs. Understanding the typical workload (4 days/week, 2 hours/day, 45-minute sessions) helps contextualize musculoskeletal complaints in equine patients used for therapy.
papers.key_finding: Therapeutic riding horses had median workloads of 4 days/week and 2 hours/day, with lameness and back soreness as the most common health issues. Chiropractic adjustment was among the top supplemental/complementary therapies utilized alongside NSAIDs and massage.

papers.title: Measurement and Analysis of Biomechanical Outcomes of Chiropractic Adjustment Performance in Chiropractic Education and Practice
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors deliver McTimoney thrusts faster and more consistently than students.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Thrust speed and consistency improve significantly with training and experience. Clinicians should aim for rapid force application with minimal variability, particularly using dominant hand technique. Biomechanical feedback during education may enhance technique development.
papers.key_finding: Experienced DCs delivered McTimoney thrusts 3× faster to peak force (70 ms vs 230 ms) and 2.5× faster overall thrust duration (118 ms vs 284 ms) compared to year-3 students, with significantly less variability. Year-5 students showed performance similar to experienced practitioners.

papers.title: Traumatic spinal injuries: A retrospective epidemiological analysis following the 2018 driving policy reform in Saudi Arabia.
papers.one_line: Motor vehicle accidents dominate traumatic spinal injury cases; lumbar region most common with 93.7% neurologically intact.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Most traumatic spinal injuries present with intact neurology and lumbar involvement, but clinicians should monitor for pulmonary complications and psychiatric comorbidities that significantly extend hospital stays. Female patients and those over 32.5 years require heightened assessment for prolonged recovery. Cervical spine injuries and vertebral subluxation/dislocation are strong predictors of neurological severity.
papers.key_finding: Four-wheel motor vehicle accidents account for 57.6% of traumatic spinal injuries; lumbar region involvement is most common (53.9%), with 93.7% of patients neurologically intact at presentation. Female sex, older age, psychiatric illness, pulmonary infection, and ICU admission are independent predictors of longer hospital stays.

papers.title: Management of Cervical lateral mass fractures -A systematic review.
papers.one_line: Floating lateral mass fractures require surgical management due to inherent spinal instability.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Floating lateral mass fractures (FLM) of the cervical spine are severe injuries with inherent instability that typically require surgical intervention rather than conservative care. Non-operative management with cervical collars results in vertebral subluxation in 31% of cases, while surgical fusion (ACDF) shows minimal post-operative complications. Chiropractors should recognize FLM as a contraindication to manipulation and refer for surgical evaluation when suspected.
papers.key_finding: Of 332 patients with floating lateral mass fractures, 31% of those treated non-operatively developed vertebral subluxation, while anterior cervical fusion (ACDF) was the most common surgical approach with minimal post-operative subluxation complications.

papers.title: Animal Chiropractic: A Basic Description and Its Importance in Veterinary Practice
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic improves function and recovery through neurological modulation when properly applied by trained professionals.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Animal chiropractic can enhance patient outcomes by improving afferent input and motor neuron function, leading to better strength, stability, and mobility. Implementation requires veterinarians to obtain extensive postgraduate training in animal chiropractic techniques. Consider incorporating AC into veterinary practice to optimize patient conditioning, performance, and postoperative recovery.
papers.key_finding: Properly applied animal chiropractic is safe and effective for improving neurological function and patient outcomes. The modality enhances afferent input and modulates ventral horn motor neurons, positively affecting strength, stability, and postoperative recovery.

papers.title: Sublaminar stabilization (stapling) of the caudal cervical instability in Yorkshire terrier-A case report
papers.one_line: Sublaminar stabilization successfully treated cervical spine instability in a small-breed dog.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this is a veterinary case, it demonstrates sublaminar stabilization techniques for cervical instability that may inform understanding of spinal stabilization principles. The 5-year follow-up outcome suggests that conservative care failure (20 months) may warrant consideration of advanced imaging and specialist referral for human patients with similar presentations of cervical instability with myelopathic signs.
papers.key_finding: A Yorkshire terrier with C6-C7 cervical instability and tetraparesis achieved long-term functional recovery (5 years) following sublaminar stabilization with Kirschner wire and suture fixation, after conservative treatment failed over 20 months.

papers.title: Atlas Subluxation Complex, National Upper Cervical Chiropractic Association Intervention, and Dizziness Improvement: A Narrative Review of Historical Perspectives, Literature Synthesis, and a Path for Future Care
papers.one_line: NUCCA intervention may address dizziness by correcting atlas subluxation complex, though high-quality evidence is limited.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Upper cervical misalignment (atlas subluxation complex) may contribute to dizziness in some patients and warrants consideration in differential diagnosis. NUCCA-style corrective care shows promise in case reports and conceptual models, but practitioners should recognize the current lack of high-quality RCT evidence and maintain appropriate referral pathways for serious underlying pathology.
papers.key_finding: Case reports and conceptual evidence suggest atlas subluxation complex may be an etiological factor in dizziness amenable to NUCCA chiropractic care, but robust RCTs and observational studies are needed to establish efficacy.

papers.title: Catastrophic failure of anterior fusion for bilateral cervical facet dislocation: illustrative case
papers.one_line: Anterior-only fusion fails in bilateral cervical facet dislocation; combined anterior-posterior fixation recommended.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize bilateral cervical facet dislocation as a surgical emergency requiring imaging confirmation and immediate physician referral. Understanding that anterior-only fusion carries high failure risk in these cases—particularly with posterior ligament damage, endplate fractures, or advanced age—helps communicate appropriate urgency to patients and surgical consultants.
papers.key_finding: Anterior-alone fusion for bilateral cervical facet dislocation resulted in construct failure and recurrent subluxation causing spinal cord injury. Risk factors for failure include advanced age, bilateral facet injury, extensive posterior ligamentous complex damage, and fractures involving endplates, facets, or pedicles.

papers.title: The Dark Side of Musculoskeletal Care: Why Do Ineffective Techniques Seem to Work? A Comprehensive Review of Complementary and Alternative Therapies.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic and osteopathy lack biological plausibility; observed benefits appear largely placebo-mediated.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This critical review questions core chiropractic concepts like vertebral subluxation and highlights methodological flaws in supporting research. Chiropractors should recognize that placebo and contextual factors substantially contribute to patient outcomes, and consider strengthening evidence through rigorous clinical trials and focusing on scientifically validated, mechanism-based interventions.
papers.key_finding: Osteopathy and chiropractic rest on concepts lacking robust empirical validation; purported effects appear substantially mediated by placebo responses rather than specific biological mechanisms.

papers.title: Vertebral Column Subluxation in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Associated Dystrophic Scoliosis: A Report of Two Cases and Narrative Review
papers.one_line: NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis with vertebral subluxation requires complex surgical correction; halo-gravity traction carries significant risks.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis with subluxation is a surgical disease requiring immediate specialist referral. Conservative management including bracing and traction is typically unsuccessful and may cause serious complications. Patients presenting with NF1, severe progressive scoliosis, and neurological symptoms warrant urgent orthopedic/neurosurgical consultation rather than chiropractic intervention.
papers.key_finding: Two patients with NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis and vertebral subluxation (T4-5 and C7-T1) required surgical deformity correction with partial vertebral column resection. Halo-gravity traction was either unsuccessful or led to serious vascular and spinal cord complications, highlighting the dangers of conservative approaches in this population.

papers.title: The best preferable sagittal vertical axis for the ankylosis spondylitis with thoracolumbar kyphosis following one-level pedicle subtraction osteotomy under different cervical range of motion
papers.one_line: Optimal sagittal vertical axis target varies with cervical mobility in ankylosing spondylitis kyphosis surgery.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This surgical study identifies ideal spinal alignment targets for ankylosing spondylitis patients undergoing corrective osteotomy, accounting for individual cervical spine mobility. Chiropractors managing AS patients should understand post-surgical alignment goals when considering conservative care or co-managing with surgical colleagues. Cervical range of motion appears critical in determining optimal postoperative sagittal balance.
papers.key_finding: The optimal sagittal vertical axis (SVA) target for correcting thoracolumbar kyphosis in ankylosing spondylitis varies depending on individual cervical range of motion, suggesting personalized surgical planning improves outcomes.

papers.title: Secondary Analysis of a Dataset to Estimate the Prevalence of Vertebral Subluxation and Its Implications for Health Promotion and Prevention
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation prevalence was 78.55% in chiropractic patients across seven clinics.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study found high prevalence of vertebral subluxation (78.55%) in patients seeking chiropractic care, supporting the potential role of chiropractic in health promotion and prevention. The broad demographic representation suggests chiropractors encounter subluxation across age and gender groups. However, the retrospective, non-randomized design from chiropractic clinics limits generalizability to the general population.
papers.key_finding: Overall prevalence of vertebral subluxation was 78.55% (95% CI = 76.68-80.42) in chiropractic patients, with all age- and gender-stratified subgroups showing ≥50% prevalence. Female prevalence was 77.17% and male prevalence was 80.15%.

papers.title: Associations between demographics and clinical ideology, beliefs, and practice patterns: a secondary analysis of a survey of randomly sampled United States chiropractors.
papers.one_line: US chiropractors' ideology and practice patterns vary significantly by education program, career length, and geography.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic practice ideology and beliefs are strongly influenced by graduation program, years in practice, and geographic location, creating significant practice variation across the profession. This heterogeneity in clinical approaches—particularly regarding subluxation detection, vaccination attitudes, and cancer treatment claims—may undermine public trust and professional credibility. Chiropractors should be aware of these ideological divisions and consider aligning with evidence-based, science-integrated practice standards to improve interprofessional relationships.
papers.key_finding: Clinical ideology, beliefs, and practice patterns among US chiropractors differ significantly based on graduation program, years since degree completion, and geographic region, with wide variation in responses regarding subluxation detection, vaccination attitudes, x-ray utilization, and claims about chiropractic treatment of cancer.

papers.title: Spinal decompression and stabilisation in a cat with lumbar vertebral pathological fracture and subluxation, following discospondylitis and spinal epidural empyema
papers.one_line: Surgical decompression and stabilization successfully treated feline spinal epidural empyema with pathological fracture.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this is a veterinary case, it demonstrates the critical importance of advanced imaging (MRI/CT) in identifying spinal infections with secondary mechanical instability. Chiropractors should recognize that progressive neurological deficits in the presence of fever or systemic signs warrant imaging to rule out serious pathology before manipulation. Surgical stabilization may be necessary when infection-induced vertebral compromise causes neurological emergency.
papers.key_finding: Hemilaminectomy with spinal decompression and PMMA-wire stabilization achieved optimal neurological recovery in a cat with discospondylitis-induced pathological fracture and epidural empyema, despite rapid deterioration to paraplegia with absent nociception.

papers.title: Veterinary Spinal Manipulative Therapy or Animal Chiropractic in Veterinary Rehabilitation
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic is a receptor-based modality with diagnostic and therapeutic potential in veterinary rehabilitation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Veterinary chiropractors should understand the neuroanatomical and biomechanical mechanisms of spinal manipulative therapy in animals, including proper indications and contraindications. Knowledge of when to refer for further diagnostics is essential, as animal chiropractic functions as part of a multimodal rehabilitation approach rather than standalone treatment.
papers.key_finding: Animal chiropractic is increasingly used in veterinary rehabilitation as a receptor-based therapeutic modality, but practitioners must understand its mechanisms, appropriate applications, and limitations to integrate it safely within multimodal treatment protocols.

papers.title: A novel Hinge-Link correction system for vertebral column resection: a pilot study in a porcine model.
papers.one_line: Novel Hinge-Link device safely corrects severe scoliosis via vertebral column resection in animal model.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study demonstrates a novel surgical technique for severe scoliosis correction with promising neurological safety and 94% deformity correction. While currently in preclinical testing, chiropractors should be aware of emerging surgical options for severe cases requiring referral. The device's three-dimensional control may improve outcomes in surgical candidates with severe, progressive scoliosis unsuitable for conservative care.
papers.key_finding: The Hinge-Link system achieved 94% scoliosis correction (from 32° to 1.8°) with no neurological deficits, vertebral subluxation, or dural impingement in all five pigs undergoing vertebral column resection.

papers.title: Remodeling morphology of the subluxated osteotomy vertebra in closing-opening wedge osteotomy in ankylosing spondylitis: would the anterior bony beak blunt?
papers.one_line: AS patients undergoing lumbar osteotomy show favorable bony beak remodeling despite some developing vertebral subluxation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that ankylosing spondylitis patients with thoracolumbar kyphosis who undergo surgical osteotomy may experience adaptive bone remodeling, though those with vertebral subluxation (≥5mm translation) have limited spinal canal remodeling capacity. Close monitoring of sagittal alignment parameters post-operatively is important for patients with subluxation complications.
papers.key_finding: After single-level lumbar closing-opening wedge osteotomy in AS patients, favorable adaptive resorption of the anterior bony beak and new bone formation occurred during 2+ year follow-up; however, patients with vertebral subluxation (≥5mm sagittal translation) demonstrated limited spinal canal remodeling ability and greater loss of global kyphosis correction.

papers.title: Use of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging to assess a case of spinal injury in a Showa koi Cyprinus carpio
papers.one_line: CT and MRI detected spinal cord compression and myelomalacia in koi with neurological dysfunction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates the clinical utility of advanced imaging (CT/MRI) for diagnosing vertebral pathology and spinal cord compression in non-traditional animal patients. While not directly applicable to human chiropractic practice, the imaging protocol illustrates how cross-sectional imaging can reveal subtle spinal cord involvement that correlates with neurological deficits. Chiropractors may consider this methodology when evaluating similar spinal pathology in human patients, particularly regarding early detection of myelomalacia.
papers.key_finding: MRI revealed extensive vertebral centra alterations with multifocal spinal cord compression and transmural myelomalacia associated with vertebral subluxation in a koi presenting with progressive neurological dysfunction.

papers.title: Posterior 3-Column Osteotomy for Treatment of Congenital Kyphosis with Multiple Thoracolumbar/Lumbar Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae: A Comparison Between Patients with Increasing Number of Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae
papers.one_line: Single-level 3-column osteotomy effectively corrects congenital kyphosis with ≤3 anterior unsegmented vertebrae but shows reduced efficacy with ≥4 vertebrae.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors managing congenital kyphosis patients should recognize that surgical candidates with ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae have significantly worse outcomes and higher complication rates. Referral timing and realistic patient expectations regarding correction limitations are critical when ≥4 vertebrae are involved. Conservative management may be preferable initially in these complex cases.
papers.key_finding: Patients with ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae had significantly higher preoperative kyphosis (82.9° vs. 59.7°), lower postoperative correction rates (61.2% vs. 75.0%), higher residual kyphosis (33.6° vs. 15.1°), and substantially higher complication rates (67% vs. 8%). Vertebral column resection was required in 83.3% of ≥4 AUV cases versus 46.1% in 3 AUV cases.

papers.title: Evaluation of United States chiropractic professional subgroups: a survey of randomly sampled chiropractors.
papers.one_line: US chiropractors self-identify into three distinct subgroups with differing clinical ideologies and practice styles.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The chiropractic profession contains three major subgroups: spine/neuromusculoskeletal-focused (57%), primary care-focused (22%), and vertebral subluxation-focused (21%). Understanding which subgroup alignment guides your practice can clarify your clinical identity, inform continuing education choices, and help position your practice within the healthcare system. Recognition of these professional divisions is important for interprofessional communication and professional identity clarity.
papers.key_finding: Three distinct chiropractic subgroups were identified based on perceived professional role in healthcare: spine/neuromusculoskeletal-focused (56.8%), primary care-focused (22.0%), and vertebral subluxation-focused (21.2%), each with substantially different clinical practice beliefs and behaviors.

papers.title: The association between chiropractors' view of practice and patient encounter-level characteristics in Ontario, Canada: a cross-sectional study
papers.one_line: Chiropractors with unorthodox views treat non-musculoskeletal conditions, diagnose subluxation more frequently, and see patients briefly.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that philosophical views of practice significantly influence clinical decision-making and patient populations served. Those adopting unorthodox subluxation-based paradigms are more likely to treat non-musculoskeletal complaints and use subluxation diagnoses, which may impact interprofessional communication and evidence-based practice alignment. Practice philosophy warrants self-reflection regarding alignment with musculoskeletal scope of practice.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors with unorthodox views (subluxation-based) had 16.5 times higher odds of non-musculoskeletal encounters and 63 times higher odds of subluxation diagnoses, with 33% shorter encounter durations compared to orthodox-view practitioners.

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest - Week ending April 05, 2026 (76 papers reviewed)
papers.one_line: Four key studies on pediatric manipulation risks, legal liability, combined self-care therapies, and SMT mechanisms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Cervical manipulation in toddlers carries serious vertebral artery dissection risk requiring caution and informed consent. Combined practitioner-delivered and self-care complementary therapies enhance patient-perceived benefits without additional pain relief. Document pre-existing risk factors thoroughly and consider alternative treatments for very young children.
papers.key_finding: Study 1: 20-month-old developed vertebral artery dissection with stroke after cervical manipulation. Study 3: Combined CIH therapies achieved ~40% clinically meaningful pain improvement with higher perceived benefits in fatigue and mental health versus single intervention.
papers.study_design: Mixed (case report, legal analysis, pragmatic trial, animal model)

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest: Week ending April 12, 2026
papers.one_line: Pediatric cervical manipulation carries vertebral artery dissection risk; combined respiratory-adjustment therapy improves scoliosis outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Exercise extreme caution with pediatric cervical manipulation due to vertebral artery dissection risk; provide comprehensive informed consent documentation. Integrate respiratory guidance with spinal adjustment protocols to achieve superior outcomes (96.7% vs 80.9% effectiveness) in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis management.
papers.key_finding: Pediatric cervical manipulation caused vertebral artery dissection in a toddler (resolved conservatively); combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment achieved 96.72% effectiveness versus 80.85% for conventional treatment in adolescent scoliosis.
papers.study_design: Digest of mixed designs: case report, legal analysis, retrospective cohort

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest: 1 Week ending April 19, 2026
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care reduces analgesics in spinal stenosis; caution warranted in pediatric cervical manipulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Standardized chiropractic programs effectively reduce analgesic use in lumbar spinal stenosis patients, particularly for NSAIDs and paracetamol, supporting non-pharmacological management guidelines. However, extreme caution is required with cervical manipulation in pediatric patients due to vertebral artery dissection risk; consider alternative gentler approaches for infants and toddlers.
