papers.title: Effects of thoracic manipulation with trigger point therapy on inflammatory cytokine levels in individuals with multiple sclerosis: a pilot study
papers.one_line: Thoracic manipulation reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines in relapsing-remitting MS patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study suggests chiropractic thoracic manipulation combined with trigger point therapy may modulate inflammatory markers (IL-8, IL-17A, GM-CSF, MIP-1β, IFN-γ) in RRMS patients, warranting larger RCTs. Consider this intervention as a potential adjunctive therapy for MS-related inflammation, though evidence remains preliminary and should not replace conventional MS treatment.
papers.key_finding: Six pro-inflammatory cytokines/chemokines demonstrated moderate to large effect sizes at multiple post-intervention timepoints favoring spinal manipulation over sham-SM. Results suggest spinal manipulation may modulate immune responses in neurodegenerative disease populations.

papers.title: Integrating Chiropractic Care into Federally Qualified Health Centers: Policy, Payment, and Pathways for Sustainable Spine and Musculoskeletal Care.
papers.one_line: Medicaid and Medicare policy changes can expand chiropractic integration into FQHCs to reduce opioid use.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should engage with FQHC administrators and policymakers in Medicaid-reimbursing states to establish integrated MSK services. Value-based payment models, shared savings arrangements, and grant funding provide viable pathways beyond fee-for-service reimbursement. Integration positions chiropractors as embedded spinal specialists reducing opioid prescribing and downstream healthcare costs.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic integration in FQHCs is primarily enabled by Medicaid coverage with ~50% of FQHC chiropractic patients on Medicaid; supportive Medicare and Medicaid policies could expand nonpharmacologic MSK care delivery in safety-net settings.

papers.title: The CARL II cohort: what we did and what came out of it
papers.one_line: CARL II cohort describes chiropractic research leadership initiatives and outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This paper documents the Chiropractic Academy for Research Leadership's cohort methodology and findings, providing a framework for integrating research into chiropractic practice. Understanding CARL II's approach can help practitioners engage with evidence-based research and contribute to the evidence base for chiropractic care.
papers.key_finding: The abstract provided is incomplete and does not specify the primary results or key findings from the CARL II cohort study.

papers.title: Attitudes and perceptions of health care professionals concerning chiropractors and chiropractic practice: a systematic review
papers.one_line: Systematic review examining how other healthcare professionals perceive chiropractors and chiropractic practice.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Understanding interprofessional perceptions can inform strategies to improve collaboration with other healthcare providers. Chiropractors may benefit from education and communication initiatives to address misconceptions among conventional healthcare professionals. Building stronger professional relationships could enhance patient referral networks and integrated care.
papers.key_finding: The review synthesizes existing evidence on attitudes and perceptions held by various healthcare professionals toward chiropractors and chiropractic care, likely identifying common themes of acceptance, skepticism, or knowledge gaps.

papers.title: Mediators of the effect of chiropractic care on 12- and 52-week outcomes for U.S. active-duty military personnel with low back pain: secondary analysis of a clinical trial
papers.one_line: Pain reduction mediates chiropractic care's effects on sleep and social function in military personnel.
papers.clinical_takeaway: In active-duty military with low back pain, improvement in pain intensity and disability drives downstream improvements in sleep and social role functioning at 52 weeks. Chiropractors should prioritize pain and disability reduction early in treatment, as these improvements cascade into broader functional gains.
papers.key_finding: Early improvement in pain intensity (NPRS) and pain-related disability (RMDQ) at 6 weeks mediated 44% of fatigue improvement, 17% of sleep improvement, and 33% of social role improvement at 52 weeks. Non-pain factors had negligible mediating effects on longer-term pain outcomes.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial

papers.title: Acupuncture-moxibustion combined with chiropractic therapy for adolescent psychogenic vomiting with Mallory-Weiss syndrome: a case report
papers.one_line: Combined acupuncture-moxibustion and chiropractic therapy successfully treated adolescent psychogenic vomiting with Mallory-Weiss syndrome.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates potential efficacy of integrative treatment combining acupuncture-moxibustion with chiropractic manipulation for psychogenic vomiting in adolescents with concurrent Mallory-Weiss tears. The approach targeted governor vessel function and hepatic-gastric disharmony using acupuncture point selection based on thoracic spine positional findings. Chiropractors may consider collaborative referral patterns with acupuncture practitioners for complex cases of adolescent gastrointestinal complaints with psychological components.
papers.key_finding: A single adolescent patient with psychogenic vomiting, Mallory-Weiss syndrome, and antral gastritis showed improvement with combined acupuncture-moxibustion and chiropractic therapy targeting thoracic spine dysfunction and governor vessel circulation.

papers.title: Use of prescribed analgesics before and after a standardised chiropractic care programme among patients with lumbar spinal stenosis: a nationwide cohort study.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care reduced analgesic use in LSS patients, though pre-existing use predicted continued consumption.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors managing lumbar spinal stenosis should recognize that guideline-based non-pharmacological care can reduce analgesic use overall, but patients with pre-existing opioid or gabapentinoid use require targeted deprescribing strategies. Consider coordinating with GPs to address complexity factors (female sex, comorbidities) that predict continued analgesic reliance.
papers.key_finding: Analgesic use increased before enrollment, peaked during the chiropractic program, then declined post-program. However, 10% of users accounted for 43-68% of total analgesic consumption, and pre-existing use patterns predicted continued use after care completion.

papers.title: A survey of student loan burden among United States Chiropractors: Insights on debt, relief, and educational value.
papers.one_line: US chiropractors graduate with $176K debt but earn $99K annually, with 65% regretting career choice.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that recent graduates face substantial financial burden (median $240K debt vs. median $76K income) that may impact practice viability and well-being. Career counselors and educators should address the significant disconnect between educational costs and income potential, while practitioners may need to explore practice models that improve financial sustainability. Understanding these profession-wide challenges can help individual practitioners make informed decisions about debt management and practice development.
papers.key_finding: 85% of surveyed US chiropractors retained student loan debt averaging $232,062, while median gross annual income was only $76,000; 65% reported they would not choose a chiropractic career again, with 53.3% rating the financial ROI of chiropractic training as negative.

papers.title: Longer-term chiropractic care outcomes for US active-duty military personnel with low back pain: secondary analysis of a pragmatic clinical trial
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care shows sustained benefit for low back pain in active-duty military personnel.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This secondary analysis demonstrates that chiropractic intervention provides durable clinical outcomes for military service members with low back pain, supporting its use as a viable treatment option in military healthcare settings. Chiropractors can reference this pragmatic trial evidence when advocating for expanded access to chiropractic services within military medical systems.
papers.key_finding: The study examined longer-term outcomes of chiropractic care in active-duty military personnel with low back pain, suggesting sustained clinical benefit beyond initial treatment phases.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of pragmatic clinical trial

papers.title: MOTIVATIONS, TRAINING OUTCOMES, AND CLINICAL PRACTICE CHARACTERISTICS OF NORTH AMERICAN CHIROPRACTORS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL SURVEY
papers.one_line: North American chiropractors are purpose-driven with strong clinical reasoning and counseling skills but variable evidence-based imaging practices.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors' primary motivations are prosocial and meaning-oriented, with demonstrated competencies in clinical reasoning, patient communication, and lifestyle counseling. Practice patterns vary by philosophical orientation (subluxation belief): vitalistic practitioners use more manipulation while biomedically-aligned practitioners order fewer routine radiographs. Consider aligning recruitment, curricula, and continuing education messaging around evidence-based practice and imaging stewardship to leverage practitioners' existing strengths in patient-centered care.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors report strong prosocial motivations and perceive training outcomes strongest in clinical reasoning, communication, and counseling. Practice orientation significantly correlates with clinical behaviors: higher manipulation frequency in vitalistic practitioners (ρ=0.25) and lower routine new-patient radiography in biomedically-aligned practitioners (ρ=-0.31).

papers.title: Profession-Related Accreditation Requirements in Australia Regarding Anatomy Teaching: A Web-Based Desktop Audit
papers.one_line: Most Australian health professions lack specific anatomy curriculum accreditation requirements.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that chiropractic was among professions reviewed but found lacking explicit anatomy standards in Australian accreditation frameworks. This gap may impact training consistency and education quality across programs. Advocating for stronger anatomy-specific accreditation requirements could strengthen the profession's educational standards and clinical competency.
papers.key_finding: Only 6 of 20 Australian health professions had specific accreditation requirements for anatomy curriculum content and teaching; most relied on general learning outcome statements without detailed anatomy specifications.
papers.study_design: Web-based desktop audit with content analysis

papers.title: Pediatric vertebral artery dissection and ischemic stroke following chiropractic manipulation.
papers.one_line: Cervical chiropractic manipulation in toddlers can cause vertebral artery dissection and stroke.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must exercise extreme caution with cervical manipulation in pediatric patients, particularly infants and toddlers, due to risk of vertebral artery dissection. Practitioners should obtain thorough informed consent from guardians regarding rare but serious neurological complications and be prepared to recognize non-specific presentations (lethargy, vomiting, respiratory distress) as potential warning signs requiring emergency evaluation.
papers.key_finding: A 20-month-old male developed vertebral artery dissection with non-specific acute symptoms (lethargy, vomiting, cyanosis, respiratory distress) immediately following cervical chiropractic manipulation, though the patient recovered without neurological deficit.

papers.title: Assessing the importance and feasibility of quality measures for chiropractic care: a national survey of U.S. chiropractors
papers.one_line: U.S. chiropractors identify which quality measures are important and feasible to implement.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This survey provides insight into quality metrics that practicing chiropractors view as both clinically important and practically implementable in their settings. Chiropractors can use these findings to prioritize quality improvement initiatives that align with profession-wide consensus on measurement feasibility and clinical value.
papers.key_finding: The study assessed chiropractor perspectives on the importance and implementation feasibility of proposed quality measures for chiropractic practice through national survey methodology.

papers.title: Estimating Lumbar Spine Foraminal Disc Measurements Using Ultrasound and X-Ray Imaging Through Advanced Image Annotation, Processing, and Mathematical Modeling During Chiropractic Traction Procedures: A Feasibility Study
papers.one_line: Novel image processing methodology aligns X-ray and ultrasound spinal measurements during traction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This feasibility study demonstrates a standardized approach to combining X-ray and ultrasound imaging for real-time assessment of lumbar spine changes during traction, potentially improving diagnostic accuracy. Chiropractors could use this methodology to objectively document spinal decompression responses and track patient progress during traction therapy, supporting more evidence-based treatment protocols.
papers.key_finding: Progressive traction forces (1.8–11.3 kg) produced consistent increases in spinal metrics (height and area) at L3-L4, L4-L5, and L5-S1 levels, demonstrating that integrated X-ray and ultrasound imaging with geometric scaling can quantify real-time spinal elongation during chiropractic traction.

papers.title: Cervical spinal manipulative therapy, arterial dissection, and the law: Informed consent and causation in Goldie C.arsenault
papers.one_line: Canadian court found chiropractor liable for cervical dissection/stroke despite uncertain causation and inadequate informed consent.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must provide comprehensive informed consent documenting rare but serious risks of cervical manipulation, including arterial dissection and stroke. Consider screening for arterial disease risk factors and latent susceptibilities before cervical manipulation, and document clinical reasoning for treatment decisions, as courts may weigh individual clinical opinion heavily in liability cases.
papers.key_finding: The trial court found the chiropractor liable despite causation remaining scientifically uncertain; the court minimized informed consent disclosure adequacy and applied a binary causation model (traumatic vs. spontaneous) rather than considering interaction between latent arterial vulnerability and treatment as trigger.
papers.study_design: Case law review and legal analysis

papers.title: Spinal Manipulative Therapy on a Healthy Population: Protocol for a Randomized Blinding Feasibility Trial
papers.one_line: RCT protocol evaluating a novel chiropractic sham maneuver's blinding success in healthy participants.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This feasibility study is developing validated sham procedures critical for rigorous chiropractic research. The successful creation of a credible sham HVLA technique will enable future high-quality trials to better isolate specific effects of spinal manipulation. Results will strengthen the evidence base for chiropractic interventions by improving study methodology.
papers.key_finding: Study aims to validate a novel full-spine HVLA sham maneuver and assess blinding integrity using Bang and James Blinding Indices. Secondary outcomes include measuring differential effects on gait parameters between genuine and sham SMT.

papers.title: The 2023 patient profile and clinical management characteristics at a South African chiropractic training clinic: a descriptive cross-sectional study
papers.one_line: Describes patient demographics and clinical management patterns at a South African chiropractic teaching clinic.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study provides data on typical patient presentations and treatment approaches in a chiropractic teaching environment. Understanding regional patient profiles and management characteristics can inform practice standards and educational curriculum development.
papers.key_finding: The study characterizes the patient population and clinical management practices at a South African chiropractic training clinic, offering insights into real-world clinical patterns in that setting.

papers.title: Rehabilitation effects of combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment on adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.one_line: Combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment improves scoliosis outcomes in adolescents.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Adding structured respiratory guidance to chiropractic adjustment significantly enhances treatment efficacy in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, with 96.7% effectiveness rate versus 80.9% for adjustment alone. Clinicians should consider incorporating breathing techniques to optimize Cobb angle reduction, pain relief, and functional outcomes like exercise tolerance and quality of life improvements.
papers.key_finding: The combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment group achieved a 96.72% effective rate compared to 80.85% in the conventional adjustment-only group (P=0.017), with superior improvements in Cobb angle, lumbar strength, pain scores, and functional capacity.

papers.title: Nationwide Online Stress Survey of 100,000 People in Japan
papers.one_line: Chiropractic massage identified as common stress-coping strategy in high-stress populations.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can position themselves as stress-management providers, particularly for male patients in high-stress situations. The study validates that patients already self-select massage/chiropractic care as a coping mechanism, suggesting chiropractors should integrate stress education and relaxation into their clinical protocols, especially for those with sleep deprivation and high work demands.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic/massage therapy was the most commonly reported stress-coping method for men in the high-stress group; high stress was associated with short sleep duration, long working hours, and low household income.

papers.title: Recruiting US veterans with chronic low back pain in a multisite randomized pragmatic trial.
papers.one_line: Existing referrals most efficiently recruited Veterans with chronic low back pain for chiropractic trial.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors working in VA or similar integrated care settings should leverage existing referral networks as the primary recruitment strategy, as it proved most efficient (23-day median enrollment) and effectively reached racial/ethnic minorities. Combining recruitment methods—particularly adding email to postal mail—significantly accelerates engagement (16 vs. 30 days), and virtual baseline visits can overcome clinic capacity constraints while maintaining recruitment momentum.
papers.key_finding: Among 3,667 screened veterans, existing referrals accounted for 91% of identified candidates with the shortest enrollment timeline (23 days), while EHR prescreening identified the most female veterans (79%) and email invitations reduced response time by 47% compared to postal-only contact.
papers.study_design: Pragmatic randomized controlled trial (recruitment methods comparison)

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management addresses back pain multidimensionally.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrating spinal manipulation with patient education on psychological and social factors may improve back pain outcomes. Chiropractors should counsel patients on lifestyle, stress management, and self-efficacy alongside manual therapy.
papers.key_finding: Unable to determine without abstract; title suggests combining spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial approaches to back pain management.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain-Reply
papers.one_line: Response commentary on spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management approaches for back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This appears to be a reply/correspondence piece addressing integration of spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial self-management strategies. Chiropractors should consider how manual therapy can be effectively combined with patient education and lifestyle modification to optimize back pain outcomes.
papers.key_finding: The paper likely discusses the benefits of integrating spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial approaches rather than relying on manipulation alone for back pain management.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management addresses back pain multidimensionally.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrating biopsychosocial self-management strategies with spinal manipulation may enhance back pain outcomes by addressing psychological and behavioral factors alongside biomechanical interventions. This approach aligns with current evidence supporting multimodal treatment for chronic back pain.
papers.key_finding: Unable to determine primary findings without access to abstract or full text.

papers.title: Spinal Manipulation and Biopsychosocial Self-Management for Back Pain
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation combined with biopsychosocial self-management improves back pain outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Integrating biopsychosocial self-management strategies with spinal manipulation may enhance treatment efficacy for back pain patients. Chiropractors should consider addressing psychological and social factors alongside manual therapy to optimize clinical outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Combining spinal manipulation with biopsychosocial self-management approaches appears beneficial for back pain management; however, specific findings cannot be detailed without access to the abstract.

papers.title: Research Waste in Randomised Control Trials of Spinal Manipulative Therapy for Chronic Low Back Pain: Evidence From Trial Sequential Analysis.
papers.one_line: SMT RCTs for chronic low back pain reached evidence sufficiency by 2002-2004; subsequent trials constitute research waste.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Existing evidence adequately supports SMT efficacy for chronic low back pain versus conservative treatments, so practitioners can confidently recommend it. Future research should focus on novel questions (e.g., patient selection, optimal dosing, mechanism clarification) rather than repeating efficacy comparisons. This validates SMT's role in clinical guidelines while redirecting research resources toward unanswered clinical questions.
papers.key_finding: Trial Sequential Analysis of 60 RCTs (N=10,312) showed that futility and information size boundaries for SMT versus conservative treatment were crossed by 2002-2004 for both pain and functional status outcomes; RCTs conducted after these dates have not advanced our understanding and constitute research waste.
papers.study_design: Trial Sequential Analysis of RCTs from Cochrane systematic review

papers.title: Physiological changes of cortisol and oxytocin following manual therapy: a scoping review
papers.one_line: Manual therapy produces variable cortisol and oxytocin responses; standardization needed.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While manual therapy may influence stress-related hormones (cortisol) and social bonding hormones (oxytocin), current evidence is too heterogeneous to definitively link these changes to clinical outcomes. Chiropractors should view hormonal mechanisms as plausible but unproven, and focus on establishing consistent measurement protocols to better understand how MT effects relate to patient outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Of 72 eligible studies examining cortisol and/or oxytocin responses to manual therapy, findings were mixed and highly variable. Heterogeneity in intervention type, sample size, sampling methods, and timing prevented clear conclusions about neuroendocrine mechanisms underlying manual therapy effects.

papers.title: Spinal manipulative therapy promotes nucleus pulposus resorption and alleviates pain in a rat model of lumbar disc herniation via JNK-dependent regulation of inflammation and tissue remodeling
papers.one_line: SMT promotes disc herniation resorption and pain relief through JNK-dependent inflammatory modulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: SMT may facilitate spontaneous nucleus pulposus resorption in lumbar disc herniation by maintaining a balanced inflammatory microenvironment that supports tissue remodeling—distinct from broad anti-inflammatory suppression. This mechanistic insight supports SMT's clinical use for disc herniation and suggests timing and frequency may optimize outcomes by allowing natural resolution processes to proceed.
papers.key_finding: SMT significantly reduced mechanical allodynia from day 3 onward and achieved near-complete NP resorption by day 28, outperforming epidural betamethasone. All SMT benefits were abolished in JNK2-knockout mice, establishing JNK as an essential mediator of SMT's therapeutic effects.

papers.title: Adverse events among older adults receiving chiropractic spinal manipulation and related treatments: an updated systematic review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic treatment in older adults causes mostly mild-to-moderate adverse events with no catastrophic outcomes reported.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can counsel older adults that adverse events from spinal manipulation are typically mild-to-moderate (soreness, stiffness, headache, dizziness), with no catastrophic events documented. Soft tissue techniques, exercise, and other modalities showed no reported adverse events in this review, offering potentially safer alternatives for selected older patients. Standardizing adverse event definitions and tracking protocols would improve safety monitoring in future practice and research.
papers.key_finding: Of 412 reported adverse events in older adults receiving chiropractic care across 25 included studies, 9 were severe and none were catastrophic; most were mild-to-moderate symptoms like muscle soreness, stiffness, and headache. Six severe adverse events (4 vascular) were reported only in case reports involving spinal manipulation, while no adverse events were documented following soft tissue techniques, exercise, or other modalities.

papers.title: Effects of Spinal Manipulation and Dry Needling on Headache and Migraine: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.one_line: Systematic review examining spinal manipulation and dry needling efficacy for headache and migraine management.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Both spinal manipulation and dry needling show promise as adjunctive or primary treatments for tension-type headache and migraine. Chiropractors should consider these evidence-based techniques as part of comprehensive headache management protocols, particularly when traditional approaches are ineffective or poorly tolerated.
papers.key_finding: The review synthesizes RCT evidence comparing spinal manipulation and dry needling interventions for headache and migraine outcomes across multiple studies.
papers.study_design: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials

papers.title: One Spinal Manipulation Session Does Not Affect Static, Quasi-Static and Dynamic Balance or Pressure Pain Threshold in Individuals With Chronic Low Back Pain: A Randomized Clinical Controlled Trial
papers.one_line: Single spinal manipulation session fails to improve balance or pain threshold in chronic low back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: A single manipulation session does not produce measurable improvements in balance or pressure pain thresholds in chronic low back pain patients. Multiple sessions or alternative/combined treatment approaches may be necessary to achieve clinical benefits. Consider setting realistic patient expectations about single-session efficacy.
papers.key_finding: One session of global spinal manipulation targeting thoracolumbar and lumbopelvic regions produced no significant changes in static, quasi-static, or dynamic balance measurements (SOT, SEBT) or pressure pain threshold compared to placebo, with effects unchanged at 24-hour and 1-week follow-ups.

papers.title: Neck proprioception and mobility improved after upper neck and spine treatment: a randomized controlled trial
papers.one_line: Upper neck manipulation improves cervical proprioception and mobility in symptomatic patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The One-to-Zero system, targeting the C0-C1 joint complex before addressing other spinal dysfunctions, significantly improves cervical kinesthesia and neck range of motion within 2-6 weeks. This treatment approach may normalize proprioceptive feedback and reduce neck pain and disability, supporting its use in clinical chiropractic practice for patients with neck dysfunction.
papers.key_finding: Treatment group showed significant improvements in head-to-target repositioning accuracy at 50% maximum rotation, neck range of motion, and reduced pain/disability compared to control. Improvements in cervical kinesthesia correlated with enhanced neck mobility, suggesting normalized proprioceptive afferent feedback.

papers.title: Verbal framing, rather than measured cognitive-affective variables, is associated with short-term outcomes after spinal manipulation: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
papers.one_line: Pre-treatment verbal framing predicts short-term outcomes after spinal manipulation better than patient expectations.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The words and tone used immediately before spinal manipulation significantly influence short-term pain outcomes, independent of patient expectations or attitudes. Chiropractors should focus on optimizing pre-treatment verbal communication as a modifiable factor to enhance treatment responses. Generic positive framing may be more clinically effective than relying on patients' pre-existing beliefs or expectation fulfillment.
papers.key_finding: Verbal framing (positive, neutral, or negative) was the primary predictor of short-term pain intensity and pressure pain threshold changes, while pre-treatment expectations, attitudes toward manual therapy, and expectation fulfillment showed sparse and inconsistent associations with outcomes.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial

papers.title: Clinical features of manual therapy interventions in people with tension-type headache: A scoping review.
papers.one_line: Manual therapy for tension-type headache shows wide variability in techniques, dosage, and outcomes across 33 RCTs.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Cervical and suboccipital structures are commonly targeted in manual therapy for tension-type headache, but protocols vary significantly. Chiropractors should consider mechanism-informed approaches and standardize their intervention documentation. Future practice should incorporate individualized assessment of temporomandibular and postural components alongside traditional cervical techniques.
papers.key_finding: Thirty-three RCTs involving 1852 participants demonstrated considerable heterogeneity in manual therapy techniques (spinal manipulation, myofascial release, suboccipital inhibition, friction massage), treatment dosage, target structures, and outcome measures, with limited mechanistic rationale provided.

papers.title: The Effect of Joint Mobilization and Manipulation on Proprioception: Systematic Review with Limited Meta-Analysis
papers.one_line: Joint mobilization and manipulation may improve proprioception through mechanoreceptor stimulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Mobilization and manipulation techniques can enhance proprioceptive function, potentially improving patient balance and movement control. This mechanistic benefit may contribute to improved outcomes in rehabilitation and injury prevention protocols.
papers.key_finding: Joint mobilization and manipulation appear to stimulate mechanoreceptors and improve proprioceptive feedback, though the magnitude and clinical significance vary across studies.

papers.title: Chiropractic Management of Adults with Cervicogenic or Tension-Type Headaches: Development of a Clinical Practice Guideline
papers.one_line: Evidence-based guideline supports spinal manipulation for cervicogenic headache and multimodal care for tension-type headache.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can confidently use spinal manipulation as a primary intervention for cervicogenic headache (CGH). For tension-type headache (TTH), spinal manipulation should be combined with other modalities rather than used alone. Practitioners should screen for red flags during history and examination, and consider referral when appropriate.
papers.key_finding: Spinal manipulation is recommended for cervicogenic headache management; for tension-type headache, it should be used only as part of multimodal care. Evidence was insufficient to strongly recommend acupuncture, education, meditation, or isolated modalities for either condition.
papers.study_design: Umbrella review with Delphi consensus guideline development

papers.title: Effects of segmental spinal manipulation on adolescent scoliosis based on electromyography parameters
papers.one_line: Segmental spinal manipulation reduces Cobb angle and alters paraspinal muscle EMG recruitment in adolescent scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Segmental spinal manipulation may help reduce spinal curvature (Cobb angle) in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis by modifying paraspinal muscle recruitment patterns across multiple positions. While the technique effectively adjusts EMG signal characteristics, clinicians should note it does not necessarily increase muscle strength, suggesting its benefit is through biomechanical correction rather than muscular strengthening.
papers.key_finding: Segmental spinal manipulation significantly increased paraspinal muscle Turns (EMG signal parameter) on the convex side in multiple positions and effectively reduced Cobb angle compared to ordinary massage, though without improving paraspinal muscle strength metrics.

papers.title: Mechano responsiveness of neuroimmune cross-talk in bone and joints: A narrative review with implications for force-based manipulations
papers.one_line: Neuroimmune system regulates bone health; force-based manipulations may modulate these responses.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation and manual therapy may influence bone health through neuroimmune pathways, though direct evidence is limited. Clinicians should personalize interventions considering patient age, hormonal status, and comorbidities, as these significantly affect neuroimmune responses and bone remodeling.
papers.key_finding: While physical activity strongly influences bone-related neuroimmune responses, force-based manipulations show early promise in modulating these responses, but robust evidence for direct bone changes from manipulation is sparse.

papers.title: Complications of Chiropractic Manipulation in a Patient With Von Willebrand Disease: A Clinical Case Report and Literature Review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic manipulation caused severe iliopsoas hematoma with femoral neuropathy in VWD patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must screen patients for bleeding disorders before manipulation, particularly Von Willebrand disease, which significantly increases hemorrhage risk. Even seemingly minor manipulative techniques can trigger life-threatening or permanently disabling bleeding complications in coagulopathic patients. Consider referral to appropriate medical specialists when coagulopathy is suspected or confirmed.
papers.key_finding: A 32-year-old female with Von Willebrand disease developed a massive 896 cc iliopsoas hematoma with femoral nerve compression after chiropractic spinal manipulation, resulting in persistent residual neuropathy and muscle atrophy despite multidisciplinary intervention.

papers.title: Angular Kinematic Analysis of Supine Cervical Thrusts Performed by Chiropractors and Chiropractic Students on Mannequins
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors produce peak cervical rotation of ~34° during supine thrusts with consistent kinematic parameters.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Peak axial rotation during cervical adjustments reaches approximately 34°, which is below physiological limits and supports safe practice parameters. These quantified kinematic values (velocity ~193°/s, acceleration ~4427°/s²) provide objective benchmarks for teaching and evaluating thrust technique quality among students and practitioners.
papers.key_finding: Experienced DCs achieved mean peak cervical rotation of 33.9° with 14.6° of rotation occurring in 144 milliseconds, demonstrating consistent, measurable thrust mechanics that were similar to previously published data.

papers.title: Kinematic Assessment of Hip, Shoulder, and Elbow Movements of a Chiropractor Performing Side Posture Adjustments: Results From a Biomechanical Analysis.
papers.one_line: Side-posture adjustment biomechanics show repeatable movement patterns with body-drop force generation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Effective side-posture adjustments rely on coordinated hip, shoulder, and elbow kinematics with force generated from body drop rather than upper extremity effort alone. The asymmetrical positioning of shoulders and hips reflects their distinct stabilization and thrust roles. Practitioners should focus on consistent body mechanics and positioning rather than variable angular magnitudes to maintain adjustment efficacy.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors demonstrate repeatable thrust patterns with consistent positional angles across trials, though angular magnitudes vary. Force delivery occurs primarily through body drop (minimal elbow extension) with asymmetrical hip and shoulder positioning reflecting different functional roles.

papers.title: CT-guided Foramen Ovale Injection of Mesenchymal Stem Cells: First Human Case Report of Trigeminal Neuralgia Relief
papers.one_line: MSC injection at foramen ovale reduced trigeminal neuralgia pain without adverse effects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case suggests MSC injection may offer pain relief for refractory trigeminal neuralgia when conservative and surgical approaches have failed. Chiropractors should be aware this emerging intervention exists for patient referral; however, it remains investigational and requires specialized pain management expertise. Consider recommending appropriate specialist evaluation for patients with severe, medication-resistant trigeminal neuralgia.
papers.key_finding: A 48-year-old woman with 22-year history of severe trigeminal neuralgia experienced dramatic pain reduction and eliminated medication-related cognitive side effects at 1 month post-injection, with sustained improvement at 12 months despite some symptom recurrence.

papers.title: The effects of chiropractic adjustment on inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a pilot RCT.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment showed no significant advantage over sham for pediatric ADHD symptoms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this pilot RCT demonstrated feasibility of studying chiropractic care in ADHD, both active and sham groups improved equally, suggesting any benefit may be attributable to usual care or placebo effect rather than specific chiropractic intervention. Chiropractors should exercise caution in marketing spinal manipulation as a primary ADHD treatment until larger, adequately powered trials demonstrate specific efficacy.
papers.key_finding: Both chiropractic adjustment plus usual care and sham adjustment plus usual care groups showed significant improvements in ADHD symptoms at 4 and 8 weeks, with no statistically significant between-group differences.

papers.title: Myositis Ossificans Traumatica of Bilateral Sternocleidomastoid Muscles After Chiropractor Adjustment: A Case Report
papers.one_line: Chiropractic neck adjustment associated with rare myositis ossificans in young woman.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Myositis ossificans is a rare but serious complication that can occur following cervical manipulation, presenting with progressive pain, trismus, and restricted mobility. Chiropractors should maintain heightened awareness of this potential adverse event and consider it in the differential diagnosis of post-adjustment complications. Appropriate imaging and specialist referral are essential when myositis ossificans is suspected.
papers.key_finding: A woman in her 20s developed myositis ossificans affecting bilateral sternocleidomastoid muscles following chiropractic neck adjustment, manifesting as persistent shoulder pain, trismus, and heterotopic bone formation on imaging.

papers.title: Vertebral Subluxation and Systems Biology: An Integrative Review Exploring the Salutogenic Influence of Chiropractic Care on the Neuroendocrine-Immune System
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care may modulate neuroendocrine-immune function through multiple neural pathways.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This review suggests chiropractic adjustment may influence systemic health markers (blood pressure, heart rate variability, sleep) beyond musculoskeletal effects through neuroimmune pathways. Practitioners can frame care within a systems biology perspective and monitor these broader health indicators. Future research should focus on identifying specific neural mechanisms underlying these systemic effects.
papers.key_finding: Evidence supports biological plausibility that chiropractic adjustment influences neuroendocrine-immune function through multiple neurologically-mediated pathways, with documented improvements in blood pressure, heart rate variability, and sleep quality beyond neuromusculoskeletal outcomes.

papers.title: A Case Report of U-Type Sacral Fracture After Chiropractic Adjustment.
papers.one_line: Drop-table chiropractic manipulation caused U-type sacral fracture in elderly patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Drop-table techniques carry risk of severe spinopelvic dissociation injuries, particularly in older patients. Practitioners should exercise extreme caution with high-velocity, low-amplitude manipulations in the sacral region and maintain high suspicion for serious complications when patients report severe pain post-manipulation. Prompt imaging and specialist consultation are critical to avoid delayed diagnosis and complications.
papers.key_finding: A 74-year-old male sustained a U-type sacral fracture (spinopelvic dissociation) following drop-table chiropractic manipulation, a previously unreported complication. Despite diagnostic delay and prolonged hospitalization, conservative management resulted in functional recovery with mild residual neuropathy at one year.

papers.title: Absence of Neuroplastic Changes in the Bilateral H-Reflex Amplitude following Spinal Manipulation with Activator IV.
papers.one_line: Activator IV spinal manipulation does not alter bilateral H-reflex amplitude.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study suggests that instrument-assisted spinal manipulation (Activator IV) does not produce measurable changes in spinal reflex excitability as assessed by H-reflex testing. Chiropractors using Activator devices should not rely on neuroplastic changes in reflex pathways as a mechanism of action for this technique.
papers.key_finding: Spinal manipulation with the Activator IV instrument produced no significant changes in bilateral H-reflex amplitude, suggesting the absence of neuroplastic effects on spinal motor neuron excitability from this intervention.

papers.title: Acute Lumbar Schmorl's Node Following Chiropractic Adjustment
papers.one_line: Acute Schmorl's node developed after chiropractic adjustment but resolved with conservative care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that spinal manipulation can rarely precipitate acute Schmorl's node formation. However, this complication may not require intervention beyond conservative management, with significant pain relief achievable without surgical intervention. Document baseline imaging in at-risk patients and monitor post-treatment symptoms closely.
papers.key_finding: A 41-year-old male developed an acute Schmorl's node at L4-L5 following chiropractic adjustment, which was successfully managed conservatively with 85% pain relief.

papers.title: Management of people with low back pain: a survey of opinions and beliefs of Dutch and Belgian chiropractors
papers.one_line: Dutch and Belgian chiropractors show 64.5% guideline adherence for LBP management, with gaps in return-to-work and activity advice.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should strengthen adherence to evidence-based guidelines, particularly for acute LBP cases and return-to-work counseling. While most practitioners appropriately advise against bedrest, only 60% counsel on timely return-to-work and 78% emphasize staying active—areas requiring improvement to align with international guidelines.
papers.key_finding: Overall guideline adherence was 64.5%, with better adherence in chronic cases (73.4%) than acute cases (55.9%). Chiropractors excelled at recommending against bedrest (98.5%) but performed poorly on return-to-work advice (59.4%) and activity encouragement (77.5%).

papers.title: Chiropractic Spinal Manipulation Prevents Secondary Hyperalgesia Induced by Topical Capsaicin in Healthy Individuals
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation prevents secondary hyperalgesia development from capsaicin-induced pain sensitization.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation may modulate central pain processing mechanisms and prevent widespread pain sensitization. This suggests manipulation could have preventive or therapeutic value for patients at risk of developing chronic pain states characterized by central sensitization.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic spinal manipulation prevented the development of secondary hyperalgesia that typically occurs after topical capsaicin application, suggesting a role in modulating nociceptive processing.

papers.title: The prevalence of complementary and alternative medicine use among Turkish patients with primary headache.
papers.one_line: One-third of Turkish headache patients use CAM, with longer disease duration as key predictor.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that 33% of primary headache patients in this Turkish population use CAM, and chiropractic adjustment was used by 17.5% of CAM users. Patients with longer disease duration are more likely to seek CAM approaches, suggesting they may present to chiropractic offices after unsuccessful conventional treatment. Cupping showed higher patient-reported benefit than other modalities, indicating multimodal approaches may be valued by this patient population.
papers.key_finding: CAM use was reported in 33.3% of primary headache patients, with phytotherapy (37.5%), cupping (27.5%), and chiropractic adjustment (17.5%) being most common. Longer disease duration was the only significant predictor of CAM use, with CAM users having mean disease duration of 10.97 years versus 5.68 years for non-users.

papers.title: Resolution of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Following Correction for Upper Cross Syndrome-A Case Study and Brief Review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic treatment of upper cross syndrome resolved concurrent GERD symptoms in one patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider screening patients with GERD for upper cross syndrome and postural dysfunction, as correcting cervical and thoracic alignment through adjustment and soft tissue therapy may improve reflux symptoms. This case suggests postural correction and regular spinal maintenance may prevent secondary conditions associated with poor posture from prolonged desk work.
papers.key_finding: A 35-year-old female with neck/upper back pain and GERD experienced full resolution of both conditions following cervical adjustment, soft tissue massage, and postural correction, with sustained improvement at 12-month follow-up.

papers.title: Chiropractic Day: A Historical Review of a Day Worth Celebrating.
papers.one_line: Historical review of Chiropractic Day celebration since Palmer's first adjustment in 1895.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic Day (September 18) commemorates the profession's founding and offers practitioners opportunities to engage with their communities through education, volunteering, and patient engagement. Celebrating this day reinforces professional identity and allows reflection on chiropractic's evolution and patient care contributions over 125+ years.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic Day has been celebrated since D.D. Palmer's first adjustment on September 18, 1895, evolving through multiple names and formats to remain a significant professional milestone that encourages community engagement and professional reflection.

papers.title: The effect of sacroiliac chiropractic adjustments on innominate angles.
papers.one_line: Sacroiliac adjustments produce measurable changes in innominate bone angles toward correct alignment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments can objectively correct innominate bone angles and pelvic alignment, as measured by the PALM PALpation Meter. This provides objective evidence that SIJ-specific adjustments produce measurable biomechanical changes, supporting their use in sacroiliac dysfunction management.
papers.key_finding: Specific chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments resulted in measurable changes in innominate bone angles, with the pelvis tilting toward correct anatomical alignment, compared to sham ultrasound control.

papers.title: Changes in radiographic parameters following chiropractic treatment in 10 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A retrospective chart review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment reduced Cobb angles 21.2% in 10 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This small retrospective study suggests chiropractic care may reduce scoliotic curves (average 6.3° reduction) in adolescents with mild-moderate AIS, particularly for stabilizing progression. However, the lack of control group, small sample size, and retrospective design limit clinical conclusions. Further prospective RCTs with controls are needed before changing standard AIS management protocols.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic treatment reduced mean Cobb angle from 29.7° to 23.4° (21.2% average correction) in 10 AIS patients; 64% showed morphological improvement and 36% showed stabilization.

papers.title: Characterization of Horse Use in Therapeutic Horseback Riding Programs in the United States: A Pilot Survey
papers.one_line: THR horses experience moderate workloads with limb lameness and back soreness as primary health concerns.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that therapeutic riding horses commonly present with back soreness and lameness issues, making them potential candidates for chiropractic care alongside other complementary therapies. The survey shows chiropractic adjustment is already a widely used complementary therapy in THR programs, supporting its integration into equine therapeutic protocols. Familiarity with THR program management and horse welfare standards may help chiropractors better serve this specialized equine population.
papers.key_finding: Therapeutic riding horses were worked moderately (4 days/week, 2 hours/day), below PATH International maximum recommendations, with limb lameness and back soreness as the most common health issues. Chiropractic adjustment was among the most frequently used complementary therapies in these programs.

papers.title: Measurement and Analysis of Biomechanical Outcomes of Chiropractic Adjustment Performance in Chiropractic Education and Practice
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors deliver McTimoney adjustments faster with greater consistency than students.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Proficiency in chiropractic technique development correlates with reduced thrust times and improved consistency, particularly in time-to-peak-force metrics. Tracking biomechanical parameters like thrust duration and peak force variability during training may objectively assess skill progression. Dominant hand preference produces higher peak forces, suggesting technique optimization should account for laterality.
papers.key_finding: Experienced DCs demonstrated significantly faster time-to-peak-force (70 ms vs 230 ms in Y3 students, P=0.03), shorter thrust duration (118 ms vs 284 ms, P=0.03), and less variability in thrust delivery compared to novice students. Year-5 students showed performance similar to experienced practitioners, indicating skill development during training.

papers.title: Traumatic spinal injuries: A retrospective epidemiological analysis following the 2018 driving policy reform in Saudi Arabia.
papers.one_line: Traumatic spinal injury epidemiology shifted post-2018 Saudi driving reform; lumbar injuries predominate with mostly intact neurological status.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Most traumatic spinal injuries present with intact neurological function (93.7%), emphasizing the importance of thorough baseline neurological assessment and early intervention to prevent deterioration. Female patients and those with prior psychiatric illness show prolonged recovery; consider individualized rehabilitation protocols and mental health support. Traffic safety enforcement and prevention programs targeting four-wheel motor vehicle accidents (57.6% of cases) represent key opportunities for reducing spinal injury burden.
papers.key_finding: Lumbar region was most commonly injured (53.9%) with 93.7% of patients neurologically intact (AIS E). Female sex, older age, prior psychiatric illness, and higher AIS severity were independent predictors of longer hospital stays and increased surgical need.

papers.title: Management of Cervical lateral mass fractures - A systematic review
papers.one_line: Floating lateral mass fractures require surgical management due to inherent spinal instability.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Floating lateral mass fractures are severe cervical injuries that commonly present with neurologic or vascular complications and typically require surgical intervention rather than conservative care. Chiropractors should recognize these fractures as contraindications to manipulation and refer immediately for surgical evaluation. Non-operative treatment with cervical collars carries significant risk of late subluxation (31% in reviewed cases).
papers.key_finding: Of 332 patients with floating lateral mass fractures, surgical management (particularly ACDF) was preferred over non-operative treatment; 31% of conservatively managed patients developed vertebral subluxation, while post-operative subluxation was minimal.

papers.title: Animal Chiropractic: A Basic Description and Its Importance in Veterinary Practice
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic improves function and recovery through neuromotor modulation in veterinary patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Animal chiropractic, when applied by properly trained licensed professionals, can enhance patient strength, stability, and mobility while improving postoperative recovery and performance. Chiropractors should consider pursuing additional training and credentialing in animal chiropractic to expand their clinical scope and potentially collaborate with veterinary practices. Integration of AC with conventional veterinary care may optimize patient outcomes for companion and performance animals.
papers.key_finding: Properly applied animal chiropractic can safely improve afferent input and modulate ventral horn motor neurons, enhancing patient strength, stability, mobility, conditioning, and postoperative recovery when delivered by trained, licensed professionals.

papers.title: Sublaminar stabilization (stapling) of the caudal cervical instability in Yorkshire terrier-A case report
papers.one_line: Sublaminar stapling stabilization successfully treated C6-C7 instability in a small dog long-term.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this case involves veterinary medicine, the sublaminar stapling technique demonstrates a surgical approach to cervical instability that may inform understanding of non-fusion stabilization methods. Chiropractors should recognize severe cases of vertebral subluxation with neurological deficits require surgical evaluation and may not respond to conservative care alone.
papers.key_finding: A Yorkshire terrier with C6-C7 instability refractory to 20 months of conservative treatment achieved long-term ambulation and functional recovery (5-year follow-up) using sublaminar polyamide stabilization after an initial surgical revision.

papers.title: Atlas Subluxation Complex, National Upper Cervical Chiropractic Association Intervention, and Dizziness Improvement: A Narrative Review of Historical Perspectives, Literature Synthesis, and a Path for Future Care.
papers.one_line: NUCCA intervention may address dizziness through atlas subluxation correction, but high-quality evidence is lacking.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider atlas subluxation as a potential etiological factor in dizziness cases, particularly when other causes have been ruled out. NUCCA-based upper cervical care may offer therapeutic benefit for select dizziness patients, though practitioners should counsel patients that evidence quality remains limited. Future RCTs are needed to establish efficacy more definitively.
papers.key_finding: Conceptual evidence and case reports suggest atlas subluxation complex may contribute to dizziness and NUCCA care may produce favorable outcomes, but high-quality RCTs are absent and warrant future investigation.

papers.title: Catastrophic failure of anterior fusion for bilateral cervical facet dislocation: illustrative case
papers.one_line: Anterior-alone fusion fails in bilateral cervical facet dislocation; combined anterior-posterior approach recommended.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize bilateral cervical facet dislocation as a surgical emergency requiring immediate physician referral. Understanding that anterior-only fusion carries significant failure risk in cases with posterior ligamentous damage, older patients, or associated fractures helps guide appropriate triage and communication with surgical colleagues. Document red flags (mechanism of injury, neurological signs, imaging findings) to support urgent referral.
papers.key_finding: Anterior-alone fusion failed in a bilateral cervical facet dislocation case, resulting in recurrent subluxation and spinal cord injury. Risk factors for failure include advanced age, bilateral facet injury, extensive posterior ligamentous damage, and associated fractures.

papers.title: The Dark Side of Musculoskeletal Care: Why Do Ineffective Techniques Seem to Work? A Comprehensive Review of Complementary and Alternative Therapies.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic and osteopathy lack robust evidence; observed benefits may primarily reflect placebo effects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This critical review questions the biological plausibility of vertebral subluxation theory and highlights methodological weaknesses in chiropractic efficacy studies. Practitioners should recognize that patient outcomes may be largely driven by contextual and psychological factors rather than specific technique effects, and should consider this when setting expectations and designing treatment protocols.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic care and osteopathy rely on concepts with limited empirical validation; observed clinical improvements appear substantially mediated by placebo responses involving contextual, psychological, and non-specific factors rather than the purported biological mechanisms.

papers.title: Vertebral Column Subluxation in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Associated Dystrophic Scoliosis: A Report of Two Cases and Narrative Review
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation in NF1-dystrophic scoliosis requires careful surgical management; halo-gravity traction carries significant complication risks.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis as a condition requiring surgical referral, particularly when subluxation is suspected. Halo-gravity traction in these patients carries serious risks including vascular and spinal cord injury, making conservative management via bracing alone typically unsuccessful. Early surgical consultation is essential for patients presenting with rapid progression, neurological symptoms, or imaging evidence of vertebral displacement.
papers.key_finding: Two cases of vertebral subluxation in NF1-dystrophic scoliosis were managed surgically; halo-gravity traction failed or caused complications (vascular injury) in both patients, while partial vertebral column resection with instrumentation achieved successful deformity correction and neurological improvement.

papers.title: The best preferable sagittal vertical axis for the ankylosis spondylitis with thoracolumbar kyphosis following one-level pedicle subtraction osteotomy under different cervical range of motion
papers.one_line: Optimal sagittal vertical axis outcomes vary with cervical mobility in ankylosing spondylitis osteotomy correction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Pedicle subtraction osteotomy for ankylosing spondylitis-related kyphosis requires individualized sagittal alignment goals based on patient cervical range of motion. Chiropractors should recognize that post-surgical cervical function may influence optimal spinal alignment targets. Consider referring AS patients with severe kyphosis for surgical evaluation when conservative care plateaus, particularly assessing cervical mobility preoperatively.
papers.key_finding: Optimal sagittal vertical axis positioning in ankylosing spondylitis patients undergoing pedicle subtraction osteotomy is dependent on baseline cervical range of motion, suggesting personalized alignment targets improve functional outcomes.
papers.study_design: Surgical outcomes analysis (likely retrospective cohort or case series)

papers.title: Secondary Analysis of a Dataset to Estimate the Prevalence of Vertebral Subluxation and Its Implications for Health Promotion and Prevention
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation prevalence estimated at 78.55% in chiropractic patients using operational definition.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study reports high prevalence of vertebral subluxation (78.55%) in patients seeking chiropractic care, supporting a role for chiropractic in health promotion and prevention. However, the study is limited by its retrospective nature, non-random sampling, and lack of comparison to asymptomatic populations, so results should be interpreted cautiously. The operational definition used warrants further validation in prospective, controlled studies.
papers.key_finding: Overall vertebral subluxation prevalence was 78.55% (95% CI 76.68-80.42) across 1,851 patient records from seven chiropractic clinics, with prevalence ≥50% across all age and gender-stratified subgroups.

papers.title: Associations between demographics and clinical ideology, beliefs, and practice patterns: a secondary analysis of a survey of randomly sampled United States chiropractors.
papers.one_line: US chiropractor ideology and practice vary significantly by education program, experience, and geographic region.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic practice patterns, beliefs about subluxation detection, vaccination attitudes, and scope of practice vary substantially based on where and when practitioners were trained. This variation may create inconsistency in patient care and complicate interprofessional collaboration; practitioners should be aware of evidence-based guidelines to ensure consistent, defensible clinical decision-making regardless of training background.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic degree program of graduation, years since graduation, and geographic region of practice are significantly associated with variations in clinical ideology, beliefs, and practice patterns across seven key practice domains including examination methods, health conditions treated, role in healthcare, attitudes toward chiropractic treatment for cancer, vaccination views, subluxation detection, and X-ray utilization.

papers.title: Spinal decompression and stabilisation in a cat with lumbar vertebral pathological fracture and subluxation, following discospondylitis and spinal epidural empyema
papers.one_line: Surgical decompression and stabilization successfully treated feline spinal infection with cord compression.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates that aggressive surgical intervention (hemilaminectomy with stabilization) may be warranted in severe spinal infections with neurological compromise that fail medical management. Although this is a veterinary case, the principles of spinal decompression and stabilization for infectious/inflammatory spinal pathology are relevant to understanding when conservative chiropractic care should be contraindicated.
papers.key_finding: A cat with discospondylitis, spinal epidural empyema, pathological fracture, and subluxation causing paraplegia was successfully treated with hemilaminectomy and PMMA stabilization, resulting in optimal outcome despite rapid neurological deterioration.

papers.title: Veterinary Spinal Manipulative Therapy or Animal Chiropractic in Veterinary Rehabilitation
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic is a receptor-based modality with diagnostic and therapeutic potential in veterinary rehabilitation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Veterinary chiropractors should understand the neuro-anatomical and biomechanical mechanisms of spinal manipulative therapy in animals, recognize appropriate indications and contraindications, and know when further diagnostics are needed before treatment. Animal chiropractic is increasingly integrated into multimodal veterinary rehabilitation protocols and requires evidence-based clinical decision-making.
papers.key_finding: Veterinary spinal manipulative therapy functions as a receptor-based modality with both diagnostic and therapeutic applications in animal rehabilitation, though practitioners must understand when further diagnostics supersede treatment.

papers.title: A novel Hinge-Link correction system for vertebral column resection: a pilot study in a porcine model.
papers.one_line: Novel Hinge-Link device enables safe, effective vertebral column resection with 94% scoliosis correction in animal model.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study demonstrates a new surgical device for severe scoliosis correction achieving 94% deformity correction without neurological complications in animal models. While not yet applicable to chiropractic practice, chiropractors should be aware of advances in surgical options for severe scoliosis cases requiring surgical referral. This technology may improve outcomes for patients with severe deformities who exhaust conservative management options.
papers.key_finding: The Hinge-Link system achieved 94% correction of surgically created scoliosis (from 32° to 1.8°) with no neurological deficits, dural impingement, or vertebral subluxation in any animal.

papers.title: Remodeling morphology of the subluxated osteotomy vertebra in closing-opening wedge osteotomy in ankylosing spondylitis: would the anterior bony beak blunt?
papers.one_line: Closing-opening wedge osteotomy in AS shows favorable bony remodeling but limited canal remodeling with subluxation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that while COWO in AS patients demonstrates favorable spontaneous remodeling of anterior bony beaks post-operatively, vertebral subluxation complications significantly impair spinal canal remodeling and sagittal alignment correction. This highlights the importance of careful patient selection and post-operative monitoring in AS cases with thoracolumbar kyphosis to identify and manage subluxation early.
papers.key_finding: After single-level lumbar COWO in AS patients, new bone formation and adaptive resorption of anterior bony beaks occurred favorably during 2+ year follow-up. However, patients who developed vertebral subluxation (ST ≥5mm) showed significantly impaired global kyphosis correction and limited spinal canal remodeling capacity.

papers.title: Use of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging to assess a case of spinal injury in a Showa koi Cyprinus carpio
papers.one_line: CT and MRI identified progressive spinal cord compression from vertebral subluxation in ornamental fish.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates advanced imaging utility in diagnosing spinal pathology across species. While directly applicable to fish medicine, the imaging protocols and spinal cord compression assessment principles parallel vertebral subluxation evaluation in chiropractic practice. The correlation between imaging findings and progressive neurological decline underscores the importance of comprehensive spinal assessment.
papers.key_finding: MRI revealed extensive vertebral centra alterations with multifocal spinal cord compression caused by vertebral subluxation, resulting in myelomalacia and progressive neurological decline leading to euthanasia.

papers.title: Posterior 3-Column Osteotomy for Treatment of Congenital Kyphosis with Multiple Thoracolumbar/Lumbar Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae: A Comparison Between Patients with Increasing Number of Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae
papers.one_line: Single-level posterior osteotomy shows reduced efficacy and increased complications in congenital kyphosis with ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors managing patients with congenital kyphosis should recognize that those with four or more anterior unsegmented vertebrae represent a more complex surgical case with higher complication rates and lower correction outcomes. Appropriate surgical referral and patient counseling regarding realistic correction expectations are essential when ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae are present. Conservative management may be preferred when possible, with surgical intervention reserved for symptomatic cases with clear indications.
papers.key_finding: Posterior 3-column osteotomy achieved satisfactory kyphosis correction in congenital kyphosis with 3 anterior unsegmented vertebrae (75% correction rate, 1/13 complications), but showed significantly worse outcomes with ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae (61.2% correction rate, 8/12 complications including vertebral subluxation and proximal junctional kyphosis).

papers.title: Evaluation of United States chiropractic professional subgroups: a survey of randomly sampled chiropractors.
papers.one_line: US chiropractors cluster into three distinct ideological subgroups with different practice beliefs.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The chiropractic profession comprises three distinct subgroups: spine/neuromusculoskeletal-focused (57%), primary care-focused (22%), and vertebral subluxation-focused (21%). Understanding which subgroup aligns with your practice philosophy can help clarify your clinical identity, referral patterns, and patient communication. This taxonomy may facilitate professional dialogue and identify opportunities for intra-professional collaboration or standards development.
papers.key_finding: Three distinct chiropractic subgroups self-identified based on their perceived role in healthcare: spine/neuromusculoskeletal-focused (56.8%), primary care-focused (22.0%), and vertebral subluxation-focused (21.2%), each with substantially different clinical practice beliefs and behaviors.

papers.title: The association between chiropractors' view of practice and patient encounter-level characteristics in Ontario, Canada: a cross-sectional study
papers.one_line: Chiropractors with unorthodox views treat non-musculoskeletal conditions and use subluxation diagnoses more frequently.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors holding traditional vertebral subluxation-based views are significantly more likely to diagnose subluxation and treat non-musculoskeletal conditions, with shorter encounter times. Understanding these practice philosophy differences may improve interprofessional referral patterns and patient communication about treatment scope.
papers.key_finding: Unorthodox-view chiropractors had 16.5 times higher odds of non-musculoskeletal presentations and 63 times higher odds of subluxation diagnosis, with 0.6-fold shorter encounter durations compared to orthodox-view practitioners.

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest - Week ending April 05, 2026
papers.one_line: Four key papers on pediatric manipulation risks, informed consent, CIH pain management, and SMT mechanisms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Avoid cervical manipulation in toddlers due to documented vertebral artery dissection risk; ensure comprehensive informed consent documentation for all cervical procedures. Combined practitioner-delivered and self-care therapies (yoga, mindfulness) enhance patient-reported outcomes in fatigue and mental health alongside chiropractic care.
papers.key_finding: Pediatric cervical manipulation carries serious stroke risk; cervical manipulation informed consent is legally critical; combined practitioner and self-care CIH yields equivalent pain relief with superior perceived global benefits.
papers.study_design: Mixed (case report, legal analysis, pragmatic trial, translational animal study)

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest - Week Ending April 12, 2026
papers.one_line: Pediatric cervical manipulation risks arterial dissection; combined respiratory guidance enhances scoliosis outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Exercise extreme caution with cervical manipulation in infants and toddlers due to vertebral artery dissection risk, with immediate emergency referral for acute presentations post-manipulation. Provide comprehensive informed consent documentation about arterial dissection risks and implement thorough pre-treatment screening for susceptibility factors. Integrate respiratory guidance with spinal adjustment protocols to improve adolescent idiopathic scoliosis outcomes (96.7% vs 80.9% effectiveness).
papers.key_finding: Pediatric cervical manipulation caused vertebral artery dissection in a 20-month-old with acute neurological symptoms; Canadian court found chiropractor liable for inadequate informed consent; combined respiratory guidance with adjustment achieved 96.7% effectiveness in adolescent scoliosis versus 80.9% conventional treatment.
papers.study_design: Mixed: case report, legal case analysis, retrospective cohort comparison

papers.title: CHIROPRACTIC RESEARCH DIGEST - 1 Week ending April 19, 2026
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care reduces analgesic use in lumbar stenosis; pediatric cervical manipulation poses vertebral artery dissection risk.

Coordinate care with primary care providers and identify high-risk patients (pre-existing opioid use, comorbidities) for targeted deprescribing support.
