But here's where it gets interesting: the evidence on what chiropractic *actually does* is increasingly specific and encouraging. A landmark Cochrane review confirms spinal manipulation works for chronic low back pain—modest effect versus sham, but meaningful edge over doing nothing. More compelling, perhaps, is the mechanistic work: animal models show SMT genuinely accelerates nucleus pulposus resorption in disc herniations through JNK-dependent immune modulation. Brain imaging studies document real neuroplastic changes in the prefrontal cortex and default mode network post-manipulation. And then there's the proprioceptive work—a solid RCT (n=72) showed upper cervical manipulation actually improves head repositioning accuracy and cervical kinesthesia, suggesting normalized afferent feedback rather than placebo. The integrated self-care trial (APPROACH, n=3,306) showed combined practitioner and self-directed therapies beat either alone for pain, fatigue, and mental health outcomes. Even your pediatric scoliosis students should know: respiratory guidance plus chiropractic adjustment hit a 96.7% effective rate versus 80.8% for conventional care alone.

The wildcard finding across multiple studies is *how much verbal framing matters*. One RCT found that the words you use—not patient expectations, not attitude toward therapy—predicted short-term pain and pressure pain threshold outcomes. Translation: your explanation of what you're doing may matter more than what you're measuring psychometrically. That's simultaneously empowering and sobering. You can't outsource this to a machine or a protocol.

Here's your concrete takeaway for this week: if you're still using subluxation language with patients or building your entire clinical narrative around "fixing misalignments," you're out of step with both the evidence and your profession's future regulatory environment. The data supports something far more sophisticated: targeted manual therapy that modulates proprioception, reduces inflammation, shifts pain processing, and works best when embedded in a coherent clinical story and complementary self-care. That's not less chiropractically interesting—it's more scientifically defensible. Start auditing your own patient conversations this week: are you explaining *mechanisms* or *philosophy*?

papers.title: MOTIVATIONS, TRAINING OUTCOMES, AND CLINICAL PRACTICE CHARACTERISTICS OF NORTH AMERICAN CHIROPRACTORS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL SURVEY
papers.one_line: North American chiropractors are purpose-driven practitioners with strong clinical reasoning and counseling skills.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors report high satisfaction with training in clinical reasoning, communication, and lifestyle counseling—core competencies that align with autonomous, patient-centered practice. Practice behaviors (manipulation frequency, imaging use) correlate with philosophical orientation (vitalistic vs. biomechanical vs. non-subluxation), suggesting targeted evidence-based practice guidelines may benefit specific subgroups. Consider leveraging purpose-driven recruitment and meaning-centered curricula to attract and retain practitioners committed to rigorous, evidence-based care.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors are predominantly motivated by prosocial and meaning-centered factors; report strong outcomes in clinical reasoning, communication, and counseling; and demonstrate practice behaviors strongly associated with philosophical orientation regarding subluxation.

papers.title: Profession-Related Accreditation Requirements in Australia Regarding Anatomy Teaching: A Web-Based Desktop Audit
papers.one_line: Most Australian health professions lack specific anatomy accreditation standards despite anatomy's foundational importance.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that chiropractic was among professions with explicit anatomy accreditation requirements in Australia, supporting the profession's emphasis on anatomical knowledge. This finding underscores the importance of maintaining robust anatomy curricula in chiropractic education, as regulatory guidance for anatomy content remains limited across most health disciplines. Consider advocating for continued emphasis on anatomy standards within chiropractic accreditation frameworks.
papers.key_finding: Only 6 of 20 Australian health professions had specific accreditation requirements relating to anatomy curriculum or teaching; four disciplines had no anatomy-related curricula specifications despite anatomy being foundational to practice.
papers.study_design: Web-based desktop audit with content analysis

papers.title: Pediatric vertebral artery dissection and ischemic stroke following chiropractic manipulation
papers.one_line: Cervical chiropractic manipulation in toddlers can cause vertebral artery dissection and stroke.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must exercise extreme caution with cervical manipulation in very young children, as vertebral artery dissection is a documented serious complication. Awareness of non-specific presentations (lethargy, vomiting, respiratory distress) following pediatric cervical manipulation should prompt emergency evaluation. Consider whether cervical manipulation is appropriate in this population or if alternative treatments are safer options.
papers.key_finding: A 20-month-old developed vertebral artery dissection with luminal irregularity in the V4 segment immediately following cervical chiropractic manipulation, presenting with acute lethargy, vomiting, cyanosis, and respiratory distress.

papers.title: Assessing the importance and feasibility of quality measures for chiropractic care: a national survey of U.S. chiropractors.
papers.one_line: National survey identifies chiropractors' views on quality measure importance and implementation feasibility.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This survey provides insight into which quality metrics chiropractors consider most important and feasible to implement in their practices. Understanding the profession's consensus on quality measures may guide the development of evidence-based standards and metrics that are both clinically meaningful and practically achievable.
papers.key_finding: The study assessed U.S. chiropractors' perspectives on the importance and feasibility of various quality measures for chiropractic care, providing data on which metrics the profession prioritizes.

papers.title: Estimating Lumbar Spine Foraminal Disc Measurements Using Ultrasound and X-Ray Imaging Through Advanced Image Annotation, Processing, and Mathematical Modeling During Chiropractic Traction Procedures: A Feasibility Study
papers.one_line: Combined ultrasound and X-ray methodology standardizes lumbar spine measurements during traction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This feasibility study demonstrates a practical approach to quantify real-time changes in intervertebral foramen dimensions during traction therapy using integrated ultrasound and X-ray imaging. Chiropractors could use standardized measurement protocols to objectively document mechanical decompression effects, potentially improving treatment documentation and patient communication about traction efficacy.
papers.key_finding: Progressive traction forces (1.8–11.3 kg) produced consistent increases in lumbar spinal metrics including disc height and foraminal area across L3-L4, L4-L5, and L5-S1 levels, demonstrating measurable elongation and flexibility under load.

papers.title: Cervical spinal manipulative therapy, arterial dissection, and the law: Informed consent and causation in Goldie C.arsenault
papers.one_line: Canadian court finds chiropractor liable for stroke after cervical manipulation despite uncertain causation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case highlights the critical importance of comprehensive informed consent documentation regarding cervical artery dissection risk, even though epidemiological causation remains uncertain. Chiropractors should document pre-existing risk factors, obtain detailed consent, and consider interaction models (latent susceptibility plus manipulation) rather than viewing dissection as purely traumatic or spontaneous.
papers.key_finding: Trial court found the chiropractor liable despite acknowledging causation uncertainty, with courts treating population-level epidemiological evidence as controversial and applying binary causation reasoning (traumatic vs. spontaneous) rather than considering multifactorial models.
papers.study_design: Legal case analysis with clinical evidence review

papers.title: Spinal Manipulative Therapy on a Healthy Population: Protocol for a Randomized Blinding Feasibility Trial
papers.one_line: Novel full-spine sham chiropractic maneuver developed and tested for blinding integrity in RCT.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This feasibility study validates a new sham chiropractic technique to enable proper blinding in future SMT research. Successful blinding methodology will improve the quality of chiropractic clinical trials and help establish the true neurophysiological effects of spinal manipulation. Chiropractors should monitor this research as it advances the evidence base for SMT efficacy.
papers.key_finding: The study is developing and testing a novel full-spine HVLA-emulating sham maneuver to achieve successful participant blinding in SMT research, with blinding success measured via Bang Blinding Index and James Blinding Index as primary outcomes.

papers.title: The 2023 patient profile and clinical management characteristics at a South African chiropractic training clinic: a descriptive cross-sectional study
papers.one_line: South African chiropractic training clinic patient demographics and management patterns documented.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This descriptive study provides insights into patient populations seeking chiropractic care in South Africa and management approaches used in a training setting. Understanding local patient profiles and treatment patterns can inform practice development and student training priorities in similar settings.
papers.key_finding: The study characterizes the patient demographics and clinical management characteristics at a South African chiropractic training clinic in 2023, providing descriptive data on practice patterns in this region.

papers.title: Rehabilitation effects of combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment on adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.one_line: Combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment outperforms conventional treatment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Adding respiratory guidance to chiropractic spinal adjustments for adolescent scoliosis patients yields superior outcomes, including higher treatment success rates (96.72% vs 80.85%), greater reductions in Cobb angle, improved trunk symmetry, and enhanced quality of life. Practitioners should consider incorporating breathing exercises into standard scoliosis management protocols to maximize patient benefits and exercise tolerance.
papers.key_finding: The combined respiratory guidance plus chiropractic adjustment group achieved a 96.72% overall effective rate versus 80.85% with conventional treatment alone, with significantly greater improvements in Cobb angle, back muscle strength, trunk rotation, pain scores, and functional outcomes.

papers.title: Nationwide Online Stress Survey of 100,000 People in Japan
papers.one_line: Survey of 100,000 Japanese adults identifies stress prevalence, demographics, and coping strategies including chiropractic massage.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic massage is recognized as a stress-coping strategy, particularly among high-stress men in Japan. Short sleep, long work hours, and low income are modifiable stress risk factors that chiropractors can address through lifestyle counseling. This epidemiological data supports positioning chiropractic care within a stress-management framework for preventive health.
papers.key_finding: High stress affected 14.8% of men and 17.7% of women; chiropractic/massage was cited as a primary coping strategy in the high-stress group, alongside sleep and bathing. Risk factors for high stress included short sleep duration, long working hours, and low household income.

papers.title: Recruiting US veterans with chronic low back pain in a multisite randomized pragmatic trial
papers.one_line: Existing referrals most efficiently recruited VA veterans with chronic low back pain for chiropractic trials.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors working in VA or similar integrated care settings should leverage existing referral pathways as the primary recruitment strategy, as this approach is fastest (23-day median) and reaches diverse populations. Combining postal mail with email communications and offering virtual visits significantly improves recruitment engagement and reduces response time by half.
papers.key_finding: Among 3,667 veterans screened, existing referrals recruited 91% of participants with 23-day median time to randomization, while EHR prescreening identified the highest proportion of female veterans (79%) and existing referrals best reached racial/ethnic minorities (33%). Virtual and email-based outreach reduced recruitment time compared to postal-only methods.

papers.title: Association of Chiropractic Colleges Educational Conference and Research Agenda Conference 2026: Connected Care
papers.one_line: 2026 ACC conference proceedings featuring connected care research and educational abstracts.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This conference proceedings document compiles current chiropractic research and educational initiatives focused on integrated, connected care models. Practitioners should review the platform and poster abstracts to identify emerging evidence and best practices in collaborative healthcare delivery relevant to their practice.
papers.key_finding: The conference brought together chiropractic educators and researchers to present research and educational content centered on connected care approaches, documented through peer-reviewed platform and poster presentations.

papers.title: Chiropractor perspectives on the use of patient reported outcome measures: a survey of Veterans Health Administration chiropractors
papers.one_line: VA chiropractors survey reveals attitudes and barriers toward implementing patient-reported outcome measures.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Understanding chiropractor perspectives on PROMs in VA settings may identify implementation barriers and opportunities for better outcome tracking in clinical practice. This survey data can inform strategies to improve adoption of standardized outcome measurement tools among chiropractic clinicians.
papers.key_finding: The study documents VHA chiropractor perspectives on patient-reported outcome measures, though specific findings are unavailable without the abstract.

papers.title: Adverse events among older adults receiving chiropractic spinal manipulation and related treatments: an updated systematic review.
papers.one_line: Systematic review examining safety profile of chiropractic manipulation in elderly patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This updated systematic review provides evidence on adverse event rates in older adult populations receiving spinal manipulation, critical for informed consent and risk stratification. Chiropractors should use these findings to identify high-risk patients and implement appropriate screening protocols before treatment.
papers.key_finding: The review synthesizes current evidence on adverse events associated with chiropractic spinal manipulation in older adults, enabling practitioners to better understand safety profiles in this vulnerable population.

papers.title: Musculoskeletal Treatments: Physical Modalities.
papers.one_line: Exercise-based therapies show strongest evidence for chronic musculoskeletal pain management.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Combine exercise-based therapies with manual therapy approaches for optimal outcomes in chronic musculoskeletal pain. Multidisciplinary rehabilitation programs are recommended over isolated single treatments. Standardization of treatment dosage and delivery protocols is needed to improve evidence quality.
papers.key_finding: Moderate-certainty evidence supports exercise-based therapies for chronic musculoskeletal pain. Low-to-moderate certainty evidence supports osteopathic manipulative treatment, with spinal manipulative therapy and chiropractic care among additional modalities available but requiring stronger evidence.

papers.title: Women's health and chiropractic: Educational audit and development of core competencies.
papers.one_line: Developed 62 core competencies across 10 domains for women's health chiropractic education.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should familiarize themselves with the 10 domains and 62 competencies to enhance their knowledge of women's health across the lifespan, including reproductive, hormonal, and age-related conditions. These competencies provide a framework for recognizing gender as a social determinant of health and understanding how social conditions affect female patients. Consider using these standards for continuing education and practice improvement.
papers.key_finding: An international expert panel achieved >80% consensus on 62 core competencies within 10 domains for women's health in chiropractic education, addressing the lifespan from puberty through menopause and beyond, including social determinants of health.
papers.study_design: Educational audit with Delphi consensus methodology

papers.title: The assessment of second year chiropractic students' comfort and confidence modifying care for vulnerable patient groups: A cross-sectional survey.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic students show lower confidence than comfort with physically/mentally disabled patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic education should enhance clinical training for managing physically and mentally disabled patients, where students report the lowest confidence levels. Educators should develop targeted curricula addressing gaps between comfort and confidence, particularly for physically vulnerable populations. Consider leveraging students' personal experiences with vulnerability to improve peer education and empathetic care delivery.
papers.key_finding: Students reported higher comfort and confidence with general and socioculturally diverse patients compared to physically/mentally disabled patients. A notable 37% of respondents identified as belonging to vulnerable populations themselves, yet confidence remained lower than comfort across most groups.

papers.title: A Mindbody Approach to Long-standing Fatigue: A Case Report on Emotional Somatic Release Using HeartSpeak Lite for BodyWork
papers.one_line: HeartSpeak Lite bodywork combined with emotional processing improved chronic fatigue symptoms in one patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case suggests integrating emotional somatic release with fascial mobilization may benefit chronic fatigue patients who haven't responded to traditional manual therapy alone. Chiropractors could consider incorporating mind-body and emotional processing elements into care plans for fatigue patients, particularly those with high perceived stress. However, this single case cannot establish efficacy; larger controlled studies are needed before widespread clinical adoption.
papers.key_finding: A 52-year-old woman with decade-long chronic fatigue syndrome showed meaningful improvements over 10 weeks with HeartSpeak Lite bodywork, with Fatigue Severity Scale scores declining from 6.8 to 4.2 and Perceived Stress Scale scores improving from 29 to 19.

papers.title: Adding Self-Care Complementary and Integrative Health (CIH) Therapies to Care for Chronic Pain-The Assessing Pain, Patient Reported Outcomes and Complementary Health (APPROACH) Study
papers.one_line: Combining practitioner-delivered and self-care CIH therapies yields equal pain relief with enhanced perceived global benefits.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Both practitioner-delivered CIH alone and combined with self-care therapies produce equivalent improvements in pain interference (~40% clinically meaningful improvement). Recommending self-care therapies (yoga, mindfulness, Tai Chi) alongside chiropractic care may enhance patient perception of improvements in fatigue, mental health, and well-being without additional pain relief burden.
papers.key_finding: Pain interference improved similarly in both arms (-0.62 vs -0.70), with 39.5% and 41.1% achieving clinically meaningful improvement respectively. However, patients receiving combined practitioner-delivered and self-care CIH reported higher perceived improvements in pain (11%), fatigue (28%), mental health (24%), and overall well-being (27%).

papers.title: Efficacy of manual therapy by different healthcare professionals on pain and function in temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials
papers.one_line: Manual therapy reduces TMD pain and improves function short-term across professions, but long-term evidence remains limited.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can incorporate manual therapy for TMD management, particularly in short-term pain reduction and mouth opening improvement. Evidence supports chiropractic approaches alongside physiotherapy and osteopathy, though practitioners should manage patient expectations regarding long-term durability and consider collaboration with dental/maxillofacial specialists for comprehensive care.
papers.key_finding: Manual therapy by various healthcare professionals (chiropractors, physiotherapists, osteopaths, dental specialists) was associated with reductions in pain and improvements in maximum mouth opening. However, evidence was predominantly short-term with limited certainty, and physiotherapists in rehabilitation settings showed most consistent outcomes.
papers.study_design: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials

papers.title: Physiological changes of cortisol and oxytocin following manual therapy: a scoping review
papers.one_line: Manual therapy produces variable cortisol and oxytocin responses with mixed findings across studies.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While manual therapy may influence stress hormones (cortisol) and bonding hormones (oxytocin), current evidence is inconsistent and lacks standardization. Chiropractors should recognize neuroendocrine mechanisms as theoretical but not yet clinically validated. Future practice should await more rigorous, standardized research before claiming specific hormonal benefits to patients.
papers.key_finding: Of 72 eligible studies examining cortisol and/or oxytocin responses to manual therapy interventions, findings were heterogeneous across outcome measures, intervention types, sampling methods, and timing protocols, with most studies measuring cortisol and fewer examining oxytocin.

papers.title: Spinal manipulative therapy promotes nucleus pulposus resorption and alleviates pain in a rat model of lumbar disc herniation via JNK-dependent regulation of inflammation and tissue remodeling
papers.one_line: SMT accelerates nucleus pulposus resorption and pain relief through JNK-regulated inflammation and tissue remodeling.
papers.clinical_takeaway: SMT appears superior to epidural corticosteroids for promoting natural disc herniation resolution while maintaining favorable inflammatory balance for tissue repair. The selective modulation of inflammatory markers and growth factors suggests SMT optimizes the body's inherent resorption mechanisms rather than broadly suppressing inflammation. These findings provide mechanistic support for SMT as a first-line intervention in acute lumbar disc herniation cases.
papers.key_finding: SMT achieved near-complete nucleus pulposus resorption by day 28 with earlier pain relief (day 3) compared to epidural betamethasone, through JNK-dependent modulation that maintained balanced inflammation supporting macrophage recruitment, neovascularization, and matrix remodeling while reducing apoptosis.

papers.title: Effects of Spinal Manipulation and Dry Needling on Headache and Migraine: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.one_line: Systematic review evaluates spinal manipulation and dry needling efficacy for headache and migraine treatment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This systematic review of RCTs provides evidence-based guidance on whether spinal manipulation and dry needling reduce headache and migraine symptoms. Chiropractors can use these findings to inform treatment decisions and patient counseling regarding these commonly used interventions. The review helps establish clinical utility of these techniques in headache management protocols.
papers.key_finding: Systematic review synthesizes RCT evidence on spinal manipulation and dry needling for headache and migraine management, providing comparative effectiveness data for these interventions.
papers.study_design: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials

papers.title: One Spinal Manipulation Session Does Not Affect Static, Quasi-Static and Dynamic Balance or Pressure Pain Threshold in Individuals With Chronic Low Back Pain: A Randomized Clinical Controlled Trial
papers.one_line: Single spinal manipulation session produces no measurable changes in balance or pain sensitivity in chronic low back pain patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: A single spinal manipulation treatment does not significantly improve balance metrics (static, quasi-static, or dynamic) or pressure pain thresholds in chronic low back pain patients, based on multiple follow-up assessments through one week post-treatment. Clinicians should consider that balance improvements may require multiple sessions, different treatment approaches, or combination therapies rather than relying on isolated manipulation sessions for functional balance restoration.
papers.key_finding: Single spinal manipulation produced no statistically significant improvements in modified Sensory Organization Test (SOT), Star Excursion Balance Test (SEBT), or pressure pain threshold measurements when compared to placebo, with no significant differences at immediate, 24-hour, or 1-week follow-up.

papers.title: Neck proprioception and mobility improved after upper neck and spine treatment: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.one_line: Upper cervical manipulation improves neck proprioception and mobility in symptomatic patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The One-to-Zero system, which prioritizes C0-C1 joint manipulation before treating other spinal regions, produces measurable improvements in cervical kinesthesia and neck mobility within 2-6 weeks. Chiropractors may consider addressing upper cervical dysfunction first to normalize proprioceptive feedback and enhance treatment outcomes for neck pain and disability.
papers.key_finding: Treatment group showed significantly greater improvements in head-to-target repositioning accuracy at 50% maximum head rotation, neck range of motion, pain, and disability compared to control, with selective improvements in cervical kinesthesia suggesting normalized proprioceptive feedback.

papers.title: Verbal framing, rather than measured cognitive-affective variables, is associated with short-term outcomes after spinal manipulation: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
papers.one_line: Pre-treatment verbal framing predicts short-term spinal manipulation outcomes better than patient expectations.
papers.clinical_takeaway: How you frame spinal manipulation verbally to patients (positive, neutral, or negative messaging) may have more influence on short-term pain outcomes than their pre-existing expectations or beliefs. Chiropractors should focus on optimizing pre-treatment communication and framing to maximize therapeutic benefit, as this appears more impactful than attempting to modify patient expectations alone.
papers.key_finding: Short-term pain intensity and pressure pain threshold were associated with verbal framing type rather than cognitive-affective variables (expectations, attitude toward manual therapy, or expectation fulfillment). Patient expectations and expectation fulfillment showed sparse and inconsistent associations with outcomes.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial

papers.title: Clinical features of manual therapy interventions in people with tension-type headache: A scoping review.
papers.one_line: Manual therapy for tension-type headache shows high variability in techniques, dosage, and mechanisms across trials.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that evidence for specific manual therapy protocols in tension-type headache is inconsistent due to heterogeneous interventions and outcomes across studies. Focus on cervical and suboccipital structures appears common, but future practice should emphasize mechanism-informed, individualized approaches with standardized outcome measurement.
papers.key_finding: Thirty-three RCTs revealed significant heterogeneity in manual therapy techniques, treatment dosage, target structures, and outcomes for tension-type headache, with most studies lacking clear mechanistic rationale.

papers.title: The Effect of Joint Mobilization and Manipulation on Proprioception: Systematic Review with Limited Meta-Analysis
papers.one_line: Joint mobilization and manipulation may improve proprioception through neurophysiological mechanisms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider mobilization and manipulation as potential tools to enhance proprioceptive function in patients with proprioceptive deficits. The neurophysiological effects on proprioception may contribute to improved movement control and stability. Further high-quality research is needed to establish optimal treatment parameters.
papers.key_finding: Joint mobilization and manipulation appear to influence proprioceptive function, though the magnitude and clinical significance of effects remain unclear due to heterogeneity in study designs and measurement methods.

papers.title: Chiropractic Management of Adults with Cervicogenic or Tension-Type Headaches: Development of a Clinical Practice Guideline
papers.one_line: Evidence-based guideline supports spinal manipulation for cervicogenic headache and multimodal care for tension-type headache.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can confidently use spinal manipulation as a primary intervention for cervicogenic headache based on evidence consensus. For tension-type headache, spinal manipulation should be integrated within multimodal treatment approaches. Practitioners should incorporate proper red flag screening during history and examination to ensure appropriate patient selection and timely referral when needed.
papers.key_finding: Thirty-two articles (31 systematic reviews, 1 guideline) were synthesized to develop consensus recommendations. Spinal manipulation is recommended for cervicogenic headache management, and for tension-type headache only as part of multimodal care; limited evidence supports acupuncture, education, and meditation as standalone interventions.
papers.study_design: Umbrella review with Delphi panel consensus development

papers.title: Effects of segmental spinal manipulation on adolescent scoliosis based on electromyography parameters
papers.one_line: Segmental spinal manipulation reduces Cobb angle and alters EMG motor unit recruitment in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Segmental spinal manipulation shows promise for reducing Cobb angle measurements in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients, with measurable changes in paraspinal muscle recruitment patterns across multiple spinal positions. While improvements in muscle strength were not demonstrated, the three-dimensional spinal adjustment approach appears effective for structural angle reduction, suggesting potential value as part of a multimodal treatment protocol for AIS.
papers.key_finding: Segmental spinal manipulation significantly increased paraspinal muscle motor unit turns (EMG parameter) across multiple positions and effectively reduced Cobb angle compared to control massage, though muscle strength improvements were not observed.

papers.title: Mechano responsiveness of neuroimmune cross-talk in bone and joints: A narrative review with implications for force-based manipulations
papers.one_line: Neuroimmune mechanisms may mediate bone responses to force-based manipulations and physical activity.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation and manual therapy may modulate bone-related neuroimmune responses through sympathetic/parasympathetic signaling and cytokine pathways. Tailor manual therapy and exercise prescriptions based on patient age, hormonal status, and comorbidities to optimize bone health outcomes. Further research is needed to establish direct mechanistic links between specific manipulations and measurable bone changes.
papers.key_finding: While physical activity's effects on bone are well-established, force-based manipulations (spinal manipulation, massage, manual therapy) show early evidence of neuroimmune modulatory effects on bone, though direct bone changes from manipulation remain understudied.

papers.title: Complications of Chiropractic Manipulation in a Patient With Von Willebrand Disease: A Clinical Case Report and Literature Review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic manipulation caused severe iliopsoas hematoma with femoral neuropathy in a Von Willebrand disease patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must screen patients for bleeding disorders (especially Von Willebrand disease) before manipulation, as even routine spinal manipulation can precipitate life-threatening hemorrhagic complications in coagulopathic patients. When coagulopathy is present, alternative or modified therapeutic approaches should be considered. Early recognition of neurological signs (progressive weakness, sensory loss) post-manipulation warrants urgent imaging and multidisciplinary referral.
papers.key_finding: A 32-year-old female with Von Willebrand disease developed an 896 cc iliopsoas hematoma with femoral nerve compression after routine chiropractic spinal manipulation, resulting in persistent neuropathy despite interventional drainage and factor replacement therapy.

papers.title: Brain functional changes following spinal manipulation therapy in patients with lumbar disc herniation and chronic low back pain: a scoping review
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation modulates prefrontal cortex and default mode network, correlating with pain and disability improvements.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation induces measurable neuroplastic changes in pain-processing brain regions (prefrontal cortex, default mode network) that correlate with clinical improvements in pain intensity, function, and mood. Chiropractors can discuss these central nervous system mechanisms with patients to explain how manipulation addresses both symptoms and underlying neural dysfunction. Future standardized protocols are needed to optimize treatment delivery based on these emerging neurobiological mechanisms.
papers.key_finding: Ten studies demonstrated that spinal manipulation induces significant changes in brain activity and connectivity, particularly in the prefrontal cortex, visual network, and default mode network, with these neuroplastic changes correlating with improvements in pain intensity, functional disability, and emotional states.

papers.title: Immediate effects of upper cervical spinal manipulation on cervical sensorimotor control in individuals with chronic primary cervical pain: an exploratory randomized controlled trial
papers.one_line: UCSM may transiently slow head-neck movement in cervical pain patients, suggesting compensatory sensorimotor control.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Upper cervical spinal manipulation at C1-C2 appears to produce immediate kinematic changes favoring movement accuracy over speed in patients with chronic cervical pain. These transient effects may reflect compensatory sensorimotor adjustments, though clinical significance remains unclear pending larger, longer-term studies.
papers.key_finding: UCSM produced a descriptive trend toward transient slowing of head-neck movement and increased movement accuracy on the cervical movement sense test compared to sham, compatible with speed-accuracy trade-off and compensatory sensorimotor control patterns.
papers.study_design: Exploratory randomized controlled trial, single-blind, sham-controlled

papers.title: The effect of Traditional Chinese Medicine Tuina massage combined with family-based prevention on visual acuity in children and adolescents with myopia: A case report of single-group interventional study
papers.one_line: Tuina massage combined with blue-light-blocking glasses significantly improved visual acuity in myopic children.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Tuina massage 3×/week for 12 weeks, combined with blue-light-blocking glasses, demonstrated statistically significant visual acuity improvements in pediatric myopia patients. Non-amblyopic patients showed greater improvement than amblyopic cases. Consider this multimodal approach as adjunctive therapy for myopic children, though lutein supplementation alone showed limited benefit.
papers.key_finding: All participants showed statistically significant visual acuity improvements post-intervention; blue-light-blocking glasses produced the most pronounced gains, while lutein supplementation alone was not statistically significant. Non-amblyopic patients benefited more than amblyopic cases.

papers.title: Spinal manipulative therapy for adults with chronic low back pain
papers.one_line: SMT shows small pain reduction versus placebo but comparable to other conservative treatments.
papers.clinical_takeaway: SMT may provide modest pain relief and functional improvement for chronic LBP, particularly versus sham/placebo and no treatment. However, evidence quality is low-to-very low, and SMT performs similarly to other conservative interventions. Patient selection and realistic outcome expectations are important when incorporating SMT into treatment plans.
papers.key_finding: SMT versus sham showed small pain reduction (MD -7.01 on 100-point scale) and medium functional improvement; versus no treatment showed medium pain and large functional improvement; versus other conservative treatments showed little-to-no pain difference and small functional improvement.

papers.title: Non-Pharmacological and Pharmacological Treatments for Non-Acute Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Protocol for a Multicenter Pragmatic Trial
papers.one_line: RCT protocol comparing acupuncture/spinal manipulation versus pharmacological treatment for lumbar disc herniation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This multicenter pragmatic trial will provide high-quality evidence on the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of manual therapy (spinal manipulation) combined with acupuncture for non-acute lumbar disc herniation. Chiropractors can expect evidence-based data on manipulation efficacy versus standard pharmacological approaches, potentially supporting integration of manual therapy into LDH management protocols.
papers.key_finding: This study protocol outlines the first large-scale, well-designed clinical trial comparing non-pharmacological strategies (acupuncture and spinal manipulation) with pharmacological interventions for non-acute lumbar disc herniation, with primary outcomes measured at 13 weeks and long-term follow-up to 3 years.

papers.title: Response to Letter to the Editor regarding "Can pre-treatment verbal suggestions influence the short-term effects of spinal manipulation in young adults with chronic non-specific low back pain? A randomized controlled trial"
papers.one_line: Authors respond to critiques of their study on verbal suggestion effects during spinal manipulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This is a response letter addressing methodological or interpretive concerns raised about a prior study examining verbal suggestion as an adjunct to spinal manipulation for low back pain. Review the original trial and this response together to evaluate the strength of evidence regarding expectancy and suggestion in manipulation outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Without access to the full text, this appears to be an author response defending or clarifying findings from an RCT on verbal suggestion effects in spinal manipulation for chronic low back pain.

papers.title: Angular Kinematic Analysis of Supine Cervical Thrusts Performed by Chiropractors and Chiropractic Students on Mannequins
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors produce peak cervical rotation of 33.9° during cervical adjustments.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Peak axial rotation during cervical adjustment is approximately 34°, below theoretical spinal ligament failure thresholds. Chiropractors achieve this rotation in 144 milliseconds with rotational velocities around 193°/s. These biomechanical parameters can serve as benchmarks for technique training and safety assessment.
papers.key_finding: Experienced doctors of chiropractic achieved mean peak cervical axial rotation of 33.9° with peak lateral bending of 32.0° and extension of 10.4° during supine cervical thrusts on a mannequin.

papers.title: Kinematic Assessment of Hip, Shoulder, and Elbow Movements of a Chiropractor Performing Side Posture Adjustments: Results From a Biomechanical Analysis.
papers.one_line: Side-posture adjustments use coordinated hip-shoulder-elbow movements with consistent thrust patterns.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Effective side-posture technique relies on asymmetrical hip and shoulder positioning for stabilization, with the right elbow functioning primarily to transfer body-drop force rather than generate thrust independently. Chiropractors can improve technique consistency by focusing on repeatable movement patterns while recognizing that table height and patient size may require individual adjustments.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors demonstrate repeatable thrust patterns across trials with consistent hip-shoulder-elbow kinematics, though angular magnitudes vary; the right elbow extends minimally, indicating force transfer from body drop rather than upper extremity generation.
papers.study_design: Biomechanical analysis using inertial measurement units

papers.title: CT-guided Foramen Ovale Injection of Mesenchymal Stem Cells: First Human Case Report of Trigeminal Neuralgia Relief
papers.one_line: MSC injection via foramen ovale provided significant trigeminal neuralgia pain relief in one patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case suggests MSC injection may be an alternative for trigeminal neuralgia patients failing conservative care, though evidence is limited to one case. Chiropractors should be aware of this emerging intervention and consider referral for patients with refractory TN seeking alternatives to medications with cognitive side effects. Further clinical trials are needed before clinical recommendations can be made.
papers.key_finding: A 48-year-old woman with 22-year history of severe TN showed dramatic pain reduction at 1 month post-MSC injection with resolution of medication side effects; partial symptom recurrence occurred by 12 months but cognitive improvements persisted with reduced medication requirements.

papers.title: The effects of chiropractic adjustment on inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a pilot RCT
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment showed no superiority over sham adjustment for pediatric ADHD symptoms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot RCT found no significant difference between real and sham chiropractic adjustments for ADHD symptoms in children, with both groups improving similarly—likely due to placebo effect or usual care. Chiropractors should not position spinal adjustment as an evidence-based standalone treatment for ADHD in children. Future larger-scale studies are warranted before recommending chiropractic care specifically for ADHD symptom management.
papers.key_finding: Both chiropractic adjustment plus usual care and sham adjustment plus usual care groups showed significant improvements in ADHD symptoms at 4 and 8 weeks, with no statistically significant differences between groups.

papers.title: Myositis Ossificans Traumatica of Bilateral Sternocleidomastoid Muscles After Chiropractor Adjustment: A Case Report
papers.one_line: Myositis ossificans developed in bilateral sternocleidomastoid muscles following chiropractic neck adjustment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While myositis ossificans is rare, chiropractors should be aware of this potential complication after cervical manipulation, particularly in patients with prior neck surgery or trauma. Severe persistent neck/shoulder pain with trismus following adjustment warrants immediate medical evaluation and imaging to rule out heterotopic ossification.
papers.key_finding: A young woman developed myositis ossificans affecting bilateral sternocleidomastoid muscles with heterotopic ossification extending to supraclavicular tissues following chiropractic cervical adjustment, presenting with persistent shoulder pain, trismus, and neck pain.

papers.title: Vertebral Subluxation and Systems Biology: An Integrative Review Exploring the Salutogenic Influence of Chiropractic Care on the Neuroendocrine-Immune System
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment may influence neuroendocrine-immune function through multiple neural pathways.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This review suggests chiropractic care may affect systemic physiology beyond musculoskeletal outcomes, with potential benefits for blood pressure, heart rate variability, and sleep quality. Practitioners can consider these broader health-promoting effects when counseling patients, though specific neural mechanisms require further investigation.
papers.key_finding: Synthesis of two decades of chiropractic research suggests spinal adjustment may modulate neuroendocrine-immune function through multiple neurologically mediated pathways, with documented improvements in blood pressure, heart rate variability, and sleep quality.

papers.title: A Case Report of U-Type Sacral Fracture After Chiropractic Adjustment.
papers.one_line: Drop-table chiropractic manipulation caused severe U-type sacral fracture in elderly patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Drop-table manipulation carries risk of catastrophic spinopelvic dissociation, particularly in older patients. Practitioners should exercise extreme caution with forceful lumbar/sacral techniques in elderly populations. Delayed diagnosis of such injuries can complicate recovery and extend hospitalization.
papers.key_finding: A 74-year-old male sustained a U-type sacral fracture (spinopelvic dissociation) following drop-table chiropractic manipulation, a previously undocumented complication. Despite diagnostic delay, conservative management allowed return to baseline function at one year, though mild residual neuropathy persisted.

papers.title: Absence of Neuroplastic Changes in the Bilateral H-Reflex Amplitude following Spinal Manipulation with Activator IV.
papers.one_line: Activator IV spinal manipulation does not produce measurable neuroplastic changes in H-reflex amplitude.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study suggests that instrument-assisted spinal manipulation using the Activator IV does not induce detectable neurological reflex changes. Clinicians should not expect H-reflex modulation as a mechanism of action with this technique, though other therapeutic effects may still occur.
papers.key_finding: Bilateral H-reflex amplitude showed no significant neuroplastic changes following Activator IV spinal manipulation, suggesting this technique may not alter spinal cord excitability through reflex pathways.

papers.title: Acute Lumbar Schmorl's Node Following Chiropractic Adjustment.
papers.one_line: Acute Schmorl's node developed post-chiropractic adjustment, resolved with conservative care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic adjustment can precipitate acute Schmorl's node formation, though this remains rare. Conservative management including rest and symptom-guided activity modification proved effective, with this patient achieving 85% pain relief. Clinicians should counsel patients on possible vertebral endplate involvement and monitor outcomes closely.
papers.key_finding: A 41-year-old male developed an acute Schmorl's node at L4-L5 immediately following chiropractic manipulation and was successfully managed conservatively with 85% pain improvement.

papers.title: Management of people with low back pain: a survey of opinions and beliefs of Dutch and Belgian chiropractors.
papers.one_line: Dutch and Belgian chiropractors show 64.5% guideline adherence for LBP management with improvement needed for acute cases.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors frequently use spinal adjustment (90%) but should increase exercise prescription (currently 33-50%) and strengthen return-to-work counseling (59% adherence). Focus on acute LBP cases reveals lower guideline compliance than chronic cases, suggesting a need for targeted education on evidence-based acute LBP management principles.
papers.key_finding: Overall guideline adherence was 64.5%, with better adherence for chronic LBP (73.4%) than acute LBP (55.9%). Chiropractors excelled at advising against bedrest (98.5%) but fell short on return-to-work advice (59.4%) and activity promotion (77.5%).

papers.title: Chiropractic Spinal Manipulation Prevents Secondary Hyperalgesia Induced by Topical Capsaicin in Healthy Individuals
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation prevents secondary hyperalgesia development in capsaicin-induced pain models.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study suggests spinal manipulation may modulate central pain processing mechanisms and prevent sensitization. Practitioners could consider manipulation as a preventive approach for patients at risk of central sensitization or chronic pain development.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic spinal manipulation prevented the development of secondary hyperalgesia (expanded pain sensitivity) that typically occurs after topical capsaicin application in healthy subjects, suggesting manipulation influences central nociceptive processing.

papers.title: The prevalence of complementary and alternative medicine use among Turkish patients with primary headache
papers.one_line: One-third of Turkish headache patients use CAM, primarily phytotherapy, cupping, and chiropractic adjustment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that 17.5% of Turkish headache patients already use chiropractic adjustment for primary headaches, and CAM use is strongly associated with longer disease duration. This suggests chiropractors may encounter headache patients with chronic disease who have prior CAM experience, presenting opportunities for integrated care discussions.
papers.key_finding: CAM use was reported in 33.3% of primary headache patients, with chiropractic adjustment used by 17.5%. CAM users had significantly longer disease duration (10.97 vs 5.68 years), and disease duration was the only independent predictor of CAM use.

papers.title: Resolution of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Following Correction for Upper Cross Syndrome-A Case Study and Brief Review
papers.one_line: Upper cross syndrome correction via chiropractic care resolved concurrent GERD symptoms in one patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider upper cross syndrome as a potential contributing factor in GERD patients presenting with postural dysfunction and neck/thoracic pain. Corrective chiropractic care addressing cervical alignment and posture may offer a non-pharmacological avenue for managing GERD symptoms in appropriately selected patients. Screen for and address postural abnormalities to potentially prevent secondary conditions.
papers.key_finding: A 35-year-old female with upper cross syndrome and GERD experienced complete resolution of both pain and reflux symptoms following cervical adjustment and soft tissue therapy, with sustained improvement at 12-month follow-up.

papers.title: Chiropractic Day: A Historical Review of a Day Worth Celebrating
papers.one_line: Historical overview of Chiropractic Day celebrating Palmer's first adjustment on September 18, 1895.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic Day (September 18) offers practitioners an opportunity to engage with their communities through education, service, and reflection on the profession's evolution. This commemorative date can be leveraged for patient education initiatives and community outreach activities that reinforce chiropractic values and professional identity.
papers.key_finding: Daniel David Palmer's first chiropractic adjustment on September 18, 1895, established the founding date of the chiropractic profession, which has been celebrated under various names for over 125 years as a way to honor the profession's heritage and continued patient care mission.

papers.title: The effect of sacroiliac chiropractic adjustments on innominate angles.
papers.one_line: Sacroiliac chiropractic adjustments produce measurable changes in innominate bone angles.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments can objectively improve innominate bone alignment toward normal anatomical position. Using the PALM PALpation Meter provides quantifiable measurement of pelvic realignment following adjustment, supporting objective patient documentation. This finding supports incorporating sacroiliac-specific adjustments into treatment protocols for pelvic dysfunction.
papers.key_finding: Specific chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments resulted in measurable changes in innominate bone angles compared to sham ultrasound treatment, with pelvis tilt improving toward correct anatomical alignment.

papers.title: Changes in radiographic parameters following chiropractic treatment in 10 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A retrospective chart review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment reduced Cobb angles by 21.2% in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis cases.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This small retrospective study suggests chiropractic care may produce measurable radiographic improvements in mild-to-moderate adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, with 64% showing curve improvement and 36% showing stabilization. However, the lack of control group, small sample size (n=10), and retrospective design limit clinical applicability; larger RCTs are needed before making treatment recommendations based on these findings.
papers.key_finding: Cobb angle averaged 21.2% reduction (from 29.7° to 23.4°) following chiropractic treatment; 64% showed morphological improvement and 36% showed stabilization, with better outcomes in mild-to-moderate curves.

papers.title: Characterization of Horse Use in Therapeutic Horseback Riding Programs in the United States: A Pilot Survey
papers.one_line: Therapeutic riding horses receive moderate workloads with chiropractic care as common complementary therapy.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic adjustment is among the most frequently used complementary therapies in therapeutic horseback riding programs, suggesting strong acceptance and perceived benefit. Limb lameness and back soreness are the primary health concerns in these horses, creating opportunities for chiropractors to establish protocols and standards of care for equine therapeutic programs.
papers.key_finding: Therapeutic riding horses work approximately 2 hours/day and 4 days/week—well below maximum recommendations—with chiropractic adjustment being among the most common complementary therapies employed, alongside NSAIDs and massage, to manage lameness and back soreness.

papers.title: Measurement and Analysis of Biomechanical Outcomes of Chiropractic Adjustment Performance in Chiropractic Education and Practice.
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors deliver McTimoney thrusts faster with greater consistency than students.
papers.clinical_takeaway: McTimoney toggle-torque-recoil technique proficiency is characterized by reduced thrust duration (117.77 ms vs 283.84 ms for students) and improved consistency. Chiropractors should use these biomechanical markers—particularly time to peak force and thrust duration—as performance feedback during technique refinement and student training.
papers.key_finding: Experienced chiropractors demonstrated significantly shorter time to peak force (3× faster), thrust duration (2.5× faster), and total thrust time compared to year-3 students, with year-5 students showing intermediate performance. Dominant hand delivery produced higher peak forces and faster execution across all groups.

papers.title: Traumatic spinal injuries: A retrospective epidemiological analysis following the 2018 driving policy reform in Saudi Arabia.
papers.one_line: Traumatic spinal injuries show male predominance with lumbar involvement; longer hospitalization linked to psychiatric history and infections.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Most traumatic spinal injury patients present neurologically intact (93.7%), with lumbar region as the most common site. Female patients and those with psychiatric illness, higher injury severity, or pulmonary complications require extended monitoring and longer hospital stays. Chiropractors should screen for mental health comorbidities and coordinate care for complex cases involving spinal trauma.
papers.key_finding: Motor vehicle accidents were the predominant cause (57.6%), lumbar region most commonly injured (53.9%), and 93.7% of patients remained neurologically intact. Female sex, prior psychiatric illness, higher AIS severity, and pulmonary infection independently prolonged hospitalization.

papers.title: Management of Cervical lateral mass fractures - A systematic review.
papers.one_line: Floating lateral mass fractures require surgical intervention; non-operative treatment risks subluxation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Floating lateral mass fractures (FLM) of the cervical spine are unstable injuries that typically require surgical management. Chiropractors should recognize FLM as a contraindication to manipulation and refer for surgical evaluation, as non-operative treatment with cervical collars shows 31% subluxation rates. These injuries commonly result from motor vehicle accidents and frequently involve neurologic or vascular complications.
papers.key_finding: Of 332 patients with FLM, anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) was the most common surgical treatment (51.4% of cases), while non-operative treatment with cervical collars resulted in vertebral subluxation in 31% of patients.

papers.title: Animal Chiropractic: A Basic Description and Its Importance in Veterinary Practice
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic improves function and outcomes in veterinary patients when delivered by trained professionals.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Animal chiropractic can enhance patient strength, stability, and mobility by modulating afferent input and motor neuron function. Veterinarians should consider incorporating AC into treatment plans to improve conditioning, performance, and postoperative recovery outcomes. Only licensed professionals with extensive postgraduate training should deliver these services.
papers.key_finding: Properly applied animal chiropractic is safe and effective, improving afferent input and motor neuron function to enhance patient strength, stability, and mobility, which positively impacts conditioning, performance, and postoperative recovery.

papers.title: Sublaminar stabilization (stapling) of the caudal cervical instability in Yorkshire terrier-A case report
papers.one_line: Sublaminar stapling stabilization successfully treated C6-C7 instability in a small-breed dog.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this case involves veterinary medicine, it demonstrates that sublaminar stabilization techniques can be effective for persistent cervical instability when conservative care fails. Chiropractors should recognize that some cervical instability cases may require surgical referral, particularly when neurological deficits (tetraparesis, proprioceptive loss) persist despite 20+ months of conservative treatment.
papers.key_finding: A Yorkshire terrier with C6-C7 instability and tetraparesis achieved sustained clinical improvement (5-year follow-up) with sublaminar stabilization surgery after conservative management failed for 20 months, though subtle ataxia persisted.

papers.title: Atlas Subluxation Complex, National Upper Cervical Chiropractic Association Intervention, and Dizziness Improvement: A Narrative Review of Historical Perspectives, Literature Synthesis, and a Path for Future Care.
papers.one_line: Atlas subluxation may contribute to dizziness; NUCCA treatment shows promise but lacks robust evidence.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider atlas subluxation as a potential etiological factor in patients presenting with dizziness, particularly those with concurrent upper cervical dysfunction. NUCCA techniques may offer a treatment option for select dizziness cases, but current evidence is limited to case reports and theory. Clinicians should pursue high-quality RCTs to establish efficacy and appropriate patient selection criteria.
papers.key_finding: Case reports and conceptual evidence suggest atlas subluxation complex may contribute to dizziness and that NUCCA chiropractic intervention may improve outcomes, but high-quality controlled studies are lacking and needed to establish clinical efficacy.

papers.title: Catastrophic failure of anterior fusion for bilateral cervical facet dislocation: illustrative case
papers.one_line: Anterior-only fusion inadequate for bilateral cervical facet dislocation; combined anterior-posterior fixation recommended.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize bilateral cervical facet dislocation as a surgical emergency requiring imaging confirmation and immediate specialist referral. Awareness of fusion failure risk factors (age, extensive ligamentous damage, endplate/facet fractures) helps identify high-risk cases requiring more complex surgical approaches than anterior fixation alone.
papers.key_finding: Anterior-only fusion failed in bilateral cervical facet dislocation with subsequent spinal cord injury. Risk factors for construct failure include advanced age, bilateral facet involvement, posterior ligamentous complex damage, and fractures to endplates, facets, or pedicles.

papers.title: The Dark Side of Musculoskeletal Care: Why Do Ineffective Techniques Seem to Work? A Comprehensive Review of Complementary and Alternative Therapies.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic and osteopathy lack robust evidence; observed effects may be primarily placebo-mediated.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This critical review challenges foundational chiropractic concepts like vertebral subluxation, citing insufficient empirical support. Chiropractors should prioritize high-quality outcome research, clearly communicate realistic expectations to patients, and consider how contextual and psychological factors contribute to perceived benefits alongside specific treatment effects.
papers.key_finding: Osteopathy and chiropractic treatments lack robust biological plausibility for core concepts; observed clinical improvements appear substantially mediated by placebo effects rather than specific mechanisms, and supporting studies frequently exhibit serious methodological limitations.

papers.title: Vertebral Column Subluxation in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Associated Dystrophic Scoliosis: A Report of Two Cases and Narrative Review
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation in NF1 dystrophic scoliosis requires surgical intervention; halo-gravity traction carries significant risks.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis with subluxation is a surgical emergency requiring immediate specialist referral. Conservative care, including bracing and traction, is typically ineffective and potentially dangerous in these cases. Early identification of rapid progression or subluxation warrants urgent imaging and multidisciplinary surgical consultation.
papers.key_finding: Two patients with NF1-associated vertebral subluxation (T4-5 and C7-T1) required surgical correction via partial vertebral column resection and instrumentation; halo-gravity traction failed in one case and caused vascular injury in another.
papers.study_design: Case report with narrative literature review

papers.title: The best preferable sagittal vertical axis for the ankylosis spondylitis with thoracolumbar kyphosis following one-level pedicle subtraction osteotomy under different cervical range of motion
papers.one_line: Optimal sagittal vertical axis targets vary by cervical mobility in ankylosing spondylitis kyphosis correction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study suggests that surgical correction goals for ankylosing spondylitis-related kyphosis should be individualized based on cervical spine range of motion. Chiropractors should recognize that post-operative spinal alignment depends on cervical compensation patterns and may inform referral timing or post-operative management strategies.
papers.key_finding: Pedicle subtraction osteotomy outcomes for thoracolumbar kyphosis in ankylosing spondylitis require adjustment of sagittal vertical axis targets according to individual cervical spine mobility to optimize alignment and function.

papers.title: Secondary Analysis of a Dataset to Estimate the Prevalence of Vertebral Subluxation and Its Implications for Health Promotion and Prevention
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation prevalence of 78.55% found in 1,851 chiropractic patients across seven clinics.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study found high prevalence of vertebral subluxation (78.55%) in chiropractic patients, supporting the clinical relevance of VS assessment in practice. The finding that patients seek care for general health and wellness, not just pain, suggests chiropractic may serve a preventive role. However, the nonrandom sample limits generalizability; results should be interpreted as describing the chiropractic population seeking care rather than the general population.
papers.key_finding: Overall vertebral subluxation prevalence was 78.55% (95% CI = 76.68–80.42) in chiropractic patients, with all age and gender-stratified prevalences ≥50%. Patients presented for various reasons including pain, headaches, and general health concerns.

papers.title: Associations between demographics and clinical ideology, beliefs, and practice patterns: a secondary analysis of a survey of randomly sampled United States chiropractors
papers.one_line: US chiropractor ideology and practice patterns vary significantly by education program, experience, and geography.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that their peers practice heterogeneously based on training and location, which may affect professional credibility and interprofessional collaboration. Understanding these variations—including differences in vaccination attitudes, subluxation beliefs, and cancer treatment claims—can help practitioners align with evidence-based standards and strengthen the profession's integration into mainstream healthcare.
papers.key_finding: Significant associations exist between chiropractor demographics (graduation program, years in practice, geographic region) and their clinical ideology, beliefs about subluxation detection, vaccination attitudes, and practice patterns. Wide variation in these beliefs across the profession may create public confusion and hinder interprofessional integration.

papers.title: Spinal decompression and stabilisation in a cat with lumbar vertebral pathological fracture and subluxation, following discospondylitis and spinal epidural empyema.
papers.one_line: Surgical decompression and PMMA stabilization successfully treated feline discospondylitis with epidural empyema.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this is a veterinary case, the surgical principles of decompression combined with stabilization using PMMA and arthrodesis wires demonstrate effective management of spinal infection with pathological fracture. Chiropractors should recognize severe infectious spinal pathology requires surgical intervention and is beyond manual therapy scope.
papers.key_finding: A cat with progressive paraparesis from discospondylitis, epidural empyema, and L1 pathological fracture with subluxation achieved optimal outcome following hemilaminectomy, decompression, and PMMA-based spinal stabilization despite rapid neurological deterioration.

papers.title: Veterinary Spinal Manipulative Therapy or Animal Chiropractic in Veterinary Rehabilitation
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic is a receptor-based modality with diagnostic and therapeutic applications in veterinary rehabilitation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Understanding the neuroanatomical and biomechanical mechanisms of animal chiropractic helps veterinary practitioners recognize when SMT is indicated versus when additional diagnostics are needed. Clinicians should be familiar with indications, contraindications, and limitations of this modality within a multimodal rehabilitation approach.
papers.key_finding: Animal chiropractic functions as a receptor-based health-care modality that can serve both diagnostic and therapeutic purposes in veterinary rehabilitation, though proper training in neuro-anatomical and biomechanical principles is essential to determine appropriate patient selection and avoid unnecessary treatment.

papers.title: A novel Hinge-Link correction system for vertebral column resection: a pilot study in a porcine model
papers.one_line: Novel Hinge-Link device safely corrects severe scoliosis via vertebral column resection in animal model.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study demonstrates a new surgical device for severe scoliosis correction with 94% deformity correction and no neurological complications in the animal model tested. While this is preclinical research, chiropractors should remain informed about surgical advances in severe scoliosis management for appropriate patient referral decisions. Further clinical trials will determine if this device improves outcomes in human patients with severe spinal deformities.
papers.key_finding: The Hinge-Link system corrected surgically-induced scoliosis by 94% (from 32° to 1.8°) with no neurological deficits or spinal cord damage observed in any of the five pigs studied.
papers.study_design: Pilot animal study (experimental surgical device testing)

papers.title: Remodeling morphology of the subluxated osteotomy vertebra in closing-opening wedge osteotomy in ankylosing spondylitis: would the anterior bony beak blunt?
papers.one_line: Closing-opening wedge osteotomy shows favorable bony remodeling in ankylosing spondylitis despite vertebral subluxation complications.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors managing AS patients should recognize that while COWO demonstrates favorable bone remodeling and anterior beak blunting, vertebral subluxation complications significantly limit spinal canal remodeling and correction maintenance. Careful monitoring of sagittal alignment parameters (SVA, global kyphosis) is essential in post-operative AS patients, particularly those developing subluxation.
papers.key_finding: After single-level lumbar COWO in AS patients, adaptive new bone formation and resorption of the anterior bony beak occurred favorably; however, patients with vertebral subluxation (≥5mm sagittal translation) showed significantly limited spinal canal remodeling and greater loss of sagittal correction.

papers.title: Use of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging to assess a case of spinal injury in a Showa koi Cyprinus carpio.
papers.one_line: CT and MRI detected severe spinal cord compression from vertebral pathology in ornamental fish.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates advanced imaging utility for non-mammalian spinal assessment, though direct chiropractic application is limited. The findings of vertebral subluxation causing myelomalacia highlight imaging's role in diagnosing spinal cord compromise. Chiropractors may reference this methodology when considering imaging protocols for various species presentations.
papers.key_finding: MRI revealed extensive vertebral centra alterations and multifocal spinal cord compression associated with vertebral subluxation and severe myelomalacia in a symptomatic ornamental fish.

papers.title: Posterior 3-Column Osteotomy for Treatment of Congenital Kyphosis with Multiple Thoracolumbar/Lumbar Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae: A Comparison Between Patients with Increasing Number of Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae
papers.one_line: Single-level osteotomy effective for congenital kyphosis with 3 unsegmented vertebrae but less effective with ≥4.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that congenital kyphosis with multiple anterior unsegmented vertebrae (≥4) requires surgical intervention and typically achieve suboptimal correction with higher complication rates. Patients with 3 or fewer unsegmented vertebrae may have better surgical outcomes. Referral timing and surgical consultation should account for vertebral anatomy complexity.
papers.key_finding: Single-level posterior 3-column osteotomy achieved satisfactory kyphosis correction (75% correction rate) in patients with 3 anterior unsegmented vertebrae but significantly lower correction rates (61.2%) and higher complication rates (67% vs 8%) in those with ≥4 unsegmented vertebrae.

papers.title: Evaluation of United States chiropractic professional subgroups: a survey of randomly sampled chiropractors.
papers.one_line: Three distinct chiropractic subgroups identified: spine-focused, primary care, and subluxation-focused.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The US chiropractic profession comprises three clearly defined subgroups with different practice philosophies and clinical approaches. Understanding these subgroups (56.8% spine/neuromusculoskeletal, 22% primary care, 21.2% subluxation-focused) can help practitioners clarify their professional identity and better position themselves within healthcare systems. This segmentation may influence professional collaboration, referral patterns, and how chiropractors communicate their scope to other healthcare providers.
papers.key_finding: A nationally representative survey identified three distinct chiropractic professional subgroups defined by their perceived role in healthcare, with substantially different patterns of clinical practice beliefs and behaviors across groups.

papers.title: The association between chiropractors' view of practice and patient encounter-level characteristics in Ontario, Canada: a cross-sectional study
papers.one_line: Chiropractors with unorthodox views treat more non-musculoskeletal conditions and diagnose subluxation more frequently.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that philosophical orientation significantly influences patient caseload and diagnostic patterns. Those with unorthodox subluxation-based views treat broader health conditions in shorter encounters, which may affect referral patterns and interprofessional relationships. Understanding these practice differences can improve communication with other healthcare providers and clarify scope of practice.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors holding unorthodox views (subluxation-based) had 16.5 times higher odds of non-musculoskeletal patient encounters and 63 times higher odds of using subluxation diagnosis, while conducting encounters 40% shorter than orthodox practitioners.

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest: 6 Months ending April 05, 2026
papers.one_line: Digest of 76 papers on pediatric VAD risk, informed consent liability, student competency gaps, and integrative pain management.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must implement rigorous pre-treatment screening for pediatric patients and ensure comprehensive informed consent documentation disclosing arterial dissection risks to mitigate legal liability. Education programs should prioritize training in care modification for physically and mentally disabled patients, where current student confidence is inadequate.
papers.key_finding: A pediatric VAD case and Canadian court liability ruling demonstrate clinical and legal risks of cervical manipulation; simultaneously, chiropractic students show significant confidence gaps in managing disabled populations, and integrative self-care therapies show promise for chronic pain management.
papers.study_design: Mixed methods: case report, legal analysis, cross-sectional survey, and intervention study

papers.title: MOTIVATIONS, TRAINING OUTCOMES, AND CLINICAL PRACTICE CHARACTERISTICS OF NORTH AMERICAN CHIROPRACTORS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL SURVEY
papers.one_line: North American chiropractors report prosocial motivations, strong clinical reasoning and communication skills, with practice patterns aligned to subluxation beliefs.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors are primarily motivated by helping patients and finding meaning in practice rather than status or money. Focus on clinical reasoning, patient communication, and lifestyle counseling—areas where training outcomes are strongest—while implementing evidence-based imaging stewardship. Aligning recruitment and education with these purpose-driven motivations may improve both practitioner satisfaction and patient outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors reported prosocial, meaning-oriented motivations; strongest training outcomes in clinical reasoning, communication, and counseling; and practice patterns (manipulation frequency, x-ray use) correlated with subluxation-based practice orientation rather than biomedical alignment.

papers.title: Profession-Related Accreditation Requirements in Australia Regarding Anatomy Teaching: A Web-Based Desktop Audit
papers.one_line: Most Australian health profession accreditation standards lack specific anatomy curriculum requirements.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should advocate for explicit anatomy competency standards in accreditation frameworks, as only 6 of 20 health disciplines have specific anatomy requirements. Current vague accreditation language may allow inadequate anatomy training despite its critical importance for safe manipulative practice. Chiropractic programs should proactively establish and document rigorous functional anatomy standards independent of accreditation minimums.
papers.key_finding: Only 6 of 20 Australian health professions had specific accreditation requirements for anatomy curriculum content, with chiropractic notably lacking explicit standards despite anatomy being foundational to practice.
papers.study_design: Web-based desktop audit with content analysis

papers.title: Pediatric vertebral artery dissection and ischemic stroke following chiropractic manipulation.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic cervical manipulation associated with vertebral artery dissection in toddler.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should exercise extreme caution with cervical manipulation in pediatric patients, as VAD risk exists even in very young children with non-specific presentations (lethargy, vomiting, respiratory distress). Thorough pre-treatment screening and awareness of dissection symptoms are essential; consider referral for imaging if suspicious signs emerge post-treatment.
papers.key_finding: A 20-month-old presented with acute lethargy, vomiting, cyanosis, and respiratory distress following cervical chiropractic manipulation; imaging confirmed right vertebral artery dissection in the V4 segment.
